36:37.title: Stripping the Day from the Night as Physical Layers (Naslakhu Minhu al-Nahāra)
36:37.summary: [Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36/37) describes night and day as physical coverings by stating that God "strips" (*naslakhu*) the day away from the night, plunging observers into sudden darkness (*muẓlimūn*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/36:37/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/36:37/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 1954](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1954)) interpret this literally as daylight being peeled off in its entirety so night advances from the east as a distinct body. Scientifically, daylight is not a substance stripped from the sky, nor does night fall globally; rather, a rotating spherical Earth turns through continuous solar illumination. This imagery reflects ancient Mesopotamian (*Enūma Eliš*), Rabbinic ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)), and pre-Islamic Arabian conceptions of light and darkness as independent cosmic layers peeled across a stationary world.
36:37.explanation:
Geocentricism. In [Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36/37), the alternation of day and night is depicted as the physical peeling away of daylight from a dark sky over a stationary world, reflecting pre-modern Near Eastern conceptions of light and darkness as independent cosmic substances rather than the axial rotation of a spherical Earth.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36/37) states: *"A sign for them is the night: We strip the day from it (naslakhu minhu al-nahāra), and suddenly they are in darkness (fa-idhā hum muẓlimūn)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), the verb *naslakhu* (`نَسْلَخُ`, from the root *s-l-kh*) specifically denotes flaying, skinning, or peeling the hide off a slaughtered animal (*salkh al-ihāb*). Applied to the cosmos alongside [Quran 7:54](https://quran.com/7/54) (*"He covers the night over the day, seeking it rapidly"*) and [Quran 91:3–4](https://quran.com/91/3-4), the verse treats "the night" (*al-layl*) and "the day" (*al-nahār*) as tangible, global layers that are peeled off and wrapped over the world in succession.

From the standpoint of astronomy and planetary physics, this model conflicts with empirical reality in three fundamental ways:
- **Daylight Is Not a Detachable Substance:** Daylight is merely the scattering of solar photons (Rayleigh scattering) through Earth's thin nitrogen-oxygen atmosphere (`~100 km` thick) on whichever hemisphere faces the Sun; beyond the atmosphere, outer space is perpetually dark.
- **Simultaneous Hemispheric Illumination on a Rotating Sphere:** Because the Earth is an oblate spheroid rotating eastward on its axis at `~1,670 km/h` at the equator, day is never "stripped" from the world in its entirety. Exactly half of the globe is illuminated by daytime at every instant while the opposite hemisphere experiences night.
- **No Independent Cosmic Entities of "Day" and "Night":** Night does not exist as a physical body that approaches or replaces day; darkness is simply the geometric shadow cone (*umbra*) cast by the Earth's own mass blocking direct sunlight.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Islamic commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions confirm that [Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36/37) was understood as the complete physical removal of day and the arrival of night across the sky:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36:37/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī defines the phrase *naslakhu minhu al-nahāra* as: *"We remove the day from it (`nanziʿu ʿanhu al-nahāra`)... so We bring the darkness and take away the day (`fa-naʾtī bi-l-ẓulmati wa-nadhhaba bi-l-nahār`)."* Crucially, when recording Qatādah's attempt to equate this verse with the seasonal merging (*īlāj*) of hours in [Quran 22:61](https://quran.com/22/61), al-Ṭabarī explicitly rejects Qatādah's view as untenable: *"And 'stripping' (`al-salkh`) has nothing to do with that, because the day is stripped from the night in its entirety (`li-anna al-nahāra yuslakhu mina al-layli kullihi`), and likewise the night from the day in its entirety, and not all of the night is made to enter into all of the day."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36:37/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr fully endorses al-Ṭabarī's refutation of Qatādah (*"What Ibn Jarīr said is true"*) and explains the verse's literal meaning: *"He has caused them to follow one another, so that one comes and the other goes (`yajīʾu hādhā fa-yadhhaba hādhā`), and so on... meaning, 'We take it away from it (`naṣrimuhu minhu`), so it goes away and the night comes.'"*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Directional Arrival of Night:** To illustrate how day departs and night arrives in [Quran 36:37](https://quran.com/36/37), Ibn Kathīr quotes the canonical Prophetic narration of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 1954](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1954) (and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1100](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1100)), in which Muhammad gestures toward the eastern and western horizons and states: *"When the night approaches from here (`idhā aqbala al-laylu min hāhunā`), and the day departs from here (`wa-adbara al-nahāru min hāhunā`), and the sun has set, then the fasting person should break his fast."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The conception of Day and Night as substantive cosmic layers or garments peeled off and drawn across a stationary earth was a widespread motif in pre-Islamic Near Eastern, Rabbinic, and Arabian literature:

- **Mesopotamian & Zoroastrian Substantialist Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* & *Bundahishn*):** In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V.12–14) and Middle Persian Zoroastrian texts (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a, 5a), day and night are treated not as optical lighting conditions on a rotating sphere, but as tangible cosmic layers drawn through eastern and western sky-doors over a flat, stationary earth, with darkness existing as a primordial substance covering the world whenever the layer of daylight is withdrawn.
- **Talmudic Veil-of-Darkness Cosmology ([Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Pesachim* 2a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.2a)):** In tractate [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), the Talmud describes the lowest heaven (*Vilon*) as a physical cosmic curtain that rolls back in the morning so daylight appears and spreads out a veil of darkness over the world each evening (*"it enters in the morning and goes out in the evening, and renews the work of creation every day"*).
- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Pastoral & Tent Imagery (*Salkh al-Ihāb*):** In pre-Islamic *Jāhilī* Bedouin poetry (such as the *Muʿallaqah* of **Imruʾ al-Qays**, who depicts the night lowering its curtains across the desert), the sky was envisioned as a dark tent-canopy from which the bright skin of day is flayed (*salakha*, peeling the hide off a slaughtered animal) at sunset, leaving the underlying nocturnal darkness exposed.

36:38.title: The Sun Running to a Nocturnal Resting Place Beneath the Throne (Li-Mustaqarrin Lahā)
36:38.summary: In [Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36/38), the Sun is described as coursing toward an appointed resting station (*tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/36:38/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/36:38/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) record Muhammad's direct explanation that this *mustaqarr* is located beneath Allah's domed Throne, where the Sun prostrates every evening after sunset and requests permission to rise again. Scientifically, sunset is an optical horizon effect of a rotating spherical Earth, and the Sun never travels beneath the Earth to bow at night. This motif reflects ancient Near Eastern solar-journey myths—including Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš*, *Epic of Gilgamesh*), Egyptian (*Amduat*), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), and Talmudic ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) geocentric traditions.
36:38.explanation:
Geocentricism. [Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36/38) depicts the Sun as physically traveling across the sky toward an appointed nocturnal resting place (*mustaqarr*), an account that canonical Prophetic traditions and classical commentators locate beneath the Divine Throne in a flat, domed, geocentric cosmos.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36/38) declares: *"And the sun: it runs to a dwelling place (appointed) for it (wa-l-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā). That is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing."* In classical Arabic, *mustaqarr* (`مُسْتَقَرّ`, from *istaqarra*, "to settle or come to rest") denotes a fixed resting station or terminal point, while *tajrī* (`تَجْرِي`) denotes active running from one place to another.

This description contradicts established heliocentric astronomy and astrophysics:
- **Earth's Rotation Causes Sunset, Not Solar Transit:** Sunrise and sunset are caused by the Earth rotating eastward on its axis every `23 hours, 56 minutes` while orbiting the Sun at `~107,000 km/h`. Relative to the Solar System's barycenter, the Sun is the central gravitational body containing `99.86%` of the system's mass.
- **Continuous Illumination Over a Spherical Earth:** The Sun never stops or settles at sunset; when it sets in Arabia, it is simultaneously shining at noon over the Atlantic and rising over the Americas.
- **Impossibility of Reversing the Sun's Course:** The canonical explanation of [Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36/38) states that the Sun is detained at night beneath the Throne and will eventually be ordered to turn back and rise from the west, assuming the Sun—rather than the spinning Earth—traverses the sky each day.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Canonical *ḥadīth* collections and foundational *tafsīr* works record Muhammad's direct exegesis of [Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36/38) as describing the Sun's nightly journey beneath the Throne:

- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* of Abū Dharr al-Ghifārī:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) (with parallels in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4802](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4802), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4803](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4803), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 7424](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7424), and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a)), Abū Dharr narrates: *"The Prophet asked me at sunset, 'Do you know where the sun goes (at the time of sunset)?' I replied, 'Allah and His Apostle know better.' He said, 'It goes (travels) till it prostrates itself underneath the Throne (`taḥta al-ʿarsh`), and takes the permission to rise again, and it is permitted; and then (a time will come when) it will be about to prostrate itself, but its prostration will not be accepted, and it will ask permission to go on its course, and it will not be permitted, but it will be ordered to return whence it has come and so it will rise in the west.' And that is the interpretation of the Statement of Allah: {And the sun runs its fixed course for a term decreed (wa-l-shamsu tajrī li-mustaqarrin lahā)}."* In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4803](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4803) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159d](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159d), Muhammad states directly: *"Its resting place is beneath the Throne (`mustaqarruhā taḥta al-ʿarsh`)."*
- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36:38/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī defines the clause: *"And the sun runs to its place of rest (`li-mawḍiʿi qarārihā`); and regarding this, a narration has come from the Messenger of Allah."* He quotes Abū Dharr's *ḥadīth* (*"so it rises from its place, and that is its dwelling place"*), alongside views from Qatādah (an appointed time limit) and others (that the Sun advances each night to the furthest of its western setting points before returning).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 36:38](https://quran.com/36:38/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Explaining the spatial resting place (*mustaqarruhā al-makānī*), Ibn Kathīr explicitly rejects the spherical cosmos of astronomers in favor of a flat-earth dome beneath the Throne: *"The first view is that it refers to its fixed course of location, which is beneath the Throne, beyond the earth in that direction. Wherever it goes, it is beneath the Throne, it and all of creation, because the Throne is the roof of creation (`saqfuhā`) and it is not a sphere as many astronomers claim (`wa-laysa bi-kuratin kamā yazʿumuhu kathīrun min arbābi al-hayʾah`). Rather it is a dome supported by legs or pillars (`qubbatun dhātu qawāʾima`), carried by the angels, and it is above the universe, above the heads of people. When the sun is at its zenith at noon, it is in its closest position to the Throne, and when it runs in its fourth orbit at the opposite point to its zenith, at midnight, it is in its furthest position from the Throne. At that point it prostrates and asks for permission to rise."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The motif of the Sun running across a domed sky to a western setting station, bowing in homage during its nocturnal transit, and returning to the east was widely attested across pre-Islamic Near Eastern and Rabbinic cosmologies:

- **Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Zoroastrian Nocturnal Solar-Journey Traditions (*Enūma Eliš*, *Gilgamesh*, *Amduat*, & *Bundahishn*):** In the Babylonian *Epic of Gilgamesh* (Tablet IX) and *Enūma Eliš* (Tablet V), the Sun-god *Šamaš* runs across the solid sky-vault by day, enters the western mountain gate of *Mashu* at sunset, and traverses the interior of heaven at night before emerging in the east at dawn. In Ancient Egyptian religion (*Amduat*), the solar barque descends into the western horizon to pass through the twelve night hours of the subterranean *Duat* amid prostration and divine acclaim before rising in the east. Likewise, Middle Persian Zoroastrian texts (*Khorshed Niyayesh* & *Greater Bundahishn* 5a) portray the Sun coursing across a stone sky above a flat earth to its stations while offering homage to Ohrmazd.
- **Talmudic Geocentric Night-Circuit Debates ([Babylonian Talmud, *Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) & [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b)):** In [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b), sages and ancient astronomers debate the Sun's nocturnal path after it exits the western sky-doors—whether it returns to the east above the solid firmament or beneath the flat earth (*"during the day the sun travels beneath the firmament, and at night it travels beneath the earth"*), directly paralleling the canonical *ḥadīth* and Ibn Kathīr's explanation of the Sun's nightly *mustaqarr* beneath the domed Throne.

36:40.title: The Sun Cannot Overtake the Moon & Night Never Outruns Day (Quran 36:40)
36:40.summary: According to [Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40), the Sun is barred from overtaking the Moon (*an tudrika al-qamar*) and the Night cannot outstrip the Day, while all four revolve in a celestial wheel (*fī falakin yasbaḥūn*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/36:40/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/36:40/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) explain that the Sun, Moon, Night, and Day all circle a stationary Earth in the dome of heaven, with each luminary restricted to its own daytime or nighttime jurisdiction (*sulṭān*). In reality, the Moon is visible in the daytime sky for half of every month, solar eclipses align both bodies during the day, and polar regions experience months of uninterrupted night or sunlight. This mirrors Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V), Greco-Roman (Ptolemy's *Almagest*), and Talmudic ([*Chullin* 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b)) geocentric traditions.
36:40.explanation:
Geocentricism. [Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40) groups the Sun, the Moon, the Night, and the Day as four revolving entities that chase one another in a celestial sphere (*falak*) around a stationary Earth, asserting strict diurnal boundaries that conflict with orbital mechanics, solar eclipses, and polar geography.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40) states: *"It is not fitting for the sun to overtake the moon (lā al-shamsu yanbaghī lahā an tudrika al-qamar), nor does the night outrun the day (wa-lā al-laylu sābiqu al-nahār), but each floats in (its own) orbit (wa-kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn)."*

Evaluated against astronomy and planetary physics, this verse contains three scientific errors:
- **Geocentric Grouping of Night, Day, Sun, and Moon in an "Orbit" (*Falak*):** The verse uses the plural *kullun* ("each/all") with the masculine plural verb *yasbaḥūn* (`يَسْبَحُونَ`, for three or more subjects, not the dual *yasbaḥān*) to include Night, Day, Sun, and Moon ([Quran 36:37–40](https://quran.com/36/37-40)), treating optical lighting conditions on a rotating Earth as orbiting bodies.
- **Separate Day/Night "Jurisdictions" vs. Daytime Lunar Visibility and Eclipses:** The claim that the Sun cannot "overtake" (*tudrika*) the Moon reflects the ancient belief that the Sun rules exclusively by day and the Moon exclusively by night. In reality, the Moon orbits the Earth (`~27.3` sidereal days) while the Earth orbits the Sun (`~365.25` days); thus, the Moon is visible in the daytime sky for roughly half of every month, and during a solar eclipse, both occupy the exact same ecliptic coordinates in the daytime sky.
- **Unawareness of Polar Day and Polar Night:** The assertion that *"nor does the night outrun the day"*—explained by classical exegetes as meaning another night cannot follow night without an intervening day—holds only at low and middle latitudes. Above the Arctic and Antarctic Circles (`>66.56°` latitude), Earth's `23.44°` axial tilt produces up to six months of uninterrupted polar night in winter and six months of midnight sun in summer.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical *tafsīr* authorities unanimously interpreted [Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40) as describing four geocentric phenomena revolving around a fixed Earth:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36:40/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains *lā al-shamsu yanbaghī lahā an tudrika al-qamar*: *"It is not suitable for the sun to overtake the moon such that its light eliminates his light, resulting in all times being day with no night in them. {'Nor does the night outrun the day'} means: and the night does not outrun the day such that its darkness eliminates its light, resulting in all times being night."* He quotes **al-Ḍaḥḥāk** (*"when the sun rises, there is no light for the moon, and when the moon rises with its light, there is no light for the sun"*), **Qatādah** (*"When the authority [`sulṭān`] of this comes, the authority of this departs"*), and **Mujāhid** (*"They seek one another rapidly, one of them slipping away from the other"*). Regarding *wa-kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn*, al-Ṭabarī states: *"And all that We have mentioned of the sun, the moon, the night, and the day, they run in an orbit (`fī falakin yajrūn`),"* quoting **Ibn ʿAbbās** that this *falak* is *"like the whorl of a spinning wheel (`ka-falaki al-mighzal`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36:40/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr quotes **ʿIkrimah**: *"This means that each of them has its authority (`sulṭān`), so it is not appropriate for the sun to rise at night."* Explaining *wa-lā al-laylu sābiqu al-nahār*, Ibn Kathīr writes: *"After night has passed, it is not fitting for another night to come until it has been day. The authority of the sun is during the day and the authority of the moon is at night."* He likewise confirms the fourfold subject of *wa-kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn*: *"means, night and day, the sun and the moon, all of them are floating, i.e., revolving, in their orbits in the heaven (`yadūrūna fī falaki al-samāʾ`). This was the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, and ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī."*
- **Pre-Scientific Lunar Casing Tradition & Canonical *Ḥadīth*:** Under [Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40), Ibn Kathīr also records via Ibn Abī Ḥātim from **ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak**: *"Indeed, the wind has a wing, and the moon takes shelter in a casing of water (`wa-inna al-qamara yaʾwī ilā ghilāfin mina al-māʾ`)."* This geocentric model is further anchored by the canonical *ḥadīth* of Abū Dharr ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199); [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a)) on the Sun's nightly journey beneath the Throne.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Every element of [Quran 36:40](https://quran.com/36/40)—separate solar/lunar "authorities" (*sulṭān*), the Moon's watery casing, and the revolving heaven—derives from pre-Islamic Near Eastern and Mediterranean cosmology:

- **Babylonian & Talmudic Separate "Jurisdictions" of Sun and Moon (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V & [Babylonian Talmud, *Chullin* 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b)):** In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V.12–22), Marduk appoints the Moon (*Nanna/Sîn*) to govern the night and defines its boundaries relative to the Sun (*Šamaš*) so each luminary keeps to its domain. Similarly, in [*Chullin* 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b), Rabbi Shimon ben Pazzi relates an aggadic tradition in which the Moon complains that *"two kings cannot use one crown,"* leading to its light being diminished so the Sun holds daytime jurisdiction and the Moon nighttime jurisdiction—matching *sulṭān al-shams bi-l-nahār wa-sulṭān al-qamar bi-l-layl* in Qatādah, ʿIkrimah, and Ibn Kathīr.
- **Greco-Roman & Talmudic Revolving Spheres and Aqueous Lunar Lore (Aristotle, Ptolemy, Pliny, & [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** In Greco-Roman astronomy (**Aristotle**, *De Caelo* II.7–8; **Ptolemy**, *Almagest*) and Talmudic cosmology ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)), the Sun and Moon revolve along circular tracks or spindle-whorl spheres (*sphairai* / *aflāk*) around a stationary Earth. Likewise, Greco-Roman natural philosophy (**Pliny**, *Natural History* II.102; **Plutarch**, *De Facie*) classified the Sun as fiery and the Moon as a moist body enveloped in watery vapors—paralleling Ibn al-Mubārak's report in Ibn Kathīr that the Moon shelters in a *"casing of water"* (`ghilāfin mina al-māʾ`).

91:1.title: The Sun and Daytime Treated as a Unified Geocentric Phenomenon (Wa-l-Shamsi Wa-Ḍuḥāhā)
91:1.summary: [Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1) opens a four-part cosmic oath—"By the sun and her morning light (*wa-ḍuḥāhā*)!"—followed immediately by the Moon trailing her ([Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2)), the Day unveiling her ([Quran 91:3](https://quran.com/91/3)), and the Night covering her ([Quran 91:4](https://quran.com/91/4)). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/91:1/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/91:1/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 705](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:705), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) explain that *ḍuḥāhā* denotes the Sun's entire daytime, before Night covers the Sun and darkens the horizons. Scientifically, the Sun shines continuously in space without morning or night, and daytime is a local effect of Earth's rotation. This mirrors Mesopotamian (*Enūma Eliš*), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), pre-Islamic Arabian, and Talmudic ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) geocentric cosmology.
91:1.explanation:
Geocentricism. In [Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1), the opening oath *"By the sun and her morning light (wa-l-shamsi wa-ḍuḥāhā)"* initiates a four-verse cosmological sequence ([Quran 91:1–4](https://quran.com/91/1-4)) that treats daytime as the Sun's universal state before it is trailed by the Moon, unveiled by the Day, and covered over by the Night across a flat, earth-centered world.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1) declares: *"By the sun and her morning light! (wa-l-shamsi wa-ḍuḥāhā)"*—which is bound via the feminine pronoun *-hā* ("her," referring to the feminine noun *al-shams*, "the Sun") to the three following oaths:
- [Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2): *"By the moon when he follows her (wa-l-qamari idhā talāhā)!"*
- [Quran 91:3](https://quran.com/91/3): *"By the day when it reveals her (wa-l-nahāri idhā jallāhā)!"*
- [Quran 91:4](https://quran.com/91/4): *"By the night when it covers her (wa-l-layli idhā yaghshāhā)!"*

In classical Arabic lexicography, *ḍuḥā* (`ضُحَى`) denotes the spreading brightness and warmth of the forenoon or the entirety of daytime (*al-nahār kulluhu*). When read within its immediate syntactic sequence ([Quran 91:1–4](https://quran.com/91/1-4)), this cosmology conflicts with modern astrophysics on three levels:
- **The Sun Has No Intrinsic "Morning" or "Daytime":** As a main-sequence G-type star (`G2V`) fusing hydrogen into helium in hydrostatic equilibrium, the Sun emits radiant energy isotropically (`~3.828 × 10²⁶ W`) at all times. It experiences neither morning (*ḍuḥā*) nor night; "morning light" and "daytime" are strictly local perspectives of an observer on a rotating planet turning into the Sun's line of sight.
- **Day Does Not "Reveal" the Sun, Nor Does Night "Cover" It:** In [Quran 91:1–4](https://quran.com/91/1-4), Day (*al-nahār*) and Night (*al-layl*) are treated as independent cosmic agents that successively unveil (*jallāhā*) and veil (*yaghshāhā*) the Sun. Physically, solar radiation itself creates daytime on Earth's sunlit hemisphere, and night is merely the shadow of the spherical Earth turning away from the Sun.
- **Geocentric Pairing with a Flat Spread Earth:** Just two verses later ([Quran 91:5–6](https://quran.com/91/5-6)), the same oath series swears *"By the sky and what built it! By the earth and what spread it (wa-l-arḍi wa-mā ṭaḥāhā)!"*—framing the Sun's daily *ḍuḥā* as an overhead transit across a built ceiling above a spread-out terrestrial plane.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators confirm that *wa-ḍuḥāhā* in [Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1) equates the Sun's brightness directly with global daytime before the Night envelops the Sun at sunset:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91:1/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī cites **Mujāhid** defining *wa-ḍuḥāhā* as *"its light (`ḍawʾuhā`)"* and **Qatādah** defining it as *"the day—and he used to say: 'Al-Ḍuḥā is the whole day (`al-nahāru kulluhu`).'"* Al-Ṭabarī then formulates the definitive classical synthesis: *"The correct view concerning that is to say: He, majestic is His praise, swore by the sun and its daytime (`bi-l-shamsi wa-nahārihā`); because the clear light of the sun is daytime (`li-anna ḍawʾa al-shamsi al-ẓāhira huwa al-nahār`)."* On the paired verse [Quran 91:4](https://quran.com/91:4/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), al-Ṭabarī explains what ends this daytime: *"By the night when it covers the sun, until it disappears and the horizons become dark (`ḥattā taghība fa-tuẓlima al-āfāq`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91:1/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr quotes the same narrations from **Mujāhid** (*"by its light"*) and **Qatādah** (*"the whole day"*), and endorses al-Ṭabarī's conclusion verbatim: *"Ibn Jarīr said, 'The correct view is that it should be said: Allah swears by the sun and its daytime, because the clear light of the sun is daytime.'"* On [Quran 91:3–4](https://quran.com/91:3/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), Ibn Kathīr likewise confirms that the feminine pronoun *-hā* refers to the Sun being unveiled by day and covered by night when the Sun disappears below the horizon.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In his commentary on [Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1), Ibn Kathīr opens with the canonical tradition of Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 705](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:705), where Muhammad instructs Muʿādh ibn Jabal to lead evening prayers with *Wa-l-shamsi wa-ḍuḥāhā* ([Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1)) and *Wa-l-layli idhā yaghshā* ([Quran 92:1](https://quran.com/92/1)). Furthermore, the Sun's daily geocentric cycle between its morning rise and evening disappearance is detailed in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199), where the Sun travels beneath the Divine Throne after sunset before receiving permission to rise again.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Describing the Sun as emerging each morning to spread universal daytime across a flat earth before being veiled by night was a standard feature of ancient Near Eastern, Rabbinic, and pre-Islamic Arabian cosmology:

- **Mesopotamian & Zoroastrian Solar Hymns (*Šamaš Hymn*, *Enūma Eliš*, & *Khorshed Niyayesh*):** In the Babylonian *Great Hymn to Šamaš* and *Enūma Eliš* (Tablet V), the Sun-god opens the eastern gates of the solid sky-vault each morning to pour universal daylight across the flat earth until entering the western gate at evening. Similarly, in the Zoroastrian *Khorshed Niyayesh* and *Greater Bundahishn* (5a), when the Sun rises over Mount Hara Berezaiti, light spreads across the entire earth until night draws its veil over the sky.
- **Talmudic Morning-Gate & Veil-of-Night Cosmology ([Babylonian Talmud, *Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b), the Sun emerges through eastern windows in the solid firmament each morning to illuminate the world by day, while [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) depicts the lowest heaven (*Vilon*) rolling back by day to reveal the Sun's light and spreading out a veil of darkness at evening so night covers the world—matching [Quran 91:1–4](https://quran.com/91/1-4).
- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Solar Oaths & Tent Cosmology:** In pre-Islamic *Jāhilī* poetry and Arabian soothsayer (*kāhin*) oaths, swearing by the rising Sun, forenoon brightness (*al-ḍuḥā*), the following Moon, and enveloping Night above a spread-out desert floor ([Quran 91:5–6](https://quran.com/91/5-6)) was a stock formula rooted in Bedouin cosmology.

91:2.title: The Moon Physically Trailing the Sun Across the Sky (Wa-l-Qamari Idhā Talāhā)
91:2.summary: [Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2) swears an oath by the Moon as it trails behind the Sun (*wa-l-qamari idhā talāhā*), portraying the Moon as a companion luminary walking along the same heavenly course after sunset. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/91:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/91:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) explain that during the first half of the lunar month the Sun walks in front while the Moon follows behind her, whereas in the second half the Moon precedes her. In celestial mechanics, the Moon orbits the Earth at ~384,400 km while the Earth orbits the Sun at ~149.6 million km; neither luminary chases the other. This echoes Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), pre-Islamic Arabian *manāzil*, and Talmudic ([*Rosh Hashanah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.25a)) geocentric traditions.
91:2.explanation:
Geocentricism. [Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2) depicts the Moon as physically following (*talāhā*) the Sun across the celestial vault to succeed daytime, reflecting the ancient observational illusion of twin luminaries marching in sequence around a stationary Earth.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2) declares: *"By the moon when he follows her! (wa-l-qamari idhā talāhā)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), the verb *talā* (`تَلَا`, imperfect *yatlū*) specifically means "to follow at the heels of, walk immediately behind, or succeed someone without interval," while the feminine object pronoun *-hā* ("her") refers directly to the Sun (*al-shams*) in [Quran 91:1](https://quran.com/91/1).

From the perspective of modern orbital mechanics and heliocentric astronomy, describing the Moon as following the Sun across the sky misrepresents the physical structure of the Solar System:
- **Completely Distinct Orbital Centers and Scales:** The Moon does not travel along the Sun's path or follow behind the Sun. The Moon is a rocky natural satellite (`diameter ~3,474 km`) orbiting the Earth in an elliptical trajectory at a mean distance of `~384,400 km`, whereas the Sun is a central star (`diameter ~1.39 million km`) located `~149.6 million km` (`1 AU`) away—nearly `390 times` more distant than the Moon.
- **Eastward Lunar Orbit vs. Apparent Westward Daily Transit:** Relative to the background stars, the Moon actually moves *eastward* around the Earth by `~13.2°` per day (`~0.55°` per hour). The visual impression that the Moon follows the Sun westward toward the horizon after sunset during the waxing phase is purely an optical effect caused by the Earth's rapid eastward axial rotation (`15°` per hour).
- **Lunar Phases Are Geometric Angles, Not a Two-Half Chase:** In the waxing crescent phase, the Moon appears near the western horizon after sunset not because it is "walking behind" a departing Sun, but because its orbital position lies at a small angular elongation (`~10°–90°` east) from the Earth–Sun line.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Islamic exegetes unanimously interpreted [Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91/2) according to the visual geocentric appearance of the Moon trailing the Sun across the sky during the lunar month:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī opens his commentary by defining the verse literally: *"He, exalted is His mention, says: And the moon when it follows the sun (`wa-l-qamari idhā tabiʿa al-shamsa`), and that is in the first half of the month, when the sun sets, the moon follows it, rising (`idhā ghuribat al-shamsu talāhā al-qamaru ṭāliʿan`)."* He then cites chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās** (*"It follows the day [`yatlū al-nahār`]"*), **Mujāhid** (*"The sun, when the moon follows it [`tabiʿahā`]"*), **Qatādah** (*"It follows it on the night of the crescent moon, so when the sun goes down, the crescent moon is seen"*), and **Ibn Zayd**, who spells out the geocentric spatial mechanics: *"The moon follows the sun in the first half of the month, and she follows him in the other half. As for the first half, he follows her, and she is in front of him and he is behind her (`wa-takūnu amāmahu wa-huwa warāʾahā`). But when it is the other half, he is in front of her, preceding her (`amāmahā yaqdumuhā`), and she follows him."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 91:2](https://quran.com/91:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr records the exact same four classical explanations from **Mujāhid** (*"It follows it [the sun]"*), **Ibn ʿAbbās** (*"It follows the day"*), **Qatādah** (*"referring to the night of the Hilāl [new crescent moon]. When the sun goes down, the Hilāl is visible"*), and **Ibn Zayd** (*"It follows it in the first half of the month, then it [the sun] follows it. And it [the moon] precedes it in the latter half of the month"*).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Context:** This exegetical model rests on the same geocentric framework articulated in the canonical *ḥadīth* of Abū Dharr ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199); [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a)), where the Sun and Moon are understood as luminaries traversing appointed courses across the sky over a stationary Earth.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that the Moon physically follows behind the Sun during the first half of the lunar month and precedes it in the second half was a well-documented astronomical tradition in the pre-Islamic Near East:

- **Babylonian & Zoroastrian Two-Half Lunar Pursuit Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V & *Greater Bundahishn*):** In the Babylonian creation epic *Enūma Eliš* (Tablet V.12–22), Marduk fixes the monthly stations of the Moon (*Nanna/Sîn*) relative to the Sun (*Šamaš*): during the first half of the month (days 1 to 14–15), the waxing crescent rises and sets after the Sun, trailing behind it across the sky until standing opposite at full moon, and in the second half of the month, the waning Moon precedes the Sun toward the horizon. The Middle Persian Zoroastrian *Greater Bundahishn* (5b) and *Māh Niyayesh* describe the exact same fifteen-day waxing pursuit and fifteen-day waning reversal across the heavenly vault—the precise two-half geocentric pursuit model reproduced by **Ibn Zayd** in the classical commentaries of al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr.
- **Talmudic & Pre-Islamic Arabian Lunar-Horizon Lore ([Babylonian Talmud, *Rosh Hashanah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.25a) & [*Chullin* 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b)):** In [*Rosh Hashanah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.25a), Rabban Gamliel examines new-moon witnesses using visual diagrams of lunar phases by asking whether the crescent moon was seen *"in front of the sun or behind the sun"* along its sky-path, while [*Chullin* 60b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.60b) portrays the Moon as the nighttime successor trailing the Sun's daytime rule. In pre-Islamic Arabian *manāzil al-qamar* (lunar mansion) lore, Bedouin sky-watchers likewise tracked the Moon as a traveler walking behind the Sun during the first fortnight (*al-layālī al-bīḍ*) and ahead of her in the second.

21:33.title: Night, Day, Sun, and Moon Swimming in a Revolving Celestial Whorl (Kullun Fī Falakin Yasbaḥūn)
21:33.summary: In [Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21/33), God is described as creating the night, the day, the sun, and the moon so that all of them glide in a circular wheel (*kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn*), right after stating that the Earth is stabilized by mountains ([Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31)) beneath a roofed sky ([Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32)). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/21:33/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/21:33/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) define *falak* as a revolving spindle-whorl or hand-mill axis in which the Sun, Moon, Night, and Day circle a stationary Earth. In astrophysics, Earth rotates and orbits the Sun, while night and day are not orbiting bodies. This reflects Mesopotamian, Greco-Roman, and Talmudic ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) geocentric models.
21:33.explanation:
Geocentricism. Situated immediately after verses depicting the Earth as anchored by mountain pegs ([Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31)) beneath a solid roofed sky ([Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32)), [Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21/33) states that the night, the day, the sun, and the moon all glide in a revolving celestial whorl (*falak*), reflecting ancient geocentric cosmology rather than modern heliocentric or galactic mechanics.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21/33) declares: *"He (it is) who created the night and the day, and the sun and the moon, each floating in (its own) orbit (kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn)."* In classical Arabic lexicons (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *falak* (`فَلَك`, cognate with Akkadian *pilakku* and Syriac *pelakkā*, "spindle whorl") denotes the circular whorl of a hand-spindle (*falakat al-mighzal*) and the revolving vault of heaven (*falak al-samāʾ*), while *yasbaḥūn* (`يَسْبَحُونَ`) denotes gliding across a medium.

Both the literal geocentric reading and modern concordist reinterpretations of [Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21/33) conflict with astronomy:
- **Total Omission of Earth's Rotation and Orbit:** Throughout [Quran 21:31–33](https://quran.com/21/31-33), the Earth is stationary and stabilized by mountains *"so that it does not sway with them"* ([Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31)), while the sky is a *"guarded roof"* (`saqfan maḥfūẓan`, [Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32)) across which the Sun and Moon glide to produce day and night. In reality, day and night are caused by Earth's 24-hour axial rotation (`~1,670 km/h`), and Earth orbits the Sun (`~107,000 km/h`), whereas the Moon orbits the Earth.
- **Plural Verb *Yasbaḥūn* Grouping Night, Day, Sun, and Moon:** Arabic grammar uses the dual (*yasbaḥān*) for two subjects and the masculine plural (*yasbaḥūn*) for three or more. By using *kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn* directly after naming the Night, the Day, the Sun, and the Moon, the verse treats night and day as physical entities revolving alongside the Sun and Moon.
- **Failure of Galactic Orbit and Axial Rotation Harmonizations:** Modern concordist claims that *falak* predicts the Sun's `~230-million-year` Milky Way galactic orbit or its axial rotation fail philologically and astronomically: a 230-million-year galactic revolution has no connection to the daily alternation of *al-layl wa-l-nahār*; the Earth orbits the galactic center at the exact same velocity alongside the Sun; and *yasbaḥūn* cannot mean axial rotation because the Moon is tidally locked to Earth and displays no independent visible rotation.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Islamic scholars unanimously understood *falak* and *yasbaḥūn* in [Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21/33) as the daily geocentric revolution of the celestial vault and its luminaries around a motionless Earth:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21:33/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī records the early exegetical definitions of *falak*: (1) **Mujāhid** and **Ibn Jurayj** defined it as *"an orbit like the shape of the iron axis of a hand-mill (`ka-hayʾati ḥadīdati al-raḥā`)"*; (2) **Ibn ʿAbbās** and **Qatādah** defined it as *"the orbit of the heaven (`falak al-samāʾ`)"*; (3) **Ibn Zayd** defined it as *"that which is between the heaven and the earth from the courses of the stars, the sun, and the moon"*; (4) **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** stated: *"The orbit (`al-falak`) is a mill like the shape of the whorl of a spindle (`ṭāḥūnah ka-hayʾati falakati al-mighzal`)"*; and (5) others defined it as *"a contained wave (`mawj makfūf`) in which the sun, the moon, and the stars run,"* or the celestial pole (*al-quṭb*). Regarding *yasbaḥūn*, al-Ṭabarī cites **Mujāhid** and **Ibn Zayd** that it simply means *"they run (`yajrūn`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 21:33](https://quran.com/21:33/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains *kullun fī falakin yasbaḥūn* as *"revolving (`yadūrūn`),"* quoting **Ibn ʿAbbās**: *"They revolve like a spindle in a whorl (`kamā yadūru al-mighzalu fī al-falakah`)."* He then quotes **Mujāhid**: *"The spindle does not turn except with the whorl, nor does the whorl turn except with the spindle. Likewise, the stars, the sun, and the moon do not revolve except with it (the orbit), nor does it revolve except with them."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Sun's Daily Geocentric Circuit:** The nature of this daily solar circuit is confirmed in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) (and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a)), where Muhammad explains that at sunset the Sun travels to prostrate beneath the Divine Throne and asks permission each night to rise again from the east.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the spindle-whorl terminology (*falak*) and luminaries "swimming" (*yasbaḥūn*) across upper cosmic waters come from pre-Islamic Near Eastern and Mediterranean cosmology:

- **Mesopotamian & Greco-Roman Spindle-Whorl Spheres (*MUL.APIN*, Plato, Aristotle, & Ptolemy):** In Babylonian astronomy (*MUL.APIN*, c. 1000 BC), the sun and moon move along circular sky-paths likened to a spindle whorl (*pilakku*, the direct Semitic cognate of *falak*). Similarly, **Plato** (*Republic* X, 616c–617b, the "Spindle of Necessity") modeled the geocentric heavens as nested whorls of a spinning spindle, while **Aristotle** (*De Caelo* II.7–8) and **Claudius Ptolemy** (*Almagest* / *Planetary Hypotheses*, 2nd century AD) placed a stationary Earth at the center of revolving spherical shells (*sphairai*, rendered in Syriac as *pelakkē* and Arabic as *aflāk*).
- **Egyptian, Babylonian, & Talmudic "Upper Waters" and Celestial Navigation (*Enūma Eliš*, Egyptian *Amduat*, & [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** In Ancient Egyptian solar cosmology (*Book of the Dead* Spell 15; *Amduat*) and Babylonian creation myth (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV.135–146), the sky is a solid roof or canopy (*Nut*) holding back the upper cosmic waters (*Nun* / Tiamat's upper waters) above a flat, mountain-anchored earth. Because the upper heavens were thought to consist of contained celestial waters—preserved directly by al-Ṭabarī as *mawj makfūf* ("a contained wave") and echoed in the Talmudic upper-waters discussions of [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) and [*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b)—the Sun and Moon were naturally described as "swimming" or "gliding" (*yasbaḥūn*) across the sky-vault, just as [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) depicts the sun and constellations revolving around a fixed Earth.

31:29.title: Seasonal Day-Length Merging & the Sun and Moon Running Like a Waterwheel (Quran 31:29)
31:29.summary: In [Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29), God merges night into day and day into night (*yūliju al-layla fī al-nahār*) while subjecting the Sun and Moon so that both run their courses for an appointed term (*kullun yajrī ilā ajalin musamman*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/31:29/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/31:29/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) explain that this refers to seasonal changes in day length and the Sun and Moon revolving like a waterwheel (*sāqiyah*) above the Earth by day and beneath the Earth at night. Scientifically, seasonal day-length variation is caused by Earth's 23.44° axial tilt during its heliocentric orbit around the Sun. This echoes Babylonian (*MUL.APIN*), Greco-Roman (Vitruvius, Cleomedes), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), and Talmudic ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) geocentric models.
31:29.explanation:
Geocentricism. In [Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29), the seasonal lengthening and shortening of day and night are paired with the subjection of the Sun and Moon running their courses over a stationary, mountain-anchored Earth ([Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10)), a process classical exegetes explain as the Sun and Moon turning like a waterwheel above and beneath the Earth.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29) declares: *"Do you not see that God causes the night to pass into the day, and causes the day to pass into the night (yūliju al-layla fī al-nahāri wa-yūliju al-nahāra fī al-layli), and has subjected the sun and the moon, each one running (its course) for an appointed time (wa-sakhkhara al-shamsa wa-l-qamara kullun yajrī ilā ajalin musamman)?"* After [Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10) describes mountains cast onto the Earth *"so that it does not sway with you,"* [Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29) attributes both the daily cycle and seasonal daylight variations (*īlāj*, merging hours of night and day) to the geocentric running (*yajrī*) of the Sun and Moon around a fixed Earth.

From the standpoint of celestial mechanics, this framework reverses the physical motions of the Earth–Sun–Moon system:
- **Earth's `23.44°` Axial Obliquity and Heliocentric Orbit Cause the Seasons:** Seasonal lengthening of summer days and winter nights (*īlāj*) is not caused by the Sun shifting its track over a stationary Earth, but by Earth's `23.44°` axial tilt during its `365.25-day` orbit around the Sun.
- **Simultaneous Opposite Seasons Across Hemispheres:** The verse describes God inserting night into day (lengthening summer days) and then inserting day into night (lengthening winter nights) as a single global process. On a spherical tilted Earth, whenever daylight hours are lengthening in the Northern Hemisphere (December to June), they are simultaneously shortening by the exact same amount in the Southern Hemisphere.
- **Asymmetry of the Sun and Moon:** Pairing the Sun and Moon as twin subjected bodies (*wa-sakhkhara al-shamsa wa-l-qamara kullun yajrī*) treats the central star of the Solar System and Earth's small rocky satellite as equivalent sky-travelers circling the Earth.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and authenticated early traditions on [Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29) explicitly confirm both the seasonal hour-transfer reading of *yūliju* and the literal subterranean night circuit of the Sun and Moon around a stationary Earth:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31:29/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains *yūliju al-layla fī al-nahāri wa-yūliju al-nahāra fī al-layli*: *"He adds from the decrease of the hours of the night into the hours of the day (`yazīdu min nuqṣāni sāʿāti al-layli fī sāʿāti al-nahār`), and He adds what has decreased from the hours of the day into the hours of the night,"* quoting **Qatādah** (*"the decrease of the night into the increase of the day"*). On *kullun yajrī ilā ajalin musamman*, al-Ṭabarī states: *"And He has subjected the sun and the moon for the interests of His creation... All of that runs by His command to a known time and a limited appointed term; when it reaches it, the sun and the moon shall be folded up (`kuwwirat`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31:29/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains that taking from the night and adding to the day *"occurs in the summer season, when the days lengthen to their utmost limit, then they begin to decrease in length, so the night lengthens and the day shortens, and this happens during the winter season."* Explaining *kullun yajrī ilā ajalin musamman*, Ibn Kathīr cites two primary proofs: first, the canonical *ḥadīth* of Abū Dharr in the Two Ṣaḥīḥs ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199); [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a)), where the Sun travels at sunset to prostrate beneath the Throne; and second, a report recorded by Ibn Abī Ḥātim from **Ibn ʿAbbās** (which Ibn Kathīr explicitly grades as having an authentic chain, *isnāduhu ṣaḥīḥ*): *"The sun is like a waterwheel (`al-shamsu bi-manzilati al-sāqiyah`). It runs during the day in the sky in its orbit, and when it sets, it runs during the night in its orbit beneath the earth until it rises from its east (`fa-idhā gharabat jarat bi-l-layli fī falakihā taḥta al-arḍi ḥattā taṭluʿa min mashriqihā`). And the same is true for the moon."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the seasonal hour-transfer model and Ibn ʿAbbās's waterwheel model of the Sun and Moon running beneath the Earth at night directly reproduce Late Antique Near Eastern, Greco-Roman, and Rabbinic geocentric traditions:

- **Rabbinic Subterranean Night Circuit & Waterwheel Analogy ([Babylonian Talmud, *Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) & [*Eruvin* 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.56a)):** In [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) (c. AD 500), the Talmud records the exact cosmological model taught by Ibn ʿAbbās under [Quran 31:29](https://quran.com/31/29): *"And the sages of the nations of the world say that during the day the sun travels beneath the firmament, and at night it travels beneath the earth (`תחת הקרקע`) and around to the east."* Classical Greco-Roman and Near Eastern writers (such as **Vitruvius**, *De Architectura* IX.1.2, and **Cleomedes**) likewise compared the geocentric revolution of the sun and moon over and under the stationary earth to the turning of a waterwheel (*tympanum* / *sāqiyah*).
- **Babylonian, Zoroastrian, & Talmudic Seasonal Hour-Transfer Cosmology (*MUL.APIN*, *Greater Bundahishn* 5a, & [*Eruvin* 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.56a)):** In the Babylonian astronomical compendium *MUL.APIN* (Tablet I–II, c. 1000 BC), the Middle Persian Zoroastrian *Greater Bundahishn* (5a, describing the Sun shifting across 180 eastern and 180 western apertures in the stone sky), and the Talmudic solstice and equinox (*tekufot*) system in [*Eruvin* 56a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.56a), seasonal day-length variation is explained geocentrically as the Sun shifting its rising and setting tracks across the sky over a stationary Earth, incrementally transferring water-clock hours (*sāʿāt*) from the night into the day until the summer solstice and returning them from the day into the night until the winter solstice—matching al-Ṭabarī's and Ibn Kathīr's explanation of *yūliju*.

18:86.title: The Sun Setting in a Terrestrial Muddy or Hot Spring (Quran 18:86)
18:86.summary: [Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18/86) states that Dhū-l-Qarnayn reached the physical "setting-place of the sun" (*maghrib al-shams*), where he found the sun setting into a "muddy spring" (*ʿayn ḥamiʾah*—or "hot spring," *ʿayn ḥāmiyah*, in the second canonical reading) and discovered a tribe living beside it. Early Muslim authorities in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/18:86/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/18:86/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), and [Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4002](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4002) understood this literally as the sun sinking into a western spring of hot water and black clay (*ṭīnah sawdāʾ*). In reality, Earth is a rotating spheroid orbiting a star 109 times its diameter at a distance of 149.6 million km, so the sun has no terrestrial setting point. This account reflects ancient Mesopotamian (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX), Greco-Roman, pre-Islamic Arabian (*Tubbaʿ* poetry), and Talmudic ([*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a)) flat-earth sunset lore.
18:86.explanation:
Cosmology / Flat Earth. In [Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18/86), the world-conqueror Dhū-l-Qarnayn journeys to the western extremity of a flat earth and reaches the physical location where the sun sets into a muddy, hot spring beside an inhabited settlement.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18/86) narrates Dhū-l-Qarnayn's western expedition: *"Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun (`maghriba al-shamsi`), he found it setting in a muddy spring (`wajadahā taghrubu fī ʿaynin ḥamiʾatin`), and he found next to it a people (`wa-wajada ʿindahā qawman`)."* Two canonical readings (*qirāʾāt mutawātirah*) exist for the spring's adjective: *ḥamiʾah* (`حَمِئَةٍ`, "possessing black mud," `ḥamaʾah`) and *ḥāmiyah* (`حَامِيَةٍ`, "blazing hot," `ḥārrah`).

Several grammatical and physical features of the text conflict with modern astronomy:
- **A Reachable Terrestrial Terminus (*Maghrib al-Shams*):** In classical Arabic morphology, *maghrib* (paired in [Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18/90) with *maṭliʿ*, "rising-place") functions here as a noun of place (*ism makān*) denoting the geographical spot where the sun descends. Furthermore, the text states that he found a people living *"next to it"* (`ʿindahā`), treating the sun's setting-place and its spring as a localized terrestrial landmark.
- **Literal Verb of Discovery Without Simile:** The verse uses the direct verb *wajadahā* ("he found it") with no particle of optical comparison (*ka-annahā*, "as if it were"). When the Quran describes an optical illusion, it explicitly marks the perception—as in [Quran 27:44](https://quran.com/27/44) (*"she thought it was a pool of water,"* `ḥasibathu lujjatan`).
- **Astrophysical Reality:** The sun is a main-sequence star with a diameter of `~1.392 million km` (`~109×` Earth's diameter) and a volume `~1.3 million` times Earth's, located `149.6 million km` (`1 AU`) away. Sunset is not the physical descent of the solar disk into a western body of water or mud, but the apparent horizon crossing caused by Earth's eastward axial rotation (`~1,670 km/h` at the equator).

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Foundational *tafsīr* and *ḥadīth* collections confirm that the earliest generations of Muslims—and the harmonization of both canonical readings by al-Ṭabarī—treated the sun's descent into a hot, muddy spring as a physical event:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18:86/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Recording transmissions from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Mujāhid**, and **Qatādah**, al-Ṭabarī quotes Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: *"Ibn ʿAbbās used to recite this word as {in a muddy (`ḥamiʾah`) spring} and say: 'Black mud (`ḥamaʾah sawdāʾ`) in which the sun sets (`taghrubu fīhā al-shams`).'"* Al-Ṭabarī also records the dispute between Caliph Muʿāwiyah (who recited *ḥāmiyah*, "hot") and Ibn ʿAbbās (who recited *ḥamiʾah*, "muddy"), in which Kaʿb al-Aḥbār testified that the sun sets in water and black mud (*thaʾṭ* / *ṭīnah sawdāʾ*). Reconciling the two canonical readings, al-Ṭabarī concludes: *"Neither of their two aspects invalidates its companion. That is because it is permissible for the sun to set in a hot spring possessing mud (`ḥamaʾah`) and clay (`ṭīn`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18:86/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Writing in the 14th century after Ptolemaic spherical astronomy entered Islamic scholarship, Ibn Kathīr reinterprets the verse as a visual impression over the ocean because the sun *"never leaves the fourth celestial sphere (`al-falak al-rābiʿ`) in which it is fixed."* Yet when reconciling *ḥamiʾah* and *ḥāmiyah*, Ibn Kathīr concedes the physical interaction of the solar rays with the spring: *"There is no contradiction between their meanings; for it could be hot due to its proximity to the glare of the sun at its setting (`li-mujāwaratihā wahaja al-shamsi ʿinda ghurūbihā`), and its meeting the rays without any barrier, and `ḥamiʾah` (muddy) being in water and black mud."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Sunan Abī Dāwūd 4002](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4002) (graded *ṣaḥīḥ* in chain by al-Albānī), Abū Dharr narrates that while riding behind Muhammad on a donkey at sunset, the Prophet asked: *"Do you know where this sets?"* and answered: *"Verily, it sets in a hot spring (`fī ʿaynin ḥāmiyatin`)."* Likewise, in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4802](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4802), Muhammad asks Abū Dharr at sunset where the sun goes and explains that it travels (*tadhhabu*) until it prostrates beneath the Throne and asks permission to rise again.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The narrative of a world-conqueror traveling to the western edge of a flat earth where the sun physically sets into a heated or muddy body of water reflects widespread Near Eastern, Mediterranean, and Arabian folklore:

- **Mesopotamian, Egyptian & Greco-Roman Sunset Lore (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX; Strabo, *Geography* III.1.5):** In the Babylonian *Epic of Gilgamesh* (Tablet IX), the hero journeys to the twin mountain gates of *Mashu* at the western and eastern ends of the flat earth guarding the setting-place (*ereb šamši*) and rising-place (*ṣīt šamši*) of the sun god Shamash, while Ancient Egyptian cosmology depicted the solar barque sinking into the western waters of *Nun*. Similarly, in Greco-Roman popular cosmology critiqued by **Posidonius** and **Strabo** (*Geography* III.1.5; cf. **Juvenal**, *Satires* 14.280; **Statius**, *Silvae* 2.7.24–27), common folklore along the Atlantic coast held that the setting sun physically plunges into the western ocean, heating the water with a sizzling hiss.
- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Poetry & Talmudic Cosmology (*Tubbaʿ* Poetry; [*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a); [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** In pre-Islamic South Arabian (*Ḥimyarī*) poetry recorded by Ibn ʿAbbās in *Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr*, **Tubbaʿ** described Dhū-l-Qarnayn seeing the sun set *"in a spring of mud (`khalab`) and black mire (`thaʾṭ ḥarmad`)."* In the Babylonian Talmud, [*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a) recounts Alexander of Macedon questioning the Elders of the South about the sun in the extreme east and west, while [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) and [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b) describe the sun passing through sky-dome windows and heating subterranean springs (*maʿyanot*) at night.

18:90.title: Reaching the Terrestrial Rising-Place of the Sun (Maṭliʿ al-Shams) in Quran 18:90
18:90.summary: [Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18/90) describes Dhū-l-Qarnayn traveling eastward until he reached the physical "rising-place of the sun" (*maṭliʿ al-shams*), where he found it rising directly upon a primitive people who had no shelter (*sitran*) from its scorching proximity. Classical commentators in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/18:90/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) and [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/18:90/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) explain that at this eastern terminus of the earth, the emerging sun was so close and intense that the inhabitants had to submerge themselves in the sea or hide in underground tunnels until noon. In reality, a spherical rotating Earth has no eastern edge where the sun rises closer to the ground, and horizon sunlight is cooler due to atmospheric scattering. This motif reflects ancient Mesopotamian (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX), Greco-Roman (*Alexander Romance*; Pliny's *Natural History* V.8), and Talmudic ([*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a)) flat-earth sunrise lore.
18:90.explanation:
Cosmology / Flat Earth. In [Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18/90), Dhū-l-Qarnayn travels to the opposite end of a flat earth—the literal geographical rising-place of the sun (*maṭliʿ al-shams*)—where a nation dwells exposed to the sun's immediate emergence without shelter.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Following his journey to the sun's western setting-place ([Quran 18:86](https://quran.com/18/86)), [Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18/90) recounts Dhū-l-Qarnayn's eastern march: *"Until, when he reached the rising-place of the sun (`maṭliʿa al-shamsi`), he found it rising on a people for whom We had not provided any shelter from it (`wajadahā taṭluʿu ʿalā qawmin lam najʿal lahum min dūnihā sitran`)."*

This description rests on two pre-modern cosmological assumptions that contradict planetary physics:
- **A Fixed Terrestrial Location for Sunrise (*Maṭliʿ al-Shams*):** In Arabic grammar, *maṭliʿ* (on the pattern *mafʿil*, paired with *maghrib* in v. 86) is a noun of place (*ism makān*) designating the physical point where the sun ascends from the eastern edge of the earth. On a spherical Earth rotating continuously on its axis (`~1,670 km/h` at the equator) at a distance of `149.6 million km` from the sun, there is no eastern boundary or "place of sunrise" on the globe; sunrise occurs successively across every meridian of longitude.
- **The Myth of Scorching Horizon Proximity:** The narrative presupposes that people living at the far eastern edge of the world require special protection because the sun emerges right beside them without a barrier (*min dūnihā sitran*). In atmospheric physics, solar irradiance is weakest—not strongest—at sunrise, because low-angle rays traverse a much thicker column of air (`~38×` greater optical air mass at the horizon than at the zenith), scattering and absorbing solar radiation before it reaches the ground.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Islamic exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions confirm that `maṭliʿ al-shams` was understood as the physical eastern extremity of the earth where the sun emerges from beneath the world:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18:90/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains that Dhū-l-Qarnayn found the sun rising upon a nation whose land had no mountains or trees and could not support buildings (`lā taḥtamilu bināʾan`), forcing them to flee from the rising sun: *"Rather, they would plunge into the waters, or burrow into tunnels (`wa-innamā yaghūrūna fī al-miyāhi aw yasrubūna fī al-asrāb`)."* Citing **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** (who attributed it to the *ḥadīth* of the Companion Samurah ibn Jundab) and **Qatādah**, al-Ṭabarī records: *"Whenever the sun rose upon them, they would plunge into the water, and when it set, they would come out grazing as animals graze,"* or hide in subterranean tunnels (*asrāb*) until the sun passed its zenith (*zālat ʿanhumu al-shams*).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 18:90](https://quran.com/18:90/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr states explicitly that Dhū-l-Qarnayn traveled until *"he reached the place where the sun rises from the earth (`intahā ilā maṭliʿi al-shamsi min al-arḍ`)."* Alongside the reports of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and Qatādah, Ibn Kathīr quotes **Ibn Jurayj** on the lethal heat at this eastern rising-point: *"When the sun rose, they would enter tunnels of theirs until the sun passed its zenith, or they would enter the sea... An army once came to them, and its inhabitants said to them: 'Do not let the sun rise on you while you are in it.' They said, 'We will not leave until the sun rises. What are these bones?' They said, 'These are the corpses of an army upon whom the sun rose right here, and they died (`hādhihi jiyafu jayshin ṭalaʿat ʿalayhimu al-shamsu hāhunā fa-mātū`).' So they fled in the earth."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Sun's Daily Return to Its Rising-Place:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4802](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4802), Muhammad describes the sun traveling after sunset to prostrate beneath Allah's Throne until it is commanded: *"Return from where you came (`irjiʿī min ḥaythu jiʾti`), and so it rises from its rising-place (`fa-taṭluʿu min maṭliʿihā`)."* Similarly, [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3273](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3273) states that the sun physically rises at dawn *"between the two horns of Satan."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the Quranic verse and the accompanying *tafsīr* traditions about eastern inhabitants diving into the sea and caves to escape the rising sun reflect ancient Mesopotamian, Hellenistic, and Talmudic flat-earth extremity lore:

- **Mesopotamian Solar-Gate & Hellenistic *Alexander Romance* Lore (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX; Pseudo-Callisthenes):** In Babylonian flat-earth cosmology (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX; *Enūma Eliš* Tablet V), the sun god Shamash emerges each morning through physical eastern mountain portals (*ṣīt šamši*, "the rising-place of the sun") at the edge of the terrestrial disk. In the Hellenistic *Alexander Romance* tradition (Pseudo-Callisthenes, Books II–III) circulating across the pre-Islamic Near East, Alexander the Great marches to the eastern extremity of the habitable earth (*oikoumenē*), encountering primitive, shelterless coastal fish-eaters (*Ichthyophagi*) and cave-dwellers (*Troglodytae*) who submerge themselves in the sea or hide in rock-cut caves to survive the scorching emergence of the sun—matching verbatim the descriptions of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, and Qatādah in classical *tafsīr*.
- **Greco-Roman Ethnography & Talmudic Extremity Cosmology (Herodotus, *Histories* III.104; Pliny, *Natural History* V.8; [*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a); [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** Classical Greco-Roman writers—including **Herodotus** (*Histories* III.104, IV.184), **Pliny the Elder** (*Natural History* V.8.45, VII.2.23), and **Tacitus** (*Germania* 45)—similarly imagined that tribes dwelling near the eastern or southern edges of the world were scorched directly by the emerging morning sun and had to shelter in water or subterranean caverns until afternoon. Likewise, the Babylonian Talmud ([*Tamid* 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tamid.32a); [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b); [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b)) portrays Alexander inquiring about the sun at the extreme east and west and describes the sun passing through physical portals at the eastern edge of the solid sky-vault.

67:5.title: Stars Placed in the Lowest Heaven as Missiles Thrown at Devils (Quran 67:5)
67:5.summary: [Quran 67:5](https://quran.com/67/5) declares that Allah adorned the "lowest heaven" (*al-samāʾ al-dunyā*) with stellar "lamps" (*maṣābīḥ*) and "made them missiles for the devils" (*wa-jaʿalnāhā rujūman li-l-shayāṭīn*). Early authorities in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/67:5/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/67:5/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4701](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4701) confirm that the stars themselves were created for three purposes: adorning the sky, guiding travelers, and pelting eavesdropping *shayāṭīn*. Scientifically, stars are massive thermonuclear plasma spheres light-years away, whereas "shooting stars" are milligram-to-kilogram meteoroids burning up 70–120 km high in Earth's atmosphere. This conflation reflects Sasanian Zoroastrian astral demonology (*Greater Bundahishn* II; *Ardā Wīrāz Nāmag*) and Talmudic cosmology ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
67:5.explanation:
Astronomy. In [Quran 67:5](https://quran.com/67/5), the visible stars are placed inside the nearest celestial ceiling as glowing lamps and equated with atmospheric meteors hurled as projectiles at eavesdropping devils.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 67:5](https://quran.com/67/5) states: *"Certainly We adorned the lower heaven with lamps (`wa-laqad zayyannā al-samāʾa al-dunyā bi-maṣābīḥa`), and made them missiles for the satans (`wa-jaʿalnāhā rujūman li-l-shayāṭīni`) – and We have prepared for them the punishment of the blazing Fire."* Parallel passages in [Quran 37:6–10](https://quran.com/37/6-10) and [Quran 41:12](https://quran.com/41/12) explicitly identify these "lamps" (*maṣābīḥ*) as the stars (*al-kawākib*) set in the nearest of seven stacked heavens.

This verse contains two fundamental astrophysical errors:
- **Conflating Stars with Atmospheric Meteors:** Grammatically, the feminine plural pronoun `-hā` ("them") in `wa-jaʿalnāhā rujūman` refers directly to `maṣābīḥ` ("lamps," i.e., the stars). Because ancient observers called meteors "falling/shooting stars," the text treats the stars adorning the night sky and the streaks of light flashing across the upper atmosphere as the same objects. In reality, stars are immense self-gravitating spheres of hydrogen and helium plasma undergoing nuclear fusion (with masses on the order of `10^29` to `10^32 kg` and distances from `4.24` light-years to billions of light-years), whereas meteors (*shuhub*) are tiny grains of interplanetary dust or rocky debris (`1 mg` to a few kilograms) vaporizing via ram-pressure friction at `70–120 km` altitude in Earth's mesosphere.
- **Inverting Cosmic Scale (`al-Samāʾ al-Dunyā`):** Placing all visible stars inside the "lowest/nearest heaven" (`al-samāʾ al-dunyā`) beneath six higher planetary or angelic heavens reverses the actual architecture of the cosmos: meteor ablation occurs within Earth's own atmosphere (`<120 km`), the moon and planets orbit within the solar system (`384,400 km` to `4.5 billion km`), and stars lie trillions to quintillions of kilometers beyond them across the Milky Way and external galaxies.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* compilers unanimously affirm that the Quran identifies the stars of the night sky as the source of the fiery missiles cast at devils:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 67:5](https://quran.com/67:5/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī confirms the direct grammatical reference of the pronoun: *"He says: {Certainly We adorned the lower heaven with lamps}, which are the stars (`wa-hiya al-nujūm`), and He made them lamps due to their illumination... {and made them missiles for the satans} He says: And We made the lamps with which We adorned the lower heaven as missiles for the satans, by which they are pelted (`wa-jaʿalnā al-maṣābīḥa allatī zayyannā bihā al-samāʾa al-dunyā rujūman li-l-shayāṭīni turjamu bihā`)."*
- **Qatādah's Canonical Dictum on the Three Purposes of Stars:** Both al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr (as well as al-Bukhārī in a chapter heading preceding [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199)) record the statement of **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah**: *"Verily, Allah only created these stars (`hādhihi al-nujūm`) for three purposes: He created them as an adornment for the lower heaven, as missiles for the satans (`wa-rujūman li-l-shayāṭīn`), and as signs by which one is guided. Therefore, whoever seeks to interpret any other meanings for them other than these has spoken with his own opinion, missed his fortune, wasted his share, and burdened himself with that of which he has no knowledge."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 67:5](https://quran.com/67:5/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) & Canonical *Ḥadīth*:** Writing after Ptolemaic astronomy had shown that fixed stars remain stationary in their constellations, Ibn Kathīr suggests that the pronoun `-hā` refers to the "species of lamps" (*jins al-maṣābīḥ*) rather than individual stars, proposing that meteors are thrown from beneath them *"and may be derived from them (`wa-qad takūnu mustamaddatan minhā`)."* Yet in [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2229a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2229a), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4701](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4701), and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4921](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4921), the Prophet himself refers to meteors directly as *"a star that is flung"* (`urmiya bi-najmin` / `al-kawkab alladhī yurmā bihi`) at eavesdropping devils.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the placement of stars in the lowest celestial tier and the folklore that "shooting stars" are fiery projectiles hurled by the starry firmament at ascending demons were deeply rooted in pre-Islamic Near Eastern cosmology:

- **Sasanian Zoroastrian Astral Guard Cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* II & V; *Dādestān ī Mēnōg ī Xrad* 49; *Ardā Wīrāz Nāmag*):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology, the celestial vault is arranged in stacked tiers in which the fixed stars occupy the lowest cosmic station (*star-pāyag*, beneath the stations of the moon and the sun) and act as Ohrmazd's front-line military garrison. When Ahriman's demons (*dēwān*) and airborne sorceress-demons (*pairikās* / *parīgān*) attempt to ascend and breach the celestial sphere, the star-captains (led by *Tishtar*, *Satavēs*, *Vanand*, and *Haptōring*) hurl fiery meteors to drive them back and prevent them from corrupting the upper heavens.
- **Talmudic Seven-Heavens & Eavesdropping-Demon Lore ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Chagigah* 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.16a)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), c. AD 500), the lower firmament (*Rakia*) is similarly described as the solid vault in which the stars and constellations are fixed, while [*Chagigah* 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.16a) teaches that winged demons (*shedim*) fly up to the firmament and *"hear from behind the curtain (`pargod`) when God reveals something of the future."*
- **Pre-Islamic Natural Philosophy (Aristotle, *Meteorologica* I.4):** Centuries before Islam, Greek natural philosophers had already distinguished fixed stars from meteors (*diattontes astēres*), noting in Aristotle's *Meteorologica* (I.4, 341b–342a) and Pliny's *Natural History* (II.36) that shooting stars occur in the sublunar upper atmosphere rather than among the celestial stars.

37:10.category: Stars are Missiles Shot at Devils
37:10.title: Piercing Meteors (Shihāb Thāqib) Pursuing Eavesdropping Devils in Quran 37:10
37:10.summary: [Quran 37:10](https://quran.com/37/10) (completing [Quran 37:6–9](https://quran.com/37/6-9)) claims that devils attempt to eavesdrop on the angelic assembly in the lowest heaven until any devil who snatches a word is pursued by a "piercing flame" (*shihāb thāqib*, i.e., a shooting star). Classical exegetes in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/37:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) and [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/37:10/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), supported by [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4701](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4701) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2229a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2229a), even assert that shooting stars began pelting devils as a sign of Muhammad's prophethood. In reality, meteors are natural interplanetary dust and rock particles burning up in Earth's mesosphere, and regular meteor showers were documented for millennia before Islam. The verse adapts Talmudic demonology ([*Chagigah* 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.16a)), Sasanian Zoroastrian star-guard myths (*Bundahishn* II), and pre-Islamic Arabian *kāhin* folklore.
37:10.explanation:
Stars are Missiles Shot at Devils. In [Quran 37:10](https://quran.com/37/10), atmospheric meteors (*shihāb thāqib*) are explained as targeted fiery projectiles launched from the starry firmament to burn airborne devils who snatch overheard words from the angels.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Within the opening cosmological passage of Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt ([Quran 37:6–10](https://quran.com/37/6-10)), the text states that God adorned the nearest heaven with stars (*bi-zīnatin al-kawākib*, v. 6) to guard it against every rebellious devil (v. 7) so they cannot listen to the Exalted Assembly (*al-malaʾ al-aʿlā*) and are pelted from every side (vv. 8–9). [Quran 37:10](https://quran.com/37/10) concludes: *"Except for the one who snatches a word (`illā man khaṭifa al-khaṭfata`), and then a piercing flame pursues him (`fa-atbaʿahu shihābun thāqibun`)."* A parallel account in [Quran 72:8–9](https://quran.com/72/8-9) portrays the *jinn* discovering that the sky has recently been filled with stern guards and flaming meteors (*shuhuban*) waiting in ambush.

This account conflicts with observational astronomy and planetary science on two levels:
- **Physical Mechanism of Meteors:** A *shihāb* (meteor or "shooting star") is not a guided weapon launched at supernatural beings near a celestial ceiling. Meteors occur when meteoroids—typically millimeter-to-centimeter grains shed by comets or fragments from asteroids—enter Earth's upper atmosphere at geocentric velocities of `11 to 72 km/s`. Compression of atmospheric air molecules ahead of the particle heats and ionizes the gas at altitudes of `70–120 km`, producing a brief luminous trail.
