- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Creation Order and Gated Heavens:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2789](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2789), light (*al-nūr*) is created on Wednesday after the soil, mountains, and trees; in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3207](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3207), the *Miʿrāj* depicts the seven heavens as seven physical stories with gates above `al-samāʾ al-dunyā`; and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3210](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3210) describes meteors guarding the lowest sky from devils.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Every element of [Quran 41:12](https://quran.com/41/12) echoes pre-Islamic Rabbinic, Mesopotamian, and Sasanian cosmology:

- **Talmudic Seven Firmaments & Earth-First Schedule ([*Chagigah* 12a–12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12a–12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), c. AD 500), the School of Hillel teaches that the earthly foundation was built before the upper heavens, and Reish Lakish enumerates the seven firmaments (*Vilon, Rakia, Sheḥakim, Zevul, Maʿon, Makhon, Aravot*), placing the sun, moon, and stars in the lower firmament (*Rakia*) and filling the higher heavens with ministering angels and storehouses of snow, hail, and water—matching al-Suddī's commentary in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 41:12](https://quran.com/41:12/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) that each heaven contains *"angels, oceans, and mountains of hail (`mina al-biḥāri wa-jibāli al-barad`)."*
- **Mesopotamian & Sasanian Seven-Tiered Heavens and Star-Lamps (*Enūma Eliš* & *Greater Bundahishn* II):** In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* IV.135–146; *KAR* 307), the sky is partitioned into stacked stone heavens (*šamû*) above the earthly floor (*Ešarra*) with constellations affixed on the lower ceiling and guards posted. Likewise, Sasanian Zoroastrian texts (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a, II; *Tir Yasht* 8) place all fixed stars in the lowest sky-station (*star-pāyag*) nearest the Earth as lamps and guards casting shooting-star missiles at airborne demons (*pairikās* and *dēws*).

2:22.title: The Sky Built as an Architectural Canopy (Bināʾ) Over a Spread-Out Earth in Quran 2:22
2:22.summary: [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22) describes God as the One who made the earth a spread-out mattress or couch (*firāshan*) and the sky an architectural structure or dome (*bināʾan*), sending down rain from that ceiling to bring forth fruit. In modern astrophysics and meteorology, Earth is an oblate spheroid (`r ≈ 6,371 km`) orbiting in a vacuum, and rain condenses from tropospheric water vapor (`~1–12 km` high) rather than descending from a solid overhead roof. Classical exegetes in [al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/2:22/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) and [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/2:22/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), together with [Bukhārī 3207](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3207), explicitly define *bināʾ* as a physical dome (*qubbah*) and solid ceiling (*saqf*) pitched over a flat terrestrial resting-place. This two-part cosmic house reflects ancient Near Eastern, Mesopotamian (*Enūma Eliš*), Talmudic ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)), and pre-Islamic Bedouin tent-and-dome cosmologies.
2:22.explanation:
Sky is a Tent/Dome. [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22) frames the cosmos as a two-part architectural edifice consisting of a flat, spread-out terrestrial floor (*firāsh*) covered by a built celestial canopy or dome (*bināʾ*), reflecting pre-modern Near Eastern roof-and-floor cosmology rather than a spherical planet surrounded by a gaseous atmosphere.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

In [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22), the text appeals to the visible structure of the world: *"(He it is) who made the earth as a couch (`firāshan`) for you, and the sky a dome (`bināʾan`), and sent down water from the sky, by means of which He produced fruits as a provision for you"* (`ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشٗا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءٗ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءٗ فَأَخۡرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزۡقٗا لَّكُمۡ`).

Lexically, the verse pairs two complementary domestic and architectural terms:
1. **`Al-arḍa firāshan` (`ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِرَٰشٗا`, "the earth as a spread bed / mattress / carpet"):** From *f-r-sh* (`فرش`), denoting a level sleeping mat or carpet spread out horizontally as a floor (paired with *mahdan*, "cradle/bed," in [Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53) and *bisāṭan*, "spread carpet," in [Quran 71:19](https://quran.com/71/19)).
2. **`Wa-l-samāʾa bināʾan` (`وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءٗ`, "and the sky as a built structure / canopy / dome"):** From *b-n-y* (`بني`, "to build or erect a structure"), which in classical Arabic denotes either a masonry ceiling or a pitched desert tent (hence *ahl al-bināʾ*, "tent-dwellers"). Across parallel passages, the Quran equates this celestial *bināʾ* with a solid overhead roof (`saqfan maḥfūẓan`, "a guarded ceiling," in [Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32); cf. [Quran 40:64](https://quran.com/40/64), [Quran 52:5](https://quran.com/52/5), and [Quran 79:27–28](https://quran.com/79/27-28)).

This depiction conflicts with physical reality on two levels:
- **No Overhead Celestial Edifice (*Bināʾ* / *Saqf*):** The sky (`al-samāʾ`) is not a built architectural roof or dome erected over a flat floor. What appears from Earth's surface as a blue vault is Rayleigh scattering of sunlight across a thin, gravitationally bound atmosphere (with `~99.99997%` of its mass below the `100 km` Kármán line) transitioning into the vacuum of space.
- **Spherical Geodesy and Tropospheric Precipitation:** The Earth is an oblate spheroid (mean radius `r ≈ 6,371 km`) rotating on its axis and orbiting the Sun at `~107,000 km/h`, where "up" is the radially outward vector from the planet's center of mass. Rain (`māʾ`) does not descend from a cosmic ceiling (*bināʾ*); it condenses within tropospheric clouds (`~1–12 km` high) driven by solar evaporation from Earth's oceans.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Muslim Companions, Successors (*tābiʿūn*), and classical lexicographers unanimously understood `firāshan` and `bināʾan` in [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22) as a literal floor and a domed ceiling:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2:22/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī (d. 923 CE) defines `al-arḍa firāshan` as an outspread resting-place (`mihādan muwaṭṭaʾan wa-qarāran yustaqarru ʿalayhā`), transmitting from **al-Suddī**, **Ibn ʿAbbās**, and **Ibn Masʿūd** (Narration 475): *"It is a couch (`firāsh`) that is walked upon, and it is the resting-place (`al-mihād`) and stable ground (`al-qarār`)."* Explaining `wa-l-samāʾa bināʾan`, al-Ṭabarī notes that a house roof is called *samāwah*, and cites **al-Suddī**, **Ibn ʿAbbās**, and **Ibn Masʿūd** (Narration 478): *"Thus the structure of the sky over the earth is in the shape of a dome, and it is a ceiling over the earth (`fa-bināʾu al-samāʾi ʿalā al-arḍi ka-hayʾati al-qubbati, wa-hiya saqfun ʿalā al-arḍ`)."* He likewise records **Qatādah** (Narration 479): *"He made the sky a ceiling for you (`jaʿala al-samāʾa saqfan laka`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2:22/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr (d. 1373 CE) explains: *"Meaning: [He made the earth] a resting-place like a bed (`mahdan ka-l-firāsh`), settled, leveled, and anchored with towering mountains (`muqarraratan muwaṭṭaʾatan muthabbatatan bi-l-rawāsī al-shāmikhāt`); 'and the sky a structure (`bināʾan`),' which is the ceiling (`wa-huwa al-saqf`)."* Ibn Kathīr cross-references [Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32) and [Quran 40:64](https://quran.com/40/64), and cites **Ibn Masʿūd** in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4477](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4477) on `andādan`.
- **Canonical Hadith on the Solid Ceiling of the Heavens:** In the *Miʿrāj* recorded in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3207](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3207) (and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 162a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:162a)), the nearest heaven (`al-samāʾ al-dunyā`) is a physical overhead ceiling with locked gates that open only when Gabriel knocks, matching the architectural *bināʾ* and *saqf* of [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Pairing the earth as a spread-out floor or mattress with the sky as a solid architectural roof or pitched desert tent—from which rainwater is released downward—was a widespread cosmological misconception across the ancient Near East and pre-Islamic Arabia:

1. **Mesopotamian, Persian, and Pre-Islamic Arabian Tent-Dome Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* & *Bundahishn*):** In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV.135–146), Marduk splits Tiamat's carcass to erect the sky as a solid overhead roof with bolts and guards to hold back the upper waters above the flat terrestrial floor (*Ešarra*). Similarly, Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a) depicts the sky (*asmān*) as a solid metallic or stone vault arched like a dome over a flat, spread-out earth. In pre-Islamic Bedouin society, where a pitched tent itself was called a *bināʾ* (hence *ahl al-bināʾ*, "tent-dwellers"), poets such as **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** and **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah** routinely envisioned the sky as a vast cosmic tent-roof erected over the flat desert floor.
2. **Talmudic Solid-Canopy and Rain-Storehouse Cosmology ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)), the lowest firmament (*Vilon* / *Raqiaʿ*) is described as a physical overhead canopy spread above the flat earth, containing literal upper storehouses and windows through which rainwater descends (cf. Rabbi Eliezer vs. Rabbi Yehoshua in [*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b)). [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22) reproduces this exact pre-modern Near Eastern pairing of a flat terrestrial mattress (*firāsh*) and an overhead architectural dome (*bināʾ*).

13:2.title: Raising the Heavens Without Visible Pillars (Bi-Ghayri ʿAmad) in Quran 13:2
13:2.summary: [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2) states that God raised up the heavens without pillars that people can see (*bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā*), mounted the Throne, and subjected the Sun and Moon to run their courses for an appointed term. Scientifically, the sky is not a heavy physical roof elevated above the earth that would otherwise require load-bearing columns (*ʿamad*), nor are the Sun and Moon co-equal luminaries traversing a dome beneath a domed Throne. Classical commentators in [al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/13:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) and [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/13:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), citing [Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199), debated only whether the sky-dome rests on invisible pillars or stands as an arch without pillars, while explicitly rejecting spherical astronomy. This motif echoes pre-Islamic Arab poetry by Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, Zoroastrian *a-stūn* (pillarless sky) cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a), and the Talmud ([*Chagigah*](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
13:2.explanation:
Sky is a Tent/Dome. [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2) presents the heavens as a massive overhead roof elevated (*rafaʿa*) above the earth without visible structural columns (*bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā*), beneath which the Sun and Moon run as twin luminaries under a domed Throne.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Opening Surah al-Raʿd, [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2) cites the suspension of the sky and the motion of the Sun and Moon as signs of divine power: *"(It is) God who raised up the heavens without pillars that you (can) see. Then He mounted the throne, and subjected the sun and the moon, each one running (its course) for an appointed time"* (`ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ عَمَدٖ تَرَوۡنَهَاۖ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ وَسَخَّرَ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَۖ كُلّٞ يَجۡرِي لِأَجَلٖ مُّسَمّٗى`).

In classical Arabic grammar, `rafaʿa al-samāwāti bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā` (cf. [Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10)) admits two syntactic readings depending on whether `tarawnahā` modifies `al-samāwāt` ("He raised the heavens without any pillars, as you see them") or `ʿamad` ("He raised the heavens upon pillars that you cannot see"). Under either reading, the physical premise conflicts with modern astrophysics:

1. **The Sky as a Heavy Elevated Roof (*Rafaʿa ... bi-Ghayri ʿAmad*):** The noun `ʿamad` (`عَمَد`, plural of `ʿamūd`) denotes load-bearing columns or tent-poles used to prop up a heavy roof (`saqf`, cf. [Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32); [Quran 79:27–28](https://quran.com/79/27-28)). Presenting the absence of visible pillars as a miracle presupposes that the sky (`al-samāwāt`) is a solid canopy that gravity would otherwise pull crashing down onto the earth—as stated in [Quran 22:65](https://quran.com/22/65) (*"He withholds the sky from falling on the earth except by His permission"*). In reality, outer space is a vacuum and Earth's atmosphere is a thin gas shell bound to a spherical planet by gravity; there is no overhead ceiling resting on invisible pillars or standing as an arch.
2. **Geocentric Pairing of the Sun and Moon (*Wa-Sakhkhara al-Shamsa wa-l-Qamara*):** The verse pairs the Sun and Moon as two co-equal bodies running (`yajrī`) across the sky beneath the Throne, whereas the Moon is a small rocky satellite (`r ≈ 1,737 km`) orbiting Earth and the Sun is a central star (`1.39 million km` wide) orbited by Earth.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and Hadith collections confirm that early Islam understood [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2) as a literal domed roof over a flat earth:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī (d. 923 CE) paraphrases: *"God raised up the seven heavens without pillars that you can see, and so made them an elevated roof (`saqfan masmūkan`) for the earth,"* defining `ʿamad` as *"columns (`al-sawārī`), and that by which a building is propped up (`wa-mā yuʿmadu bihi al-bināʾ`)."* Al-Ṭabarī records two schools among the Companions and Successors: (1) **Invisible Pillars:** Narrations 20051–20058 from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Mujāhid**, **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī**, and **Ibn Jurayj** state: *"[He raised them] with pillars that you do not see (`bi-ʿamadin lā tarawnahā`),"* resting on Mount Qāf; and (2) **A Pillarless Dome:** Narration 20059 from **Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah** states: *"The heaven is domed over the earth like a dome (`al-samāʾu muqabbabatun ʿalā al-arḍi mithla al-qubbah`),"* alongside **Qatādah** (Narration 20060): *"He raised it without pillars."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) and Rejection of Spherical Astronomy:** Ibn Kathīr (d. 1373 CE) cites both **Ibn ʿAbbās / Mujāhid** (`lahā ʿamadun wa-lākin lā turā`) and **Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah** (`al-samāʾu ʿalā al-arḍi mithlu al-qubbah`), describing the seven heavens as concentric roofs separated by `500 years'` travel. On `thumma istawā ʿalā al-ʿarshi wa-sakhkhara al-shamsa wa-l-qamar`, Ibn Kathīr cites **Abū Dharr** in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4802](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4802)—where the Sun sets and prostrates beneath the Throne—and explicitly rejects spherical Greek astronomy (*al-falak al-mustadīr*): *"According to the correct view proved by the textual evidence, it [the Throne] is like a dome (`ka-l-qubbah`) over the world from this side, and does not surround it like the celestial spheres (`wa-laysa bi-muḥīṭin ka-sāʾiri al-aflāk`), because it has legs (`qawāʾim`) and bearers who carry it; and this cannot be conceived in a spherical orb (`wa-lā yutaṣawwaru hādhā fī al-falaki al-mustadīr`)."* He further groups the Sun and Moon among *"the seven wandering stars/planets (`al-kawākib al-sayyārah al-sabʿah`)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both rival interpretations in [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2)—cosmic pillars holding up the sky versus a heavy firmament suspended without pillars—were widespread in pre-Islamic Near Eastern literature:

1. **Pre-Islamic Arabian Poetry (Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt / Zayd ibn ʿAmr):** On [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), Ibn Kathīr quotes a pre-Islamic *ḥanīfī* poem attributed to **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** (or **Zayd ibn ʿAmr**): *"Did You level this [earth] without pegs (`bi-lā watadin`) until it settled cleanly as You commanded? And say to It: Did You raise this [heaven] without pillars (`a-anta rafaʿta hādhī bi-lā ʿamadin`)? How gentle a builder (`bānin`) You are!"*
2. **Sasanian Pillarless Vault (*A-stūn*) & Near Eastern Sky-Supports (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a & *Gilgamesh* IX):** While Egyptian and Mesopotamian myths imagined the sky propped up by cosmic pillars (*sḫn.w*) or mountain peaks (*Mashu* in *Gilgamesh* IX), Sasanian Zoroastrian cosmogony (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a.6; *Dādestān ī Dēnīg* 90) marvels that Ohrmazd suspended the solid sky-vault (*asmān*) over the earth *"without pillars"* (Middle Persian *a-stūn*) and subjected the Sun (*Mihr*) and Moon (*Māh*) to run across the dome.
3. **Talmudic Cosmic Pillars vs. an Arched Dome ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b)):** The Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) debates whether the cosmos rests upon one, seven, or twelve pillars (*ʿammūdim*), paralleling the **Ibn ʿAbbās / Mujāhid** school (`bi-ʿamadin lā tarawnahā`), while [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b) and [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) describe the sky as an arched dome (*kippah*) over the flat earth—matching **Iyās ibn Muʿāwiyah's** dome (`mithla al-qubbah`).

81:11.title: Stripping Off the Sky Like an Animal Hide or Tent Covering (al-Samāʾu Kushiṭat)
81:11.summary: [Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81/11) portrays the eschatological dismantling of the cosmos by declaring that the sky will be "stripped off" (*wa-idhā al-samāʾu kushiṭat*), employing a verb reserved in classical Arabic for skinning the hide from a slaughtered camel or pulling away a physical roof covering. Early exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/81:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/81:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical traditions ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4812](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4812)) confirm that this describes detaching, pulling off, and rolling up a solid overhead canopy. In modern astrophysics, the blue sky is merely Rayleigh-scattered sunlight within a gaseous atmosphere fading into the vacuum of space, whereas this imagery reflects pre-Islamic Bedouin leather-tent cosmology, Mesopotamian and Zoroastrian solid-vault traditions (*Enūma Eliš*, *Greater Bundahishn* 1a), and Talmudic depictions of the firmament ([Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
81:11.explanation:
Sky is a Tent/Dome. In [Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81/11), the sky (*al-samāʾ*) is depicted as a solid, tangible overhead sheet or hide that will be physically peeled back, pulled off, and rolled up on the Day of Resurrection.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81/11) states: *"And when the sky is stripped off (wa-idhā al-samāʾu kushiṭat)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), the passive verb *kushiṭat* (`كُشِطَتْ`, from the root *k-sh-ṭ*, with a dialectal variant *qushiṭat* `قُشِطَتْ` transmitted from ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd) denotes the mechanical flaying or peeling off of an outer covering that adheres to an underlying body—specifically skinning the hide off a camel or sheep (*kashaṭa al-jilda ʿan al-baʿīr*) or stripping off a physical roof or tent canopy (*kashaṭa al-saqfa aw al-ghiṭāʾ*). Across the wider Quranic cosmology, this overhead *samāʾ* is consistently described as a constructed roof or canopy ([Quran 21:32](https://quran.com/21/32), *saqfan maḥfūẓan*; [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22), *bināʾan*) that will eventually be rolled up like a parchment scroll ([Quran 21:104](https://quran.com/21/104)).

Scientifically, there is no solid dome, membrane, or physical ceiling above the Earth that could be peeled off, tugged away, or rolled up:
- **Atmospheric Gas & Rayleigh Scattering:** What human observers perceive as the "sky" is a tenuous envelope of gases (primarily nitrogen and oxygen) held around a spherical Earth by gravity, appearing blue during the day due to Rayleigh scattering of shorter solar wavelengths.
- **Gradual Transition to Interplanetary Vacuum:** Atmospheric density decreases exponentially with altitude (passing the Kármán line at ~100 km and merging continuously into the exosphere and interplanetary space) without any solid boundary, skin, or structural vault.
- **Incompatibility with Cosmic Expansion:** Beyond the atmosphere lies nearly 93 billion light-years of observable three-dimensional spacetime containing hundreds of billions of galaxies—not a two-dimensional skin or tent cover enclosing a terrestrial floor.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Authoritative classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* literature unanimously interpret *kushiṭat* as the literal physical detachment, pulling away, and folding up of the overhead firmament:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī defines the clause directly: *"He, Exalted is His mention, says: And when the sky is removed, drawn away, and then rolled up (`nuziʿat wa-judhibat thumma ṭuwiyat`)."* Al-Ṭabarī transmits chains from **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** stating that *kushiṭat* means *"it is drawn away (`judhibat`),"* and notes that in the recitation of **ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd** it is read *qushiṭat* with a *qāf*, explaining that *al-qashṭ* and *al-kashṭ* share the identical meaning of stripping or peeling off a covering.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under the heading *"Removing the Heavens,"* Ibn Kathīr records the consensus of early *salaf* authorities: *"Mujāhid said, 'It is drawn away (`ijtudhibat`).' Al-Suddī said, 'Stripped off (`kushifat`).' Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said, 'It is stripped off and goes away (`tankashiṭu fa-tadhhabu`).'"* Later classical commentators such as al-Qurṭubī and al-Baghawī likewise add: *"That is, it is pulled off from its places just as a hide is skinned from a sheep (`ka-mā yukshaṭu al-jildu ʿani al-shāh`) and as a roof is stripped off."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Rolling Up the Heavens:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4812](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4812) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 7382](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7382), Abū Hurayrah narrates that Muhammad said: *"Allah will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection and roll up the heavens in His Right Hand (`wa-yaṭwī al-samāwāti bi-yamīnihi`), and then He will say: 'I am the King; where are the kings of the earth?'"* Likewise, in [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3333](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3333), Muhammad singles out Surah al-Takwīr ([Quran 81:1](https://quran.com/81/1)–14): *"Whoever wishes to look at the Day of Resurrection as though he were seeing it with his own eyes, let him recite: 'When the sun is wrapped up' (81:1)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The conception of the sky as a solid tent-cloth, animal hide, or vaulted covering stretched over the earth that can be peeled back and folded up was a widespread cosmological motif across pre-Islamic Arabia and the ancient Near East:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin Tent & Hide Cosmology (*Bayt al-Shaʿr* & *Qubbah*):** In pre-Islamic pastoral Arabia (*Jāhiliyyah*), nomadic dwellings were constructed from tanned leather hides (*adīm* / *qubbah*) or woven goat-hair canopies (*bayt al-shaʿr*) pitched over the desert floor, which were dismantled when breaking camp by stripping off and folding the outer hide or roof covering (*kashaṭa al-ghiṭāʾ*). Pre-Islamic poets such as **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** and **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah** routinely projected this domestic tent architecture onto the cosmos, envisioning the heavens as a pitched leather or cloth canopy stretched over the earth.
- **Mesopotamian, Persian, and Talmudic Solid-Canopy Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*, & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In the Babylonian creation epic (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV.135–140), Marduk splits the carcass of Tiamat like a dried fish and stretches half of her hide overhead as a solid sky-roof to hold back the upper waters, while Sasanian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a, 34) depicts the sky (*asmān*) as a physical vault enclosing the world until the final cosmic renovation (*Frashokereti*). Likewise, in [Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) and [*Pesachim* 94a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94a), the firmament (*rāqîaʿ*) is described as a solid physical vault or tent curtain spread above the earth, directly paralleling the Bedouin hide-stripping metaphor of [Quran 81:11](https://quran.com/81/11).

34:9.category: Sky can Fall Down on People
34:9.title: Solid Fragments of the Sky Falling Down as Punishment (Kisafan mina al-Samāʾ)
34:9.summary: [Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34/9) warns unbelievers that God could either cause the ground to swallow them or drop solid "fragments of the sky" (*kisafan mina al-samāʾ*) down upon their heads, presupposing that the sky is a rigid physical vault surrounding humanity from above. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/34:9/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/34:9/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) confirm that *kisafan* means broken physical chunks or pieces (`qiṭaʿan`) of the overhead heaven, pairing this threat with historical accounts of Meccan skeptics demanding falling sky-stones ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4648](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4648)). In atmospheric physics, the sky is a gaseous envelope held by gravity rather than a solid ceiling that can break into falling slabs, a notion rooted in ancient Near Eastern (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*), Greco-Roman, and Talmudic solid-firmament traditions ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
34:9.explanation:
Sky can Fall Down on People. In [Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34/9), the sky (*al-samāʾ*) is conceptualized as a solid physical ceiling encompassing the earth whose broken fragments (*kisaf*) can be dropped onto human beings as a mechanical counterpart to the ground collapsing beneath them.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34/9) asks: *"Do they not look to what is before them and what is behind them of the sky and the earth? If We (so) please, We could cause the earth to swallow them, or make fragments of the sky fall on them (aw nusqiṭ ʿalayhim kisafan mina al-samāʾi). Surely in that is a sign indeed for every servant who turns (in repentance)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *kisaf* (`كِسَف`, plural of *kisfah* `كِسْفَة`, or singular collective in alternate readings) denotes broken-off solid pieces, chunks, or severed fragments of a physical object. This motif recurs across the Quran: in [Quran 22:65](https://quran.com/22/65), God *"holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His leave"* (`wa-yumsiku al-samāʾa an taqaʿa ʿalā al-arḍi`); in [Quran 26:187](https://quran.com/26/187) and [Quran 17:92](https://quran.com/17/92), skeptics challenge prophets to drop *"pieces of the sky"* (`kisafan mina al-samāʾi`) upon them; and [Quran 52:44](https://quran.com/52/44) states that even if they saw *"a fragment of the sky falling"* (`kisfan mina al-samāʾi sāqiṭan`), they would dismiss it as heaped-up clouds.

From the standpoint of atmospheric physics and astronomy, the pairing of the ground caving in beneath people with chunks of the sky falling down upon them rests on a pre-scientific structural cosmology:
- **Gaseous Composition of the Sky:** The visible sky is not a solid roof, dome, or crystalline shell suspended above the Earth; it is an atmosphere of gas molecules (78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 1% argon and trace gases) already resting on Earth's surface under hydrostatic equilibrium.
- **Impossibility of Falling "Sky Fragments":** A gas cannot fracture into solid slabs or pieces (*kisaf*) that detach and crash down onto a population. While stony or metallic meteoroids orbit the Sun in space and occasionally enter Earth's atmosphere as meteorites, they are independent solar-system bodies, not broken pieces of an overhead ceiling.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegesis and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions confirm that early Muslims understood [Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34/9) as describing a tangible overhead roof encompassing humans that could literally break into falling pieces:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34:9/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains the spatial framing of the verse: *"So that they may know that wherever they are, My earth and My sky are encompassing them (`muḥīṭatun bihim`) from before them and from behind them, and from their right and from their left... out of caution that We might command the earth and cause it to swallow them, or the sky and cause fragments to fall upon them (`aw al-samāʾa fa-tasquṭa ʿalayhim qiṭaʿan`)."* Citing **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah**, al-Ṭabarī glosses *kisafan mina al-samāʾi* directly as *"pieces from the sky (`qiṭaʿan mina al-samāʾi`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34:9/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr similarly highlights the physical canopy model: *"Meaning, wherever they go, in whatever direction, the heavens are a canopy shading over them (`fa-l-samāʾu miẓallatun muẓallilatun ʿalayhim`), and the earth is beneath them, just as He said: {With Hands did We construct the heaven... And We have spread out the earth} ([Quran 51:47](https://quran.com/51/47)–48)... And His saying: {If We will, We shall sink the earth with them, or cause a piece of the heaven to fall upon them} means: If We wished, We could do that to them because of their wrongdoing and Our power over them."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4648](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4648), Anas ibn Mālik reports how Abū Jahl challenged Muhammad in Mecca using this same cosmological premise: *"O Allah! If this is indeed the Truth from You, then rain down on us a shower of stones from the sky (`fa-amṭir ʿalaynā ḥijāratan mina al-samāʾi`),"* while [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 2118](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:2118) describes the companion punishment of the earth literally sinking and swallowing (*yukhsafu*) an entire army in the desert.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that the sky is a solid vault subject to structural collapse—and that it can fracture into falling chunks above humanity—was widespread throughout Talmudic, ancient Near Eastern, Pre-Islamic Arabian, and Greco-Roman tradition:

- **Talmudic Solid-Vault & Pillars Cosmology ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b), & [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud, [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) depicts the firmament (*rāqîaʿ*) as a thick, solid overhead ceiling resting upon cosmic pillars above the terrestrial plane, while [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b) and [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) describe the sky as a rigid arched dome (*qubbah*) enclosing the world whose physical structure must be held aloft over the earth.
- **Mesopotamian, Persian, Pre-Islamic Bedouin, and Greco-Roman Sky-Collapse Beliefs (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*, & Classical Ethnography):** Across the ancient Near East, the sky was conceptualized as a rigid physical roof—fashioned from Tiamat's split hide in Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV.135–146), from solid stone or crystal (*asmān*) in Sasanian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a), and as a raised tent-roof in pre-Islamic Bedouin poetry (such as **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** and **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah**). Similarly, in classical Mediterranean philosophy and ethnography (Aristotle, *On the Heavens* II.1, 284a, critiquing the ancient belief that the sky requires Atlas to keep it from collapsing onto the earth; Arrian, *Anabasis Alexandri* 1.4.8; Strabo, *Geography* 7.3.8), ancient peoples routinely feared that the solid vault of heaven might fracture and fall upon them, matching the threat of falling sky-fragments (*kisaf*) in [Quran 34:9](https://quran.com/34/9).

15:26.title: Direct Creation of Humanity from Ringing Clay and Molded Mud (Ṣalṣāl min Ḥamaʾin Masnūn)
15:26.summary: [Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15/26) asserts that God created the first human directly from "dry ringing clay" (*ṣalṣāl*) formed out of "molded black mud" (*ḥamaʾin masnūn*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/15:26/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/15:26/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2611](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2611)) interpret this literally as Adam being sculpted into a hollow earthenware statue that rang when tapped before being animated. Scientifically, clay and mud are hydrous aluminosilicate minerals dominated by silicon and aluminum, whereas human biochemistry is carbon-based with virtually zero structural silicon, and genomic and fossil evidence proves that *Homo sapiens* evolved gradually from ancestral primates rather than from a ceramic figure, echoing ancient Mesopotamian (*Atrahasis*), Greco-Roman (Prometheus), and Talmudic ([*Sanhedrin* 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38b)) clay-molding anthropogonies.
15:26.explanation:
Evolution. In [Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15/26), human origins are attributed to the direct physical sculpting of a hollow ceramic statue out of sun-dried clay and altered black mud, contradicting both elemental biochemistry and the evolutionary history of *Homo sapiens*.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15/26) states: *"Certainly We created the human from dry clay, from molded mud (`wa-laqad khalaqnā al-insāna min ṣalṣālin min ḥamaʾin masnūnin`),"* followed in [Quran 15:28–29](https://quran.com/15/28-29) by God telling the angels: *"Surely I am going to create a mortal from dry clay, from molded mud. So when I have proportioned him (`sawwaytuhu`) and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him prostrating."* A parallel verse, [Quran 55:14](https://quran.com/55/14), adds that this *ṣalṣāl* was *"like potter's earthenware"* (`ṣalṣālin ka-l-fakhkhār`). In classical Arabic lexicography, *ṣalṣāl* (`صَلْصَال`) denotes parched, hardened clay that emits a ceramic ringing sound (*ṣalṣalah*) when struck, while *ḥamaʾin masnūn* (`حَمَإٍ مَسْنُونٍ`) denotes dark, fetid alluvial mud shaped into a form.

This ceramic creation account conflicts with modern natural science on two fundamental levels:
- **Geochemical vs. Biological Composition:** Terrestrial clay and mud (*ṣalṣāl* / *ḥamaʾ*) consist of **hydrous aluminosilicate minerals** (kaolinite, montmorillonite, illite) whose crystal lattices are built from **silicon (`Si`), aluminum (`Al`), and oxygen (`O`)**. By contrast, the human body is an organic, carbon-water system composed (`~99%` by mass) of **oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, calcium, and phosphorus**; silicon and aluminum occur only in trace parts-per-million (`<0.005%`), and aluminum is biologically non-essential and neurotoxic. Moulding wet river mud and drying it into pottery-like clay cannot chemically yield cellular tissues, lipids, proteins, or nucleic acids.
- **Evolutionary & Genomic Continuity vs. Instantaneous Sculpting:** Independent lines of empirical evidence—including a continuous hominin fossil record across Africa and Eurasia (*Australopithecus* → *Homo erectus* → *Homo sapiens*), shared endogenous retroviral insertions (ERVs) at identical orthologous loci across humans and chimpanzees, and the head-to-head telomeric fusion on **human chromosome 2** (preserving vestigial interstitial telomeres at band `2q13` and an inactivated ancestral centromere at `2q21.3–2q22.1`)—prove that humans evolved gradually from earlier primate populations rather than originating from an inanimate clay statue.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Muslim exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* unanimously affirm that [Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15/26) describes the literal sculpting of Adam's lifeless clay body prior to its animation:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15:26/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains: *"Certainly We created Adam, who is the human (`wa-laqad khalaqnā Ādama wa-huwa al-insānu`), from Salsal (dry clay)... It is dry clay that has not been touched by fire; if you tap it, it sounds (`fa-idhā naqartahu ṣalla`) and you hear its ringing sound (`ṣalṣalah`)."* Citing chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Qatādah**, and **Mujāhid**, al-Ṭabarī records that *ṣalṣāl* is *"the thinned clay from which pottery (`fakhkhār`) is made"* or mud that cracks *"until it becomes like thin earthenware (`ka-l-khazaf al-riqāq`),"* while *ḥamaʾin masnūn* is *"clay that has altered into blackness (`al-ṭīnu al-mutaghayyiru ilā al-sawād`)"* and been molded into a complete human figure (`ḥamaʾun muṣawwarun tāmm`).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 15:26](https://quran.com/15:26/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr cites **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Mujāhid**, and **Qatādah** stating that *ṣalṣāl* means *"dry mud (`al-turāb al-yābis`),"* cross-referencing [Quran 55:14](https://quran.com/55/14), and explains *min ḥamaʾin masnūn* as dried clay derived from black, smooth (`amlas`), poured (`maṣbūb`), or putrid (`muntin`) mud.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Adam's Hollow Clay Body:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2611](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2611), Anas ibn Mālik narrates that Muhammad said: *"When Allah fashioned Adam in Paradise, He left him as He liked him to leave. Then Iblīs roamed around him to see what actually that was, and when he found him hollow from within (`fa-lammā raʾāhu ajwafa`), he recognized that he had been created with a disposition that he would not have control over himself."* Similarly, [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3326](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3326) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2841](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2841) state that Adam was created directly at a height of *"sixty cubits"* (`sittīna dhirāʿan`, ~30 meters).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The conception of the first human as a ceramic statue molded out of dark alluvial mud and dried into pottery-like clay before being animated was a widespread anthropogonic myth across the pre-Islamic Near East and Mediterranean:

- **Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Greco-Roman Potter-God Anthropogonies (*Atrahasis*, Khnum, & Prometheus):** In the Sumerian myth *Enki and Ninmah* and the Old Babylonian epic *Atrahasis* (Tablet I.190–260), the gods knead alluvial river clay (*ṭīṭu*) to sculpt the first human figures. In ancient Egyptian religion (inscribed at the temples of Esna and Elephantine), the ram-headed potter god **Khnum** literally molds human bodies out of dark Nile alluvial mud (`ḥamaʾ`) on a potter's wheel (`fakhkhār`) before life is breathed into the clay figure. Likewise, in Greco-Roman mythology (**Hesiod**, *Works and Days* 60–61; **Apollodorus**, *Library* 1.7.1; **Ovid**, *Metamorphoses* 1.80–83), **Prometheus** mixes earth and water to fashion the first humans as lifeless clay statues before Athena breathes a living soul into them.
- **Talmudic & Pre-Islamic Arabian Clay-Statue Traditions ([*Sanhedrin* 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Sanhedrin* 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.38b)), Rabbi Yoḥanan bar Ḥanina divides the creation of the first human on Friday into sequential hours: in the first hour his dust was gathered; in the second it was kneaded into a shapeless mass of mud (*golem*); in the third his limbs were molded; and in the fourth a soul was cast into the lifeless figure. Pre-Islamic Arabian poetry (such as verses attributed to **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** and **ʿAdī ibn Zayd al-ʿIbādī**) similarly circulated folkloric accounts of the first man being sculpted from wet mud and dried into ringing potter's clay (*ṣalṣāl* / *fakhkhār*) prior to animation.

2:117.title: Instantaneous Fiat Creation without Precursor Forms (Badīʿ al-Samāwāt wa-l-Arḍ / Kun Fa-Yakūn)
2:117.summary: [Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2/117) describes God as the unpreceded Originator (*Badīʿ*) of the heavens and earth who brings creatures into existence instantaneously by saying "Be! and it is" (*kun fa-yakūn*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/2:117/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/2:117/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) define *Badīʿ* as creating *de novo* without any prior model or ancestor (*ʿalā ghayri mithālin sabaqa*), linking *kun fa-yakūn* to the instantaneous creation of Adam from dust ([Quran 3:59](https://quran.com/3/59)) in the twinkling of an eye ([Quran 54:50](https://quran.com/54/50)). Scientifically, both the cosmos (13.8 billion years of cosmic expansion and planetary accretion) and life (3.8 billion years of descent with modification from ancestral species) developed through gradual evolutionary processes rather than verbal fiat, reflecting Egyptian (*Memphite Theology*), Mesopotamian (*Enūma Eliš*), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), and Talmudic ([*Chagigah* 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12a)) doctrines.
2:117.explanation:
Evolution. In [Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2/117), the origin of the cosmos and living beings is attributed to instantaneous verbal fiat (*kun fa-yakūn*) without any prior template or precursor (*badīʿ*), conflicting with both biological evolution by descent with modification and astrophysical deep time.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2/117) declares: *"Originator of the heavens and the earth (`badīʿu al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍi`). When He decrees something, He simply says to it, 'Be!' and it is (`fa-innamā yaqūlu lahu kun fa-yakūnu`)."* Across the Quranic corpus, these two expressions form the foundation of an explicitly anti-evolutionary, instantaneous creation model:
- **Creation Without Precursor (`Badīʿ`):** Morphologically derived from *ibdāʿ* (to originate without precedent), *Badīʿ* asserts that the structures of the cosmos and its inhabitants were brought into being *de novo*, without any prior ancestral form or prototype.
- **Instantaneous Verbal Fiat (`Kun Fa-Yakūn`):** The command *"Be! and it is"*—which [Quran 54:50](https://quran.com/54/50) equates in duration to *"the twinkling of an eye"* (`ka-lamḥin bi-l-baṣar`; cf. [Quran 16:40](https://quran.com/16/40) and [Quran 36:82](https://quran.com/36/82))—is explicitly applied in [Quran 3:59](https://quran.com/3/59) to the biological origin of Adam and Jesus: *"Surely the likeness of Jesus with God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then He said to him, 'Be!' and he was (`thumma qāla lahu kun fa-yakūnu`)."*

This doctrine of unpreceded, instantaneous fiat creation contradicts empirical evidence across evolutionary biology and astrophysics:
- **Descent with Modification from Precursor Species:** Living organisms were not originated without prior models (*ʿalā ghayri mithālin sabaqa*). Comparative genomics, paleontology, and molecular phylogenetics show that all extant species evolved over `~3.8 billion years` by gradual modification of pre-existing ancestral lineages. Humans share **~98.8% alignable nucleotide identity** with chimpanzees, thousands of orthologous endogenous retroviral insertions (ERVs), and identical disabling mutations in shared pseudogenes—such as the frameshift deletion in exon 10 of the **L-gulonolactone oxidase (*GULO*) pseudogene** across all haplorhine primates—proving inheritance from a common ancestor.
- **Cosmic and Planetary Deep Time:** Neither the heavens nor the Earth came into being simultaneously by an instantaneous decree; radiometric dating and cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations show that the universe expanded over **13.8 billion years**, requiring billions of years of stellar nucleosynthesis before the solar system and Earth coalesced **4.54 billion years ago**.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators on [Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2/117) stress that *Badīʿ* and *kun fa-yakūn* exclude prior origins, ancestral models, or gradual intermediate causes:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2:117/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains that *Badīʿ al-samāwāti wa-l-arḍ* means *al-Mubdiʿ*, defined as *"the Initiator and Maker of that which no one has preceded Him in initiating or making anything similar to it (`al-munshiʾu wa-l-muḥdithu mā lam yasbiqhu ilā inshāʾi mithlihi wa-iḥdāthihi aḥad`)."* He concludes that God is *"their Maker, Creator, and Bringer into being from no origin, and without any pattern which He followed for them (`wa-mūjiduhā min ghayri aṣlin, wa-lā mithālin iḥtadhāhā ʿalayhi`),"* citing **al-Suddī** (#1859): *"He originated them and thus created them, and nothing was created before them so that He could take it as an example (`wa-lam yukhlaq qablahā shayʾun fa-yatamaththala bihi`)."* Al-Ṭabarī adds that the same *kun fa-yakūn* decree produced the Messiah without a father and transformed Sabbath-breakers directly into *"despised apes"* (`qiradatan khāsiʾīn`).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 2:117](https://quran.com/2:117/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr quotes **Mujāhid** and **al-Suddī** defining *Badīʿ* as *"their Creator without any precedent model (`khāliquhumā ʿalā ghayri mithālin sabaqa`),"* endorses al-Ṭabarī's explanation that God originated the world and Jesus *"without any origin and without any prior model,"* and explains `kun fa-yakūn` as an instantaneous command uttered *"once, and it is (`marratan wāḥidatan fa-yakūnu`),"* citing [Quran 54:50](https://quran.com/54/50) and Adam's creation in [Quran 3:59](https://quran.com/3/59).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Primordial Creation:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3191](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3191) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2653b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2653b), Muhammad states that God ordained the measures of creation fifty thousand years before creating the heavens and the earth while His Throne rested upon water.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Instantaneous creation by spoken divine command (*creatio per verbum*) without prior material or biological precursors was a widespread cosmological motif across the ancient Near East:

- **Egyptian & Mesopotamian Creation by Spoken Command (*Memphite Theology* & *Enūma Eliš*):** In the Egyptian **Memphite Theology** (inscribed on the **Shabaka Stone**, c. 710 BC), the creator-god **Ptah** conceives each cosmic structure and living creature in his heart (*ḥaty*) and brings them into immediate existence solely by pronouncing their names with his tongue (*ns*). Similarly, in the Babylonian creation epic ***Enūma Eliš*** (Tablet IV.19–26), the gods test **Marduk's** creative power by placing a constellation (*lumāšu*) before him: *"Command both destruction and creation (`abātu u banû`), and let it be so (`li-ib-ši`)!"* Marduk speaks a word and the constellation vanishes; he speaks again and it is instantaneously re-created.
- **Zoroastrian, Greco-Roman, & Talmudic Creation Without Precursor ([*Chagigah* 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12a)):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1.1–59), **Ahura Mazda** fashions the spiritual (*mēnōg*) and material (*gētīg*) creations directly without evolutionary precursors by reciting the sacred *Ahunawar* formula, while Greco-Roman Stoic and Neoplatonic cosmologies (*Plotinus*, *Enneads* V.1) modeled cosmic origination as an immediate emanation of divine reason (*logos*) without temporal trial-and-error. Likewise, in the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12a)), Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva debate whether the heavens and the earth were brought into existence simultaneously at a single instant, assuming instantaneous *de novo* origination without any prior physical template or ancestral lineage.

7:189.title: Monogenetic Origin of Humanity from a Single Soul and Rib-Derived Mate (Min Nafsin Wāḥidah)
7:189.summary: [Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7/189) states that God created all humanity from a "single person" (*nafsin wāḥidah*, Adam) and fashioned his spouse (*zawjahā*, Eve) directly out of him, followed by humanity's first pregnancy. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/7:189/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/7:189/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3331](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3331), [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1468a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1468a)) confirm that Eve was literally formed from one of Adam's ribs and that all humans descended from this primeval couple. In population genetics, human genetic diversity—especially trans-species *HLA* alleles—proves that *Homo sapiens* never passed through a two-person bottleneck (requiring an ancestral effective population of ~10,000+ individuals), and female mammals evolved alongside males over 160 million years ago rather than from a primeval man's rib, echoing Sumerian (*Enki and Ninhursag*) and Talmudic ([*Eruvin* 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.18a)) traditions.
7:189.explanation:
Evolution. In [Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7/189), the entire human species is traced to a single primordial male individual (*nafsin wāḥidah*) and a female consort fashioned directly out of his body, a monogenetic and anatomical claim refuted by human population genetics and mammalian evolutionary biology.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7/189) declares: *"He (it is) who created you from one person (`khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin`), and made from him his spouse (`wa-jaʿala minhā zawjahā`), so that he might dwell with her. And when he covered her (`fa-lammā taghashshāhā`), she bore a light burden and passed on with it. But when she became heavy, they both called on God their Lord, 'If indeed You give us a righteous (child), we shall indeed be among the thankful.'"* Together with [Quran 4:1](https://quran.com/4/1) and [Quran 39:6](https://quran.com/39/6), this verse makes two explicit biological claims: (1) strict **single-couple monogenism**, asserting that all humans descend from a solitary founding pair, and (2) **somatic derivation of the first female from a male**, asserting that the first woman was constructed physically from the first man's body before they conceived the first human child.

Both claims conflict directly with established findings in genetics and evolutionary biology:
- **Population Genetics Rules Out a Two-Person Bottleneck:** A single founding couple (`N = 2` diploid individuals) can carry at most **4 distinct alleles** at any autosomal locus. However, modern human populations possess dozens of deeply divergent allelic lineages at the **major histocompatibility complex (*HLA-A*, *HLA-B*, *HLA-DRB1*)** that exhibit **trans-species polymorphism**—meaning these alleles diverged millions of years before the speciation of *Homo sapiens* and were inherited continuously from ancestral primate populations. Coalescent modeling and PSMC analyses of whole human genomes demonstrate that the ancestral effective population size ($N_e$) of the human lineage never fell below **~10,000 to 15,000 breeding individuals**.
- **Mammalian Sex Determination & the Impossibility of Rib-Derived Females:** Sexual reproduction and chromosomal sex determination (`XX` female / `XY` male) evolved in early therian mammals over **160 million years ago**, long before hominins appeared; there was never a stage where a single male existed prior to females. Moreover, somatic tissue from a genetic male's rib (`46,XY`) carries male sex chromosomes and cannot anatomically or genetically generate an independent female genome (`46,XX`).

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* unanimously affirm that [Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7/189) refers literally to Adam, the creation of Eve (*Ḥawwāʾ*) from his rib, and her first pregnancy:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7:189/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī states: *"He says: {He (it is) who created you from one person (`khalaqakum min nafsin wāḥidatin`)}, meaning by the one person: Adam,"* citing **Mujāhid** (#15497) and **Qatādah** (#15498). On `{and made from him his spouse (`wa-jaʿala minhā zawjahā`)}`, al-Ṭabarī writes: *"And He made from the one person, which is Adam, his spouse Eve,"* quoting **Qatādah** (#15499) verbatim: *"Eve, so she was made from one of his ribs (`Ḥawwāʾ, fa-juʿilat min ḍilaʿin min aḍlāʿihi`), so that he might dwell with her."* Al-Ṭabarī explains `{she bore a light burden}` as *"the fluid that Eve bore in her womb from Adam (`al-māʾu alladhī ḥamalathu Ḥawwāʾu fī raḥimihā min Ādam`),"* and records from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Abū al-Bakhtarī**, and **Abū Mālik** (#15507) that when Eve's pregnancy grew heavy, Adam and Eve prayed for a *"normal human being (`basharan sawiyyan`)"* because *"they feared it might be a beast (`ashfaqā an yakūna bahīmatan`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7:189/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr writes: *"Allah states that He created all mankind from Adam (`khalaqa jamīʿa al-nāsi min Ādam`), peace be upon him, and that He created his wife, Hawwa' (Eve), from him (`wa-annahu khalaqa minhu zawjahu Ḥawwāʾ`). Then, people spread from them,"* cross-referencing [Quran 4:1](https://quran.com/4/1) and quoting **al-Ḍaḥḥāk** from **Ibn ʿAbbās** that during Eve's pregnancy *"they feared it might be a beast."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Eve's Creation from a Rib:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3331](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3331) (cf. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 5186](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5186)) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1468a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1468a), Abū Hurayrah reports that Muhammad said: *"Treat women nicely, for a woman is created from a rib (`fa-inna al-marʾata khuliqat min ḍilaʿin`), and the most curved portion of the rib is its upper portion; so if you should try to straighten it, it will break, but if you leave it as it is, it will remain crooked."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Forming the first woman out of the first man's rib or body and tracing all humanity to their first conception in [Quran 7:189](https://quran.com/7/189) mirrors ancient Near Eastern, Greco-Roman, Persian, and Talmudic traditions:

- **Sumerian Rib Etiology, Greco-Roman Somatic Splitting, and Zoroastrian Monogenism (*Enki and Ninhursag*, Plato's *Symposium*, & *Bundahishn*):** Generating a female figure from a male's rib traces back to the Sumerian poem ***Enki and Ninhursag*** (lines 250–268, c. 2000 BC): when Enki suffers pain in his rib (`ti`), the goddess Ninhursag brings forth from his body **Ninti** (`Nin-ti`), playing on the Sumerian homonym `ti` (*"rib"* and *"to make live"*). In Greek philosophical myth (**Plato**, *Symposium* 189d–191d), primordial humans were single bodies (`nafsin wāḥidah`) that Zeus split in two, creating male and female halves that long to dwell together (`li-yaskuna ilayhā`). Likewise, Zoroastrian anthropogony (*Greater Bundahishn* 14.1–10) traces humanity to a single founding pair (**Mashya and Mashyanag**) who grew as one joined body before separating into male and female.
- **Talmudic Aggadah on the Rib-Derived Consort ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a) & [*Eruvin* 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.18a)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a) and [*Eruvin* 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.18a)), rabbinic debates between Rav and Shmuel analyze the physical derivation of the first woman from the first man's body—either as a second side separated from a dual-bodied human or as an anatomical rib fashioned into a spouse (cf. [*Sanhedrin* 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.39a)).

2:36.title: Expulsion and Descent of a Fully Formed Founding Couple from Paradise to Earth (Wa-Qulnā Ihbiṭū)
2:36.summary: [Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2/36) states that after Satan caused Adam and his wife to slip in the primordial Garden, God expelled them and commanded them to "Go down" (*ihbiṭū*) to the Earth as a temporary dwelling place with mutual enmity (*baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduww*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/2:36/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/2:36/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 854a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:854a), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4738](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4738)) affirm that a fully formed, giant-statured Adam, Eve, and a four-legged serpent physically descended from heaven to locations like India and Arabia. Scientifically, *Homo sapiens* evolved *in situ* on Earth from earlier terrestrial hominins over hundreds of thousands of years, and snakes evolved leglessness from burrowing lizards over 100 million years ago rather than losing camel-like legs in a fall, reflecting Near Eastern (*Adapa*, *Gilgamesh*), Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*), and Talmudic ([*Sotah* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.9b)) traditions.
2:36.explanation:
Evolution. In [Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2/36), humanity's presence on Earth is explained as the physical descent (*hubūṭ*) of an already fully formed founding couple expelled from a celestial Paradise, contradicting the paleoanthropological, genomic, and biogeographical record of *in situ* terrestrial evolution.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2/36) declares: *"Then Satan caused them both to slip from there (`fa-azallahumā al-shayṭānu ʿanhā`), and to go out from where they were (`fa-akhrajahumā mimmā kānā fīhi`). And We said, 'Go down, some of you an enemy to others (`wa-qulnā ihbiṭū baʿḍukum li-baʿḍin ʿaduwwun`)! The earth is a dwelling place for you (`wa-lakum fī al-arḍi mustaqarrun`), and enjoyment (of life) for a time.'"* Read together with [Quran 2:35](https://quran.com/2/35) and [Quran 7:19–25](https://quran.com/7/19-25), the text posits that anatomically modern, linguistically articulate humans originated outside the terrestrial biosphere in a heavenly Garden (*al-Jannah*) and only began inhabiting the Earth after being cast down (`ihbiṭū`) for eating from a forbidden tree.

This narrative conflicts with multiple independent lines of empirical science:
- **In Situ Terrestrial Evolution of *Homo sapiens*:** The fossil and paleogenomic records demonstrate that *Homo sapiens* did not arrive on Earth as displaced outsiders from a non-terrestrial realm. Rather, modern humans evolved *in situ* in Africa (with early anatomically modern fossils dated to **~300,000 years ago** at Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, and **~195,000–233,000 years ago** at Omo Kibish, Ethiopia) as an unbroken terrestrial chronospecies sequence (*Australopithecus* → *Homo habilis* → *Homo erectus* → *Homo heidelbergensis*).
- **Coevolution with Earth's Biosphere & the Fossil History of Snakes:** Human anatomy and physiology—from endogenous retroviruses shared with African great apes and vitamin D3 synthesis tuned to solar UV-B radiation, to cospeciated gut microbiomes—prove that humanity is indigenous to Earth's ecosystem. Furthermore, the classical etiology attached to `{Go down, some of you an enemy to others}`—that snakes were four-legged beasts in Paradise whose legs retracted into their bellies when cursed alongside Adam and Eve—is refuted by vertebrate paleontology: Cretaceous snake fossils (*Najash rionegrina*, *Haasiophis terrasanctus*, *Pachyrhachis problematicus*) show that snakes evolved limb loss from lizards over **100 million years ago**, long before humans existed.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* interpret [Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2/36) as a literal expulsion and physical descent of Adam, Eve (*Ḥawwāʾ*), Iblīs, and the serpent from the heavenly Paradise to Earth:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2:36/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Explaining how Satan caused Adam and Eve to slip (`fa-azallahumā`) and why God commanded `{Go down, some of you an enemy to others}`, al-Ṭabarī cites **Wahb ibn Munabbih** (#742) and **Ibn ʿAbbās / Ibn Masʿūd** (#743 via al-Suddī): *"When Iblīs wanted to cause them to slip, he entered into the belly of the snake, and the snake had four legs, as if it were a Bukhtī camel (`wa-kānat li-l-ḥayyati arbaʿu qawāʾima ka-annahā bukhtiyyah`), among the finest beasts that Allah created."* After they ate the fruit, God cursed the snake: *"You are the one in whose belly the cursed one entered until he deceived My servant; cursed are you, a curse that makes your legs withdraw into your belly (`tazaḥḥul qawāʾimuki fī baṭniki`), and you shall have no sustenance except the dust. You are the enemy of the children of Adam and they are your enemies."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2:36/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr cites **Ubayy ibn Kaʿb** that Allah created Adam *"as a tall man, with thick hair on his head, looking like a lofty date-palm tree (`ka-annahu nakhlatun suḥūq`),"* and quotes **Ibn ʿAbbās** and **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** on their landing sites: *"Adam was sent down to India (`bi-l-Hind`), Hawwāʾ to Jeddah, Iblīs to Dastumaysān near Baṣrah, and the snake to Iṣfahān (`wa-uhbiṭat al-ḥayyatu bi-Aṣbahān`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Expulsion from Paradise:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 854a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:854a), Muhammad states: *"The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday; on it Adam was created, on it he was made to enter Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it (`wa-fīhi ukhrija minhā`)."* Likewise, [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4738](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4738) records Moses saying to Adam: *"You are the one who got the people out of Paradise by your sin,"* and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3326](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3326) states Adam was 60 cubits (~30 m) tall.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The expulsion from a celestial realm in [Quran 2:36](https://quran.com/2/36) and the four-legged serpent etiology in al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr parallel ancient Near Eastern, Persian, and Talmudic traditions:

- **Mesopotamian & Zoroastrian Myths of Celestial Expulsion and the Deceptive Serpent (*Adapa*, *Gilgamesh*, & *Bundahishn*):** In the Akkadian myth of ***Adapa*** (14th–7th centuries BC), the first sage Adapa ascends to the heaven of Anu, where deceptive counsel regarding the *"bread and water of life"* leads to his return down to Earth as a mortal, while in the ***Epic of Gilgamesh*** (Tablet XI.287–305), a serpent steals the plant of rejuvenation from humanity. In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 4.10–20; 14.11–30), the evil spirit **Ahriman** enters creation in the form of a serpent (*mār*), corrupts the primordial human couple (**Mashya and Mashyanag**) through forbidden food and falsehood, and plunges humanity into terrestrial struggle and perpetual enmity against noxious creatures (*khrafstras*, chief among them serpents).
- **Talmudic Folklore on the Legged Primeval Serpent ([*Sotah* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.9b) & [*Sanhedrin* 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.59b)):** Al-Ṭabarī's report (#742–743) that the pre-curse serpent originally walked on legs before losing them mirrors late antique rabbinic aggadah in the Babylonian Talmud ([*Sotah* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.9b) and [*Sanhedrin* 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.59b)), where the sages depict the primeval serpent as a tall, legged creature capable of walking upright like a camel or servant before its limbs were severed and its food was turned to dust.

86:6.title: Creation from Dual Parental 'Spurting Water' (Māʾ Dāfiq) Emerging from the Torso
86:6.summary: [Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86/6) asserts that a human being is formed directly out of "spurting water" (*māʾ dāfiq*), which the next verse locates as issuing from between the backbone and the ribs. Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/86:6/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/86:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311)) define this liquid as ejaculated sexual fluid bursting forth from both the father and the mother to produce the child. In human reproductive biology, women do not ejaculate a gamete-bearing fluid, bulk seminal plasma is blocked at the cervix rather than becoming the fetus, and gametes originate in pelvic or scrotal gonads instead of the torso. This account echoes the Greco-Roman two-seed ejaculation theory of Hippocrates and Galen alongside Talmudic dual-seed embryology ([*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)).
86:6.explanation:
Anatomy. In [Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86/6), human formation is attributed to macroscopic "spurting water" (*māʾ dāfiq*) emitted from the torso—a description rooted in pre-modern dual-ejaculation and spinal-seed anatomy rather than cellular embryogenesis.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86/6) states: *"He was created from spurting water"* (`خُلِقَ مِن مَّاءٍ دَافِقٍ`, *khuliqa min māʾin dāfiq*), qualified by the adjectival clause in [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7): *"It comes forth from between the spine and the ribs"* (`yakhruju min bayni al-ṣulbi wa-al-tarāʾib`). In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*, root *d-f-q*), *dāfiq* denotes a liquid poured forth with forceful impetus or discharged in spurts, specifically designating ejaculated semen (*al-maniyy*). Grammatically, *māʾin dāfiq* is both the material substrate from which the human is said to be created (*khuliqa min*) and the explicit subject of the verb *yakhruju* ("it emerges") in verse 7.

This claim conflicts with human reproductive anatomy and physiology on three empirical levels:
- **Absence of Female Seminal Ejaculation:** Classical exegesis identifies *māʾ dāfiq* as the combined sexual fluids spurting from both the man and the woman. Biologically, women do not discharge or spurt a reproductive fluid (*māʾ*) containing an ovum during climax; ovulation is a non-ejaculatory follicular rupture releasing a single microscopic secondary oocyte (`~100–120 µm`) into the fallopian tube, while vaginal lubrication contains zero gametes.
- **Seminal Plasma Is Not the Material Substrate of the Embryo:** In males, the forcefully spurted fluid (*māʾ dāfiq*) consists over 98% of acellular seminal plasma secreted by the seminal vesicles (`~65–70%`), prostate gland (`~25–30%`), and bulbourethral glands (`~1%`). This alkaline fluid serves only as a transport medium in the vaginal canal; it is blocked by the cervical mucus plug and never forms the physical body of the embryo, which develops from the fusion of a single spermatozoon with the oocyte.
- **Pelvic Origin vs. Torso Emergence:** Because *māʾin dāfiq* is the grammatical antecedent of *yakhruju* in [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7), the text asserts that this spurting fluid emerges from between the vertebral column (*al-ṣulb*) and the ribs/chest (*al-tarāʾib*), whereas both spermatozoa and seminal plasma are produced and expelled entirely within the scrotum, lesser pelvis, and perineum. Concordist attempts to redefine *māʾ dāfiq* as a microscopic motile sperm cell contradict Arabic lexicography, since a single cell is neither "water" (*māʾ*) nor "spurting" (*dāfiq*).

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Muslim exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions unanimously confirm that *māʾ dāfiq* denotes macroscopic ejaculated sexual fluid emitted by both parents:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86:6/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains: *"Then He said: {He was created from spurting water (`khuliqa min māʾin dāfiq`)}, meaning: from spurted water (`yaʿnī: min māʾin madfūq`), and it is among that which the Arabs expressed with the wording of an active participle (`fāʿil`) while it carries the meaning of a passive participle (`mafʿūl`)."* In **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 86:8](https://quran.com/86:8/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**, al-Ṭabarī records that **Mujāhid** and **ʿIkrimah** interpreted *rajʿihi* as referring directly to the *māʾ dāfiq*—explaining that Allah can return the spurted semen *"into the urethra"* (`fī al-iḥlīl`) or *"into his backbone"* (`fī ṣulbihi`), proving that the *Salaf* understood verses 6–7 strictly as ejaculated seminal liquid.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explicitly includes both male and female fluids in *māʾ dāfiq*: *"Meaning, the sexual fluid (`al-maniyy`) that comes out bursting forth (`yakhruju dafqan`) from the man and from the woman. Thus, the child is produced from both of them by the permission of Allah (`يعني المني يخرج دفقا من الرجل ومن المرأة فيتولد منهما الولد`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Dual Parental Emission:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329), Muhammad states that women emit seminal fluid just as men do: *"The fluid of the man (`māʾ al-rajul`) is thick and white, and the fluid of the woman (`māʾ al-marʾah`) is thin and yellow. From whichever of the two rises above or precedes (`ʿalā aw sabaqa`), the resemblance comes."* Likewise, [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) states that whichever parental fluid prevails determines the child's sex.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that human beings are formed from forceful seminal emissions discharged by both parents from the torso was a foundational doctrine of Greco-Roman medicine and Late Antique rabbinic tradition:

- **Hippocratic Corpus (*On Generation* / *De Genitura* §§1–6, c. 420 BC):** The Hippocratic treatise *On Generation* taught that during intercourse, bodily heat causes humor gathered from the brain and spinal marrow to foam and spurt forth (`apokrinesthai`) as seed (*gonē*). In §4, the author asserted that women also ejaculate reproductive seed (*kai hē gynē aphiei*) from their loins into the uterus during climax, forming the embryo by mixing both spurted fluids.
- **Galen of Pergamon (*On Semen* / *De Semine* I.5–8, II.1–4, 2nd century AD):** Galen defended the two-seed ejaculation theory across the late antique Mediterranean, arguing that the female reproductive tract discharges a thinner seminal fluid that spurts into the womb to commingle with the thicker male semen—matching [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311).
- **Aristotelian & Talmudic Dual-Fluid Parallels (Aristotle & [*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)):** **Aristotle** (*History of Animals* I.1; *Generation of Animals* I.19–20, c. 350 BC) classified sperm alongside blood, marrow, and milk as a homogeneous liquid part (`homoiomerē`) that acts as a fluid coagulant in the womb, while the Babylonian Talmud ([*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)) and Mishnah ([*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3)) likewise trace human creation to a poured seminal drop (`tippah`) and dual parental fluid emissions (*"if the woman emits seed first, she bears a male; if the man emits seed first, she bears a female"*).

86:7.title: Semen Emerging from Between the Spine (al-Ṣulb) and the Female Ribs (al-Tarāʾib)
86:7.summary: [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7) states that the reproductive fluid of the preceding verse issues from between the backbone (*al-ṣulb*) and the ribs (*al-tarāʾib*). Classical lexicographers and commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/86:7/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/86:7/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)), citing Ibn ʿAbbās and pre-Islamic poetry, define *al-ṣulb* as the man's vertebral column and *al-tarāʾib* as the woman's upper chest or collarbones where a necklace rests (*mawḍiʿ al-qilādah*), corroborated by [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a). Anatomically, spermatozoa develop in scrotal testes and seminal plasma is secreted by pelvic accessory glands far below the rib cage and thoracic spine. This claim reflects the Greco-Roman encephalomyelogenic seed doctrine of Hippocrates, Plato, and Galen alongside Talmudic dual-seed anatomy ([*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)).
86:7.explanation:
Anatomy. In [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7), the origin of human reproductive fluid is localized "between the spine and the ribs," reflecting the ancient Mediterranean medical belief that seminal fluid descends along the spinal column and thoracic cage.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Following [Quran 86:6](https://quran.com/86/6) (*"He was created from spurting water"*), [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7) specifies the anatomical source of that fluid: *"It comes forth from (a place) between the spine and the ribs"* (`يَخْرُجُ مِن بَيْنِ الصُّلْبِ وَالتَّرَائِبِ`, *yakhruju min bayni al-ṣulbi wa-al-tarāʾib*). In classical Arabic philology, both anatomical terms have well-attested meanings:
- **`Al-Ṣulb` (`الصُّلْب`):** Denotes the vertebral column, backbone, or loins of a man (cf. [Quran 4:23](https://quran.com/4/23), `min aṣlābikum`, *"from your loins"*).
- **`Al-Tarāʾib` (`التَّرَائِب`, plural of `tarībah`):** Unanimously defined by early Arabic lexicographers—al-Farāhīdī (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*), al-Jawharī (*al-Ṣiḥāḥ*), and Ibn Manẓūr (*Lisān al-ʿArab*, root *t-r-b*)—as the upper chest, collarbones, or upper four ribs where a woman's necklace rests (`mawḍiʿ al-qilādah min al-ṣadr`), as attested in the *Muʿallaqah* of Imruʾ al-Qays (*"her breastbones [`tarāʾibuhā`] are polished like a mirror"*).

Modern reproductive anatomy establishes that neither spermatozoa nor seminal plasma originates in or passes between the vertebral column (*al-ṣulb*) and the thoracic ribs/chest (*al-tarāʾib*):
- **Scrotal Spermatogenesis:** Spermatozoa develop exclusively within the seminiferous tubules of the testes, housed externally in the scrotum to maintain a temperature `2–3°C` below core body temperature (`~34.4°C`).
- **Pelvic Accessory Glands & Urethral Pathway:** Seminal fluid is produced entirely inside the lesser pelvis by the seminal vesicles (posterior to the urinary bladder), the prostate gland (inferior to the bladder), and the bulbourethral glands, and is expelled through the urethra—never descending from the spinal cord or female chest.
- **Inadequacy of Modern Harmonizations:** Proposals that [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7) refers to embryonic gonadal migration, childbirth, or the testicular neurovascular bundle conflict with Arabic syntax and anatomy: (1) under *al-jumal baʿda al-nakirāt ṣifāt*, the clause *yakhruju* modifies *māʾin dāfiq* ("spurting water"), whereas fetal gonads neither are liquid nor secrete semen; (2) childbirth traverses the bony pelvis (`al-ʿānah`), never the upper chest/ribs (`al-tarāʾib`); and (3) systemic vessels and nerves supply every organ without making its secreted fluid emerge from the spine and ribs.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators record that the earliest generations (*al-Salaf*) understood [Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86/7) literally as describing parental fluids issuing from the male backbone and female chest (or the male spine and upper torso):

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86:7/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains that *"from between the spine and the ribs"* means *"it comes forth from both of them"* (`yakhruju minhumā`). Surveying early authorities—including **Ibn ʿAbbās** (*"At-Tarāʾib is the place of the necklace"* and *"From between the breasts of the woman"*), **ʿIkrimah** (*"The spine of the man, and the ribs of the woman"*), **Saʿīd ibn Jubayr** (*"the chest"*), **Mujāhid** (*"between the shoulders and the chest"* or *"below the collarbones"*), **Sufyān al-Thawrī** (*"above the breasts"*), **Qatādah** (*"between the spine of the man and his upper chest [`naḥrihi`]."*), and **Maʿmar ibn Abī Ḥabībah** (*"the extract of the heart [`ʿuṣārat al-qalb`]."*)—al-Ṭabarī concludes: *"The correct statement regarding that in our view is the statement of those who said: It is the place of the necklace on the woman, where it rests upon her chest; because that is what is well-known in the speech of the Arabs, and their poetry has come with it,"* quoting the verses of al-Muthaqqab al-ʿAbdī (`عَلَى تَرِيبٍ`) and another Arab poet (`عَلَى تَرَائِبِهَا`).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 86:7](https://quran.com/86:7/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr opens with Shabīb ibn Bishr from ʿIkrimah from **Ibn ʿAbbās**: *"{Proceeding from between the backbone and the ribs}: The backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman (`ṣulbu al-rajuli wa-tarāʾibu al-marʾah`). It (the fluid) is yellow and fine in texture (`aṣfaru raqīq`). The child will not be born except from both of them,"* noting that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah, and al-Suddī said the same, and that Ibn ʿAbbās placed his hand on his chest to indicate *al-tarāʾib*.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** Ibn ʿAbbās's description of the woman's *tarāʾib* fluid as *"yellow and fine in texture"* echoes [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a) (*"The water of the man is white and the water of the woman is yellow"*) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Locating the generation and descent of reproductive seed in the spinal column, loins, and thoracic vessels was standard medical doctrine across Greco-Roman, Talmudic, and pre-Islamic Near Eastern traditions:

- **Greco-Roman Encephalomyelogenic Theory (Hippocrates, Plato & Alcmaeon):** In *On Generation* (*De Genitura* §§1–2, c. 420 BC) and *Airs, Waters, Places* (§22), **Hippocrates** (following **Alcmaeon of Croton**) taught that reproductive seed is drawn from the brain and bodily humors *"especially into the spinal marrow (`nōtiaios myelos`); and from the spinal marrow passages lead to the kidneys and along the torso to the testicles and penis."* Similarly, **Plato** (*Timaeus* 77d, 91a–b) identified the spinal marrow (`myelos`) running down the vertebral column (`rhachis`) as the conduit of seed (`sperma`), and **Aristotle** (*History of Animals* I.14–15) grouped the backbone (`rhachis`), loins (`osphys`), and ribs (`pleurai`) as the connected frame of the trunk.
