- **Galenic Para-Spinal Vessels, Rabbinic Two-Seed Theory & Pre-Islamic Arabia:** **Diogenes of Apollonia** held that seed is frothy blood drawn from the heart and lungs along the thoracic ribs and spine (matching Maʿmar's gloss *ʿuṣārat al-qalb*, "extract of the heart," in al-Ṭabarī), while **Galen** (*De Semine* I.12–16, II.1–4) taught that seminal vessels descend alongside the spine (*para tēn rhachin*) and that female thin seed mixes with male thick seed—paralleling Babylonian Talmud [*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) and the Greco-Persian curriculum taught at Gundeshapur to **al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah**.

77:20.title: Creation from 'Despicable Water' (Māʾ Mahīn) & the Ancient Putrid-Drop Motif
77:20.summary: [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20) asks rhetorically whether humanity was created from "despicable water" (*māʾin mahīn*), treating macroscopic ejaculated fluid as the raw material out of which the fetus is molded. Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/77:20/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/77:20/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)) define *māʾ mahīn* as a weak, lowly drop of seminal liquid that pools in the uterus and solidifies into blood and flesh. Scientifically, embryogenesis is not the coagulation of bulk seminal fluid (over 98% of which is acellular plasma discarded outside the uterus), but the cellular fusion of a spermatozoon and an oocyte carrying equal genomic information. This verse echoes the rabbinic homily in [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) ("From a putrid drop") alongside Greco-Roman seminal coagulation models in Aristotle and Galen.
77:20.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20), human generation is depicted as the direct material fashioning of the fetus from "despicable water" (*māʾin mahīn*), reflecting the ancient Near Eastern conception of semen as a uniform liquid substrate that curdles in the womb.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20) opens an argument for bodily resurrection by asking: *"Did We not create you from despicable water,"* (`أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم مِّن مَّاءٍ مَّهِينٍ`, *a-lam nakhluqkum min māʾin mahīn*), followed in [Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77/21) by *"and put it in a secure dwelling place (`fa-jaʿalnāhu fī qarārin makīn`)?"*—a formula echoed in [Quran 32:8](https://quran.com/32/8) (*"Then He made his progeny from an extract of despicable water,"* `min sulālatin min māʾin mahīn`). In classical Arabic lexicography (Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*, root *m-h-n*), *mahīn* (`مَهِين`) means weak (*ḍaʿīf*), lowly (*ḥaqīr*), or of little worth, qualifying *māʾ* ("water/fluid") to denote macroscopic ejaculated semen.

Treating *māʾ mahīn*—which verse 21's singular pronoun (`-hu`, "it") places directly inside the womb—as the physical substance transformed into a human being conflicts with developmental biology:
- **Bulk Seminal Fluid Does Not Become the Embryo:** Ejaculated semen (*māʾ*) is not a raw liquid material that enters the uterus and congeals into an embryo. Over 98% of semen consists of acellular seminal plasma (fructose, buffers, and coagulating enzymes from the seminal vesicles and prostate) that remains in the vagina and is barred by cervical mucus from entering the uterine cavity.
- **Omission of the Maternal Oocyte & Cellular Fertilization:** A human embryo is created from two specialized, genetically equivalent haploid cells—a paternal spermatozoon (`23` chromosomes) and a maternal secondary oocyte (`23` chromosomes plus all cytoplasmic organelles and mitochondrial DNA)—which fuse in the fallopian tube. Describing human creation as placing "despicable water" in the womb reduces embryogenesis to the pre-microscopic observation of ejaculated liquid.
- **Pre-Modern Coagulation Model:** Rather than recognizing discrete cellular gametes, the Quranic sequence treats the liquid *māʾ mahīn* / *nuṭfah* as an undifferentiated fluid puddle that sits in the uterus for forty days before coagulating into a blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) and a lump of flesh (*muḍghah*).

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and *ḥadīth* authorities unanimously interpret *māʾin mahīn* as a literal drop of weak seminal liquid deposited in the womb and transformed into the fetus:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77:20/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī glosses the verse directly: *"He, whose mention is exalted, says: {Did We not create you}, O people, {from despicable water (`min māʾin mahīn`)}, meaning: from a weak drop of semen (`yaʿnī: min nuṭfatin ḍaʿīfah`)."* He cites the transmission chain of Muḥammad ibn Saʿd from **Ibn ʿAbbās**: *"Regarding His saying: {Did We not create you from despicable water}, he means by 'despicable' (`al-mahīn`): the weak (`al-ḍaʿīf`)."* Similarly, in **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 32:8](https://quran.com/32:8/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**, al-Ṭabarī defines *māʾin mahīn* as *"a weak, thin seminal fluid"* extracted by the pouring out of a man's water.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77:20/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains: *"{Did We not create you from despicable water} meaning, weak and despised (`ḍaʿīf ḥaqīr`) in comparison to the power of the Creator (`أَيْ ضَعِيفٍ حَقِيرٍ بِالنِّسْبَةِ إِلَى قُدْرَةِ الْبَارِئِ`),"* citing the *ḥadīth* of Busr ibn Jaḥḥāsh (*Musnad Aḥmad* 17842) in which the Prophet spits into his palm and quotes Allah saying: *"O Son of Adam! How can you think that I am unable, when I created you from something like this (i.e., semen)?"* In **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 32:8](https://quran.com/32:8/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)**, Ibn Kathīr adds that this *māʾ mahīn* is *"a drop of fluid (`nuṭfah`) that comes forth from between the loins of a man and the ribs of a woman."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Liquid Drop in the Womb:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a), the embryo's initial stage is described as seminal liquid (*nuṭfah*) collected in the mother's womb for forty days before turning into a clot of thick blood (*ʿalaqah*), while [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1438k](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1438k) states: *"The child does not come from all the liquid (`māʾ`)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the rhetorical structure of [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20) and its depiction of human origin from a lowly liquid drop are directly attested in pre-Islamic rabbinic and Greco-Roman medical literature:

- **Rabbinic Literature ([*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) & [Babylonian Talmud *Niddah* 30b–31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)):** In tractate [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) of the Mishnah (c. AD 200), Rabbi Aqabiah ben Mahalalel employs the same rhetorical question about human creation from a despised or putrid drop of fluid to remind humanity of resurrection and judgment: *"Reflect upon three things and you will not come into the clutches of sin: Know from where you come (`מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ`), and where you are going, and before whom you are destined to give an account and reckoning. From where do you come? From a putrid drop (`מִטִּפָּה סְרוּחָה`, mi-tippah seruchah)."* Likewise, Babylonian Talmud [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)–[31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) (c. AD 500) pairs embryonic formation from a deposited seminal droplet with divine sovereignty over birth and death.
- **Greco-Roman Liquid-Coagulation Embryology (Aristotle, Hippocrates & Galen):** In *Generation of Animals* (*De Generatione Animalium* I.19–20, 727a–729a; II.4, 739b, c. 350 BC), **Aristotle** modeled conception as male seminal liquid curdling maternal blood in the womb like rennet coagulating milk into cheese, while **Hippocrates** (*On Generation* §§1–8) and **Galen** (*De Semine* I.5–8, 2nd century AD) likewise treated bulk ejaculated seminal fluid (*gonē* / *sperma*) as the raw material substrate that pools in the uterus and solidifies into the embryo.

77:21.title: Depositing Seminal Fluid Directly in the Womb (Qarār Makīn) to Settle and Pool
77:21.summary: [Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77/21) states that after forming man from "despicable water," Allah placed that liquid inside a "secure dwelling place" (*qarār makīn*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/77:21/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/77:21/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)) explain that the pronoun "it" (`-hu`) refers to the ejaculated fluid (*al-māʾ al-mahīn*) settling in the womb (*al-raḥim*), where the fluids of the man and woman pool together for forty days. In reproductive biology, ejaculated semen is deposited in the vagina and blocked by cervical mucus from pooling in the uterus, while fertilization actually occurs in the fallopian tube between a single sperm and an ovum. This model reflects the Hippocratic and Galenic doctrine of uterine seed retention alongside Talmudic womb descriptions ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)).
77:21.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77/21), the ejaculated seminal fluid (*māʾ mahīn*) is described as being placed directly inside the uterus (*qarār makīn*) to settle and pool—a physiological misconception shared with ancient Greco-Roman and Near Eastern medicine, which was unaware of the fallopian tubes and tubal fertilization.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Continuing the clause from [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20) (*"Did We not create you from despicable water"*), [Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77/21) states: *"and put it in a secure dwelling place"* (`فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ`, *fa-jaʿalnāhu fī qarārin makīn*)—a phrase parallel to [Quran 23:13](https://quran.com/23/13) (*"Then We made him a drop in a secure dwelling place,"* `thumma jaʿalnāhu nuṭfatan fī qarārin makīn`). Grammatically, the masculine singular object pronoun `-hu` ("it") in *fa-jaʿalnāhu* refers back to *māʾin mahīn* ("despicable water" / seminal fluid) in verse 20, while *qarārin makīn* (literally, "a firmly established resting/settling place," from *q-r-r*, "to settle/rest," for a liquid) denotes the uterus (*al-raḥim*).

This depiction of seminal liquid being deposited and retained inside the uterus as a pooled fluid conflicts with human reproductive physiology in three fundamental respects:
- **Seminal Fluid Does Not Settle in the Uterus:** During coitus, semen is ejaculated into the posterior vaginal fornix, not the uterine cavity. The cervical canal is sealed by viscoelastic cervical mucus that acts as a strict barrier blocking seminal plasma, cellular debris, and abnormal sperm from entering the uterus; only individual motile spermatozoa (`~50 µm`) swim through the cervical mucus.
- **Fertilization Occurs in the Fallopian Tube, Not the Uterine Cavity:** Human conception does not take place by pooling male and female fluids inside the womb (*al-raḥim*). Instead, a single spermatozoon fertilizes the secondary oocyte in the ampulla of the **fallopian tube** (oviduct)—an anatomical structure whose function was unknown in antiquity.
- **Blastocyst Implantation vs. 40-Day Fluid Retention:** Following tubal fertilization, the single-celled zygote undergoes mitotic cleavage for `5–6 days` as it travels down the fallopian tube, entering the uterine cavity only as a multicellular **blastocyst** (`~100–200 cells`) that implants into the endometrium between days `6` and `10`. At no point does a liquid drop (*māʾ* / *nuṭfah*) sit pooled in the womb for forty days.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegesis and canonical *ḥadīth* explicitly confirm that [Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77/21) describes the liquid semen of the man and woman settling inside the uterine cavity:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77:21/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī states: *"And His saying: {and put it in a secure dwelling place}, He says: So We placed the despised water in a womb in which it settled and became securely established (`فَجَعَلْنَا الْمَاءَ الْمَهِينَ فِي رَحِمٍ اسْتَقَرَّ فِيهَا فَتَمَكَّنَ`)."* Al-Ṭabarī then cites two transmission chains from **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** defining *fī qarārin makīn* simply as *"The womb (`al-raḥim`)."* Likewise, in **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 23:13](https://quran.com/23:13/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**, al-Ṭabarī explains that *qarār makīn* is *"where the drop of the man (`nuṭfatu al-rajul`) settles in the womb of the woman."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 77:21](https://quran.com/77:21/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explicitly describes the womb as a receptacle where both parental liquids pool: *"{and put it in a secure dwelling place} meaning, We gathered him in the womb, where the fluid of the man and the woman settles (`يَعْنِي جَمَعْنَاهُ فِي الرَّحِمِ وَهُوَ قَرَارُ الْمَاءِ مِنَ الرَّجُلِ وَالْمَرْأَةِ`). The womb has been prepared for this, as a protector of the fluid deposited in it (`حَافِظٌ لِمَا أُودِعَ فِيهِ مِنَ الْمَاءِ`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on 40-Day Uterine Fluid Collection:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 7454](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:7454), and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a), Muhammad states: *"Verily the creation of each one of you is brought together in his mother's womb (`yujmaʿu khalquhu fī baṭni ummihi`) for forty days as a drop of fluid (`nuṭfah`), then he becomes a clot (`ʿalaqah`) for a like period"*—confirming that classical Islam understood *fa-jaʿalnāhu* (*"jamʿnāhu fī al-raḥim"* in Ibn Kathīr) as the literal gathering of seminal fluid inside the uterus for forty days.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Before Gabriele Falloppio described the oviducts in AD 1561 and Karl Ernst von Baer discovered the mammalian ovum in AD 1827, ancient medical and rabbinic writers universally believed that ejaculated semen entered the uterine cavity directly and pooled there to form the conceptus:

- **Hippocratic Corpus (*On Generation* §5 & *On the Nature of the Child* §§12–14, c. 420 BC):** The Hippocratic authors taught that when a woman conceives, the ejaculated seed (*gonē*) of both the man and the woman flows directly into the uterus (*mētrē*), which immediately draws its mouth (*stoma*) shut to retain the liquid seed inside so that it does not trickle back out, allowing the mixed fluids to settle, warm, and condense.
- **Galen of Pergamon (*On the Natural Faculties* III.3 & *De Semine* I.2–4, 2nd century AD):** Galen elaborated the doctrine of the "retentive faculty" (*kathēktikē dynamis*) of the womb, asserting that the uterus actively draws in and clasps the ejaculated male and female seminal fluids within its cavity until the pooled liquid coagulates with menstrual blood—matching Ibn Kathīr's description of the womb as *"where the fluid of the man and the woman settles... a protector of the fluid deposited in it."*
- **Rabbinic & Late Antique Medical Parallels ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b), [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) & Soranus of Ephesus):** **Soranus of Ephesus** (*Gynecology* I.12, I.43, 2nd century AD) defined the uterus (*mētra*) as the chamber designed to receive and hold the discharged seed until it solidifies, while Mishnah [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) and Babylonian Talmud [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) describe the conceptus developing from a deposited seminal drop (`tippah`) enclosed inside the folded chamber of the mother's womb.

77:22.title: Gestational Duration ('A Known Term,' Qadar Maʿlūm), Six-Month Viability & 40-Day Stages
77:22.summary: [Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77/22) states that the deposited seminal fluid remains in the womb "for a known term" (*ilā qadarin maʿlūm*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/77:22/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/77:22/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) define this appointed duration as a gestation of "six months to nine months" (derived from [Quran 46:15](https://quran.com/46/15) and [Quran 2:233](https://quran.com/2/233)), while canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)) divide the first 120 days of that term into three 40-day periods of static semen, clotted blood, and unformed flesh. Biologically, organogenesis finishes by day 56 (week 8) rather than day 120, and infants born at six lunar months (`~177 days` post-conception) lacked pulmonary surfactant and could not survive in antiquity. This timetable mirrors Hippocratic, Aristotelian, and Talmudic ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)) gestational numerology.
77:22.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77/22), the duration for which reproductive fluid remains in the womb (*ilā qadarin maʿlūm*, "for a known term") is interpreted in classical Islamic sources through a pre-modern gestational calendar of three 40-day pre-fetal stages and a six-lunar-month minimum full-term threshold.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Completing the sentence begun in [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20)–[77:21](https://quran.com/77/21) (*"Did We not create you from despicable water, and put it in a secure dwelling place"*), [Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77/22) adds: *"for a known term?"* (`إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ`, *ilā qadarin maʿlūm*, literally "until a known measure/appointed duration")—an expression repeated in [Quran 23:12](https://quran.com/23/12)–[23:14](https://quran.com/23/14). Within the Quranic and canonical *ḥadīth* corpus, this "known term" of intrauterine development is specified in two ways that conflict with modern obstetrics and developmental biology:

- **The Six-Lunar-Month Minimum Full-Term Gestation ([Quran 46:15](https://quran.com/46/15) & [Quran 2:233](https://quran.com/2/233)):** As [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77:22/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) explains, classical Islam defines the "known term" of pregnancy as lasting *"from six months to nine months."* This six-month minimum was derived by subtracting the 24-month nursing period in [Quran 2:233](https://quran.com/2/233) and [Quran 31:14](https://quran.com/31/14) from the combined 30-month pregnancy-plus-nursing period in [Quran 46:15](https://quran.com/46/15). However, six lunar months equal only `~177 days` (`25.3 weeks`) from conception (`~27 weeks` menstrual gestational age). In human physiology, fetal lungs remain in the canalicular stage until week 26, with insufficient Type II pneumocytes and pulmonary surfactant; prior to late-20th-century neonatal intensive care and exogenous surfactant therapy, deliveries at six lunar months from conception were not viable full-term births.
- **The `40 + 40 + 40 = 120` Day Intrauterine Schedule:** Canonical *ḥadīth* divide the first four months (`120 days`) of this "known term" into three consecutive 40-day intervals: `40 days` as a liquid drop (*nuṭfah*), `40 days` as a blood clot (*ʿalaqah*, days 41–80), and `40 days` as a chewed lump of flesh (*muḍghah*, days 81–120) before skeletal and organ differentiation. In reality, human embryogenesis completes all embryonic stages and organogenesis by **Day 56 (Week 8)**—when the conceptus (`~30 mm`) already possesses a four-chambered beating heart, brain hemispheres, limb buds with separated fingers and toes, and cartilaginous bones—more than two months before Day 120.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Foundational commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* explicitly define the "known term" (*qadar maʿlūm*) of [Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77/22) according to this six-to-nine-month calendar and the three 40-day embryonic phases:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77:22/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains: *"And His saying: {for a known term? (`ilā qadarin maʿlūm`)} He says: to a known time for its emergence from the womb with Allah (`إِلَى وَقْتٍ مَعْلُومٍ لِخُرُوجِهِ مِنَ الرَّحِمِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ`)."* In **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 23:13](https://quran.com/23:13/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**–**[23:14](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**, al-Ṭabarī details that during this term in the *qarār makīn*, the fluid remains until it transforms sequentially into a piece of blood (*ʿalaqah*), a piece of flesh (*muḍghah*), and bones clothed with flesh.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 77:22](https://quran.com/77:22/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr defines the verse concisely: *"{for a known term?} Meaning, for a fixed period of time, which is from six months to nine months (`إِلَى مُدَّةٍ مُعَيَّنَةٍ مِنْ سِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ أَوْ تِسْعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ`)."* Cross-referencing **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 23:13](https://quran.com/23:13/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)** and **[Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22:5/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)**, Ibn Kathīr connects [Quran 77:20](https://quran.com/77/20)–[77:22](https://quran.com/77/22) directly to the 40-day schedule, writing that the drop stays in the womb for forty days, turns into a red clot for forty days, and then becomes a lump of flesh for forty days.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Intrauterine Timeline:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6594](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6594), and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a), Muhammad states on the authority of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: *"Each one of you is collected in the womb of his mother for forty days (`arbaʿīna yawman`), and then turns into a clot (`ʿalaqah`) for an equal period, and turns into a piece of flesh (`muḍghah`) for a similar period, and then Allah sends an angel..."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the 40-day embryonic formation period and the ancient debate over 6-, 7-, and 9-month gestational terms were staples of Greco-Roman medicine and Late Antique rabbinic literature:

- **Greco-Roman Gestational Calendars (Hippocrates, Aristotle & Galen):** In *On the Nature of the Child* (§18, c. 420 BC), *On Seven Months' Children*, and *On Eight Months' Children*, Hippocratic physicians constructed schematic numerical calendars for gestation, asserting that the embryo remains unformed fluid and blood before articulating in 30-to-42-day intervals. **Aristotle** (*History of Animals* VII.3–4, 583b–584b) likewise posited a 40-day threshold for embryonic differentiation and debated fixed monthly pregnancy durations, while **Galen** (*De Semine* I.7–8) divided early intrauterine development into sequential fluid, bloody coagulum, and unformed flesh phases.
- **Rabbinic Gestational Timetables ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b), [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a) & [*Yevamot* 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.42a)):** Babylonian Talmud [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) and [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a) (c. AD 500) preserve the exact same **40-day** milestone (`אַרְבָּעִים יוֹם`, *arbaʿim yom*) as the boundary before which the conceptus in the womb is treated as mere unformed liquid (`maya b'alma`, "mere water"), while [*Yevamot* 42a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.42a) and [*Niddah* 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.27a) codify fixed monthly gestational terms (between six-and-a-half/seven and nine lunar months) to adjudicate paternity and viability.

80:18.title: 'From What Thing Did He Create Him?' — Reducing Human Origin to Seminal Fluid Alone
80:18.summary: [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18) asks rhetorically, "From what thing did He create him?" (*min ayyi shayʾin khalaqahu*), which the following verse answers: "From a drop (*nuṭfah*)!" Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/80:18/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/80:18/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318)) explain that Allah rebukes human arrogance by pointing to man's material origin from a single "despised thing" (*al-shayʾ al-ḥaqīr*)—an ejaculated drop of fluid. Scientifically, a human being is not formed out of a single liquid secretion; embryogenesis requires two complex haploid cells—a spermatozoon and a maternal oocyte—with the ovum providing half the nuclear genome plus all mitochondrial DNA and cytoplasmic machinery. The verse echoes the rabbinic catechism of [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) alongside Talmudic ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)) and Greco-Roman seminal-drop models.
80:18.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18)–[80:19](https://quran.com/80/19), the rhetorical question *"From what thing did He create him?"* is answered exclusively with *"From a drop (*nuṭfah*)!"*—equating the material origin of the human organism with macroscopic ejaculated fluid in keeping with pre-microscopic Near Eastern embryology.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Following the rebuke in [Quran 80:17](https://quran.com/80/17) (*"May the human perish! How ungrateful he is!"*), [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18) poses a direct ontological question: *"From what did He create him?"* (`مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَهُ`, *min ayyi shayʾin khalaqahu*, literally "From which thing did He create him?"), which [Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80/19) answers: *"From a drop! He created him, and determined him"* (`min nuṭfatin khalaqahu fa-qaddarahu`). By asking *min ayyi shayʾin* ("from what thing/substance") and answering with the singular noun *nuṭfah* ("a trickling drop of fluid," specifically ejaculated semen, cf. [Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37)), the text identifies a visible liquid emission as the sole physical thing out of which a human is constructed.

From the standpoint of modern reproductive and cellular biology, reducing the material origin of a human being to a liquid drop (*nuṭfah*) reflects pre-modern observational limitations:
- **Dual Cellular Gametes vs. a Single Liquid Drop:** A human being is not created from a droplet of seminal fluid. Rather, a new human organism begins as a diploid **zygote** formed by the syngamy of two distinct, microscopic cells: a paternal **spermatozoon** (`~50 µm`) and a maternal **secondary oocyte** (`~100–120 µm`).
- **Indispensable Maternal Oocyte Contribution:** Far from being formed out of an ejaculated drop, the zygote derives the vast majority of its cellular volume, 100% of its **mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)**, its cytoplasmic organelles, and the maternal mRNA transcripts and proteins that drive early embryonic cleavage directly from the **maternal ovum**—a cellular structure unknown in the 7th century.
- **Acellular Seminal Liquid Is Discarded:** The macroscopic liquid drop (*nuṭfah*) visible to the naked eye is over 98% seminal plasma (water, fructose, citrate, and proteins), which never enters the fallopian tube and contributes zero material to the developing embryo.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* confirm that [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18) points specifically to the lowly, visible drop of ejaculated seminal fluid as the substance from which man is fashioned:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80:18/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains the rhetorical force of the question: *"He, whose mention is exalted, says: From what thing did He create the man who disbelieves in his Lord, such that he becomes arrogant and exalts himself above obeying his Lord and acknowledging His Oneness (`مِنْ أَيِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقَ الْإِنْسَانَ الْكَافِرَ رَبَّهُ حَتَّى يَتَكَبَّرَ وَيَتَعَظَّمَ`)."* In the following entry (**[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**), al-Ṭabarī states: *"Then He explained that from which He created him, and said: {From a drop! He created him, and determined him}, in states: a drop (`nuṭfah`) at one time, then a clinging clot (`ʿalaqah`) at another, then a lump of flesh (`muḍghah`), until his states came upon him while he was in his mother's womb."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80:18/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr states: *"Then Allah explains how He created him from something despised (`كَيْفَ خَلَقَهُ مِنَ الشَّيْءِ الْحَقِيرِ`) and that He is able to bring him back to life just as He created him initially. He says: {From what did He create him?}"*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6595](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6595), Muhammad describes the embryo in the uterus strictly through this macroscopic fluid-to-clot progression: *"At every womb Allah appoints an angel who says, 'O Lord! A drop of semen (`nuṭfah`)! O Lord! A clot (`ʿalaqah`)! O Lord! A little lump of flesh (`muḍghah`)!'"* Similarly, [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1438k](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1438k) identifies the reproductive material as ejaculated liquid (*al-māʾ*).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The exact rhetorical question-and-answer sequence of [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18)–[80:22](https://quran.com/80/22)—asking what substance man comes from, answering "from a drop," and linking it to the grave and final resurrection—was a well-known homiletical formula in Late Antique rabbinic literature and Greco-Roman embryology:

- **Rabbinic Wisdom in Mishnah [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) (c. AD 200):** In one of the most widely recited maxims of the Mishnah, Aqabiah ben Mahalalel rebukes human pride using the identical three-part sequence (origin from a drop, burial in the earth, and resurrection for judgment) found in [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18)–[80:22](https://quran.com/80/22):
  * *Question & Answer on Origin:* *"From where do you come? From a putrid drop"* (`מֵאַיִן בָּאתָ, מִטִּפָּה סְרוּחָה`, *me-ayin bata? mi-tippah seruchah*)—directly paralleling [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18)–[80:19](https://quran.com/80/19) (*"From what did He create him? From a drop!"*).
  * *Burial in the Earth:* *"Where are you going? To a place of dust, of worm and of maggot"*—paralleling [Quran 80:21](https://quran.com/80/21) (*"Then He causes him to die and buries him"*).
  * *Resurrection & Judgment:* *"Before whom are you destined to give an account and reckoning? Before the King of the kings of kings"*—paralleling [Quran 80:22](https://quran.com/80/22) (*"Then, when He wills, He raises him up"*).
- **Babylonian Talmud ([*Niddah* 30b–31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b), [*Yevamot* 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.69b)) & Greco-Roman Embryology (Aristotle & Galen):** Tractate [*Yevamot* 69b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.69b) characterizes the early conceptus for the first forty days as *"mere water"* (`maya b'alma`) before it solidifies inside the womb ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)–[31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)), while **Aristotle** (*De Generatione Animalium* I.19–20, II.4) and **Galen** (*De Semine* I.5–8) similarly identified macroscopic ejaculated seminal fluid (*gonē* / *sperma*) as the initial liquid stage from which the embryo is fashioned.

80:19.title: Creation from a Seminal Drop (Nuṭfah) & Post-Implantation Determination of Sex (Fa-Qaddarahu)
80:19.summary: [Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80/19) declares, "From a drop (*min nuṭfatin*)! He created him, and determined him (*fa-qaddarahu*)." Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6595](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6595)) explain *fa-qaddarahu* as both the embryo's sequential transformation from a liquid drop into a blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) and lump of flesh (*muḍghah*), and the angelic decree (*taqdīr*) of the fetus's sex (male or female), limbs, and lifespan after 40 to 42 nights in the womb. In modern genetics and embryology, chromosomal sex (`XX` or `XY`) and genetic traits are fixed at fertilization (`Day 0`), and the conceptus never passes through a blood-clot phase. This account echoes Galenic stage models and Talmudic traditions of angelic womb decrees ([*Niddah* 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.16b)).
80:19.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80/19), human embryogenesis is portrayed as beginning from a macroscopic seminal drop (*nuṭfah*) that is subsequently "proportioned and determined" (*fa-qaddarahu*) through clot-to-flesh stages and post-40-day sex determination—contradicting chromosomal genetics and cellular developmental biology.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Answering the question posed in [Quran 80:18](https://quran.com/80/18) (*"From what did He create him?"*), [Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80/19) states: *"From a drop! He created him, and determined him"* (`مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ`, *min nuṭfatin khalaqahu fa-qaddarahu*). In classical Arabic, *nuṭfah* (`نُطْفَة`) denotes a macroscopic droplet of trickling liquid—specifically ejaculated semen—while the verb *qaddara* (`قَدَّرَ`, Form II of *q-d-r*) signifies both "to proportion/fashion in measured stages" and "to decree/determine (*taqdīr*) one's attributes and destiny." Notice the sequential conjunction `fa-` ("and then"): first the conceptus is created as a *nuṭfah* (*khalaqahu*), and *then* it is proportioned and determined (*fa-qaddarahu*).

Both dimensions of *min nuṭfatin khalaqahu fa-qaddarahu* documented in classical Islamic sources conflict with modern reproductive science:
- **Chromosomal Sex & Genetic Traits Are Determined at Fertilization (`Day 0`), Not After 40+ Days:** In canonical Islamic tradition, the *taqdīr* (*fa-qaddarahu*) of the embryo—including whether the fetus will be **male or female** (*a-dhakarun am unthā*) and whether its limbs will be sound or imperfect—takes place only *after* the *nuṭfah* has remained in the womb for `40 to 42 nights` (or after the *muḍghah* stage), when an angel asks Allah what sex to make the embryo. Biologically, genetic sex (`46,XX` female vs. `46,XY` male) and the complete diploid genome are determined at the **exact moment of fertilization** (`Day 0`) in the fallopian tube when an X- or Y-bearing spermatozoon fuses with the maternal oocyte.
- **No Fluid-Drop-to-Blood-Clot Progression:** As al-Ṭabarī explains under [Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80/19), *fa-qaddarahu* also refers to fashioning the conceptus across sequential states: a liquid drop (*nuṭfah*), then a congealed blood clot (*ʿalaqah*), then a chewed lump of flesh (*muḍghah*). In reality, a living human embryo is a dividing cellular structure (zygote $\rightarrow$ morula $\rightarrow$ blastocyst $\rightarrow$ trilaminar embryonic disc) and never exists as a pooled seminal droplet or a coagulated blood clot.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Foundational *tafsīr* works and *ṣaḥīḥ* *ḥadīth* collections explicitly unite both meanings of *fa-qaddarahu*—the clot-to-flesh stages and the post-40-day angelic determination of fetal sex and destiny:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains *min nuṭfatin khalaqahu fa-qaddarahu* as sequential physical stages inside the uterus: *"Then He, majestic is His praise, explained that from which He created him, and said: {From a drop! He created him, and determined him}, in states (`aḥwālan`): a drop (`nuṭfah`) at one time, then a clinging clot (`ʿalaqah`) at another, then a lump of flesh (`muḍghah`), until his states came upon him while he was in his mother's womb (`أَحْوَالًا نُطْفَةً تَارَةً ثُمَّ عَلَقَةً أُخْرَى ثُمَّ مُضْغَةً إِلَى أَنْ أَتَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَحْوَالُهُ وَهُوَ فِي رَحِمِ أُمِّهِ`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr glosses *fa-qaddarahu* through the canonical *qadar* (predestination) traditions: *"{From a drop! He created him, and determined him} meaning, He decreed his life span, his sustenance, his deeds, and whether he would be miserable or happy (`أَيْ قَدَّرَ أَجَلَهُ وَرِزْقَهُ وَعَمَلَهُ وَشَقِيٌّ أَوْ سَعِيدٌ`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Post-40-Day Sex & Limb Determination:** The mechanism of this intrauterine *taqdīr* is detailed in [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a), where Muhammad states: *"When forty-two nights pass after the semen (`nuṭfah`) gets into the womb, Allah sends the angel and gives him shape (`fa-ṣawwarahu`). Then he creates his sense of hearing, sense of sight, his skin, his flesh, his bones, and then says: 'My Lord, would he be male or female (`أَذَكَرٌ أَمْ أُنْثَى`)?' And your Lord decides (`fa-yaqḍī`) as He desires, and the angel writes it down."* Similarly, [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2644](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2644), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318), and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6595](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6595) state that only after the *nuṭfah*, *ʿalaqah*, and *muḍghah* stages does the angel ask: *"O Lord! Will it be a male or a female, wretched or blessed, and what will its livelihood and lifespan be?"*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the belief that embryonic sex remains undetermined until day 40 and the tradition of an angel of the womb petitioning God to decree the embryo's traits are attested in pre-Islamic rabbinic and Greco-Roman medical sources:

- **Rabbinic Literature ([*Niddah* 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.16b), [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a), [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) & [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3)):** In Babylonian Talmud [*Niddah* 16b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.16b) (c. AD 500), Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa teaches that the angel appointed over conception (named *Lailah*) takes the seminal drop (`tippah`), sets it before God, and asks: *"Master of the Universe, what shall become of this drop (`טִפָּה זוֹ מָה תְּהֵא עָלֶיהָ`)? Shall it be strong or weak, wise or foolish, rich or poor?"* Furthermore, [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a) and [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) teach that for the first **forty days** of gestation, the embryo's sex is not yet fixed, so a father may pray during days `3 to 40` that the fetus be formed as a male or a female.
- **Greco-Roman Medicine (Hippocrates, Aristotle & Galen):** **Hippocrates** (*On the Nature of the Child* §18), **Aristotle** (*History of Animals* VII.3, 583b), and **Galen** (*De Semine* I.7–8) taught that the conceptus begins as unformed seminal fluid (*gonē*), coagulates into a bloody mass (*haimatoeides*), and turns into flesh (*sarx*), acquiring sexual differentiation only around the 30th to 42nd day—matching the 40-to-42-night *taqdīr* timetable in [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a) and [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 80:19](https://quran.com/80:19/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari).

76:2.title: Mingled Male and Female Seminal Fluids & the Ancient Two-Seed Theory (Nuṭfah Amshāj)
76:2.summary: [Quran 76:2](https://quran.com/76/2) states that humans are created from a "mingled drop" (*nuṭfah amshāj*), which classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/76:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/76:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a)) define as the macroscopic mixing of thick white male semen with a thin yellow female "seminal fluid" (*māʾ al-marʾah*) said to determine the child's sex, resemblance, and flesh vs. bone tissues. In human reproductive biology, women do not ejaculate an ovum in a liquid secretion; fertilization is the cellular fusion of a single sperm with a microscopic oocyte in the fallopian tube, and paternal chromosomes alone determine fetal sex. This description reflects the pre-Islamic Greco-Roman and Talmudic "two-seed" (*dual-seminal*) misconception documented in Hippocrates, Galen, and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)).
76:2.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 76:2](https://quran.com/76/2), human conception is attributed to the physical mixing of emitted male and female reproductive fluids, reflecting the pre-modern Mediterranean "two-seed" model of embryology rather than cellular fertilization.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 76:2](https://quran.com/76/2) declares: *"Surely We created the human from a drop, a mixture (min nuṭfatin amshājin)—We test him—and We made him hearing and seeing."* In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *nuṭfah* (`نُطْفَة`) denotes a macroscopic droplet of trickling liquid—specifically ejaculated semen, as confirmed in [Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37) (*"a drop of emitted semen,"* `nuṭfatan min maniyyin yumnā`) and [Quran 53:46](https://quran.com/53/46)—while *amshāj* (`أَمْشَاج`, plural of *mashīj*) denotes mixed liquids or blended bodily secretions (*akhlāṭ*).

Scientifically, mammalian conception does not occur through the macroscopic mingling or coagulation of bulk male and female ejaculated fluids in the uterus:
- **No Female Seminal Emission:** Women do not emit or ejaculate a reproductive seed (*māʾ* / *maniyy*) during intercourse; vaginal lubrication (Bartholin and transudative fluids) contains **zero ova**.
- **Cellular Gamete Fusion:** Fertilization takes place in the ampulla of the fallopian tube when a single microscopic spermatozoon (`~50 µm`) penetrates a non-motile secondary oocyte (`~100–120 µm`) released from the ovary at ovulation, while seminal plasma is filtered out at the cervix.
- **Equal Diploid Genetics & Chromosomal Sex Determination:** Both parents contribute 23 chromosomes equally to every somatic tissue in the body (rather than male fluid forming bones and female fluid forming flesh), and fetal biological sex is determined strictly by whether the fertilizing sperm carries an X or Y chromosome—never by which parent's fluid "prevails" or arrives first.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Foundational Islamic commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* collections unanimously corroborate that *nuṭfah amshāj* refers literally to the physical mixing of male and female sexual fluids:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 76:2](https://quran.com/76:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī opens his exegesis by defining the verse directly: *"We have created the offspring of Adam from a drop (nuṭfah), meaning: from the fluid of the male and the fluid of the female (`min māʾi al-rajuli wa-māʾi al-marʾah`). And His statement {a mixture (amshāj)} means: mixtures (`akhlāṭ`)."* Citing multiple transmission chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **ʿIkrimah**, **Mujāhid**, **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī**, and **al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas**, al-Ṭabarī concludes that the mingling of male and female fluids is the sole grammatically sound meaning because Allah describes the liquid *nuṭfah* itself as a mixture before it becomes a clot (*ʿalaqah*).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 76:2](https://quran.com/76:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr quotes Ibn ʿAbbās: *"This means the fluid of the man and the fluid of the woman when they meet and mix (`idhā ijtamaʿā wa-ikhtalaṭā`),"* adding that ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, and al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas all stated: *"Amshāj is the mixing of the man's fluid with the woman's fluid."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Fluid Dominance and Tissue Division:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 315a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:315a), Muhammad states: *"The water of the man is white and the water of the woman is yellow. When they meet (`fa-idhā ijtamaʿā`), and the semen of the man (`maniyyu al-rajuli`) prevails over the semen of the woman (`maniyya al-marʾati`), they produce a male child by Allah's permission; and when the semen of the woman prevails over the semen of the man, they produce a female child."* Similarly, [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 311](https://sunnah.com/muslim:311) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3329](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3329) attribute a child's physical resemblance to whichever parent's fluid *"rises above or precedes"* (*ʿalā aw sabaqa*), while classical exegetes (al-Qurṭubī, al-Baghawī, and *Musnad Aḥmad* 4206) record that the man's thick white fluid forms the bones and sinews whereas the woman's thin yellow fluid forms the flesh and blood.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Every feature of this two-fluid reproductive model was an established medical and religious misconception across the ancient Mediterranean and Near East centuries before Islam:

- **Greco-Roman Medicine (Hippocrates & Galen):** The Hippocratic treatise *On Generation* (*De Genitura* §§4–8, c. 420 BC) formulated the "two-seed theory" (*semen duplex*), asserting that both men and women emit reproductive fluid (*gonē*) into the womb where the two seeds mix (*symmignyetai*), and that whichever parent's seed is stronger or greater in quantity determines the fetus's sex and physical resemblance. **Galen of Pergamon** (*On Semen* / *De Semine* I.5–8, II.1–4, 2nd century AD)—whose medical curriculum was translated into Syriac by Sergius of Reshaina (d. AD 536) and taught at Gundeshapur—similarly taught that thinner female semen mixes with thicker male semen, with male seed forming the white "spermatic" tissues (bones, nerves, sinews) and maternal blood forming the red fleshy organs.
- **Rabbinic Literature ([Babylonian Talmud, *Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) & [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3)):** Tractate [*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) (c. AD 500) preserves the exact same anatomical tissue division: *"His father seeds the white substance, from which are formed the bones, sinews, nails, the brain in his head, and the white of the eye; his mother seeds the red substance, from which are formed his skin, flesh, hair, blood, and the dark of the eye,"* while also teaching that fetal sex depends on which parent emits seed first. Likewise, [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) pairs human origin from a *"putrid drop"* (`טִפָּה סְרוּחָה`) with moral accountability before God, and **Aristotle** (*Generation of Animals* I.19–20, 727a–729a) similarly modeled conception as male seminal fluid coagulating maternal blood in the womb like rennet curdling milk.

96:2.title: Human Creation from a Congealed Blood Clot (ʿAlaq) & Ancient Menstrual Coagulation
96:2.summary: [Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96/2) declares that God formed humanity out of a clot (*min ʿalaq*). Across classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*, *Lisān al-ʿArab*), classical exegesis ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/96:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/96:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)), and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)), *ʿalaq* (plural of *ʿalaqah*) is defined as thick, congealed red blood (*al-dam al-jāmid*) lasting from Day 40 to Day 80 of gestation. In developmental biology, a living human embryo never passes through a clotted-blood stage; embryonic blood circulates continuously inside vessels from Day 21 onward, while by Days 40–80 the conceptus is already a fetus with limbs and organs. Rather than anticipating microscopy, the verse reflects the Greco-Roman (Aristotle, Hippocrates, Galen) and Talmudic ([*Niddah* 30b–31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)) misconception that semen coagulates maternal blood into a clot.
96:2.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96/2), human embryonic development is said to begin from *ʿalaq* (congealed, clotted blood)—preserving the standard pre-Islamic Mediterranean and Near Eastern medical misconception that the embryo forms when seminal fluid coagulates maternal menstrual blood.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

In Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, [Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96/2) states: *"creates the human from a clot"* (`خَلَقَ الْإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ`, *khalaqa al-insāna min ʿalaq*). In classical Arabic lexicography—al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn* (*"qiṭʿat dam jāmidah,"* a piece of thick, congealed blood), Ibn Fāris's *Maqāyīs al-Lughah* (`والعَلَقُ: الدَّمُ الجامِد، والقطعة منه عَلَقَة`), al-Jawharī's *al-Ṣiḥāḥ*, and Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*—when the collective noun *ʿalaq* (or its unit noun *ʿalaqah*) is used in human generation, it denotes **exclusively** thick, moist, coagulated blood (*al-dam al-jāmid*).

Modern embryology establishes that human development never involves a blood-clot stage, and refutes late-20th-century concordist attempts (popularized by Maurice Bucaille and Keith L. Moore) to reinterpret *ʿalaq* as simultaneously meaning a "blood clot," a "clinging blastocyst," and an "aquatic leech":
- **No Congealed Blood-Clot Stage:** Living embryos never consist of clotted or stagnant blood. Embryonic hematopoiesis and vasculogenesis develop inside endothelial tubes, and the primitive tubular heart initiates peristaltic circulation by **Days 21–22**; intravascular blood clotting in vivo causes thrombosis and embryonic death.
- **Fallacy of Semantic Overload (*Illegitimate Totality Transfer*):** Because the triliteral root *ʿ-l-q* denotes adherence/sticking, Arabic derived distinct nouns from it: congealed blood (*ʿalaqah*, because wet clots stick to the hand) and an aquatic leech (*ʿalaqah*, because it clings to skin). Claiming that [Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96/2) simultaneously intends all dictionary derivatives of the root violates historical linguistics (analogous to claiming "bat" in an English sentence simultaneously means a flying mammal and a wooden club).
- **Chronological & Anatomical Contradiction:** An implanting blastocyst (Days 6–10) is a microscopic sphere (`0.1–0.2 mm`) invisible to the naked eye, containing zero blood and bearing no resemblance to a leech; a Day 24 somite embryo (`2–3 mm`) is already past implantation and never sucks maternal blood across the placental barrier; and during the canonical **Day 40 to Day 80** window assigned to *ʿalaqah* in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208), the conceptus is a `15–60 mm` fetus with fingers, toes, facial features, and ossifying bones.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

For over thirteen centuries, classical Quranic commentators and *ḥadīth* traditions unanimously defined *ʿalaq* in [Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96/2) as coagulated red blood, with zero mention of aquatic leeches or microscopic blastocysts:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96:2/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī provides the exact lexical and grammatical definition: *"Then He clarified that which He created, saying: {creates the human from a clot (`khalaqa al-insāna min ʿalaq`)}, meaning: from blood (`يَعْنِي مِنَ الدَّمِ`). And He said: 'from ʿalaq'; and what is intended by it is 'from an ʿalaqah' (a single clot), because He used the collective plural form, just as it is said: shajarah (a tree) and shajar (trees)... because 'the human' (`al-insān`) carries a collective plural meaning."* Likewise, in **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)** and **[Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75:38/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)**, al-Ṭabarī defines *ʿalaqah* as *"a piece of blood"* (`al-qiṭʿah min al-dam`).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 96:2](https://quran.com/96:2/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr states: *"{creates the human from a clot}: Drawing attention to the beginning of man's creation from a dangling clot (`التَّنْبِيهُ عَلَى خَلْقِ الْإِنْسَانِ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ`)."* Cross-referencing **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22:5/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)** and **[Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)**, Ibn Kathīr explains that after forty days as a drop, *"it turns into a red clot (`ʿalaqah ḥamrāʾ`) by the permission of Allah, and remains like that for forty days,"* quoting **ʿIkrimah**: *"This is blood (`wa-hiya dam`),"* and noting in 22:5 that women observe this clot with the naked eye during miscarriages (*kamā tushāhidūnahā*).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a), Muhammad specifies that the embryo stays in the womb *"for forty days as a seed (`nuṭfah`), then he becomes a clot of thick blood (`thumma yakūnu ʿalaqatan mithla dhālika`) for a like period (of forty days)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Because menstruation ceases during pregnancy (gestational amenorrhea) and early first-trimester miscarriages are expelled encased in dark red decidual blood clots, ancient Greco-Roman, Talmudic, and Persian writers deduced that the embryo begins as a coagulated clot of blood:

- **Greco-Roman Medical Theory (Aristotle, Hippocrates, Galen & Pliny):** In *On the Generation of Animals* (I.19–20, II.4, 739b, c. 350 BC), **Aristotle** taught that male semen acts like rennet upon milk, *"curdling the menstrual blood (`katamēnia`)"* into a solidifying clot (echoed by **Pliny the Elder**, *Natural History* VII.15.66). **Hippocrates** (*On the Nature of the Child* §§14–15, c. 420 BC) described maternal blood wrapping around the seed and congealing into a clot, and **Galen** (*De Semine* I.7–8, 2nd century AD)—whose works were taught at Alexandria and Gundeshapur—codified his second stage of embryogenesis as a blood-filled coagulum (*haimatoeides*) preceding unformed flesh (*sarx*).
- **Talmudic & Persian Parallels ([*Niddah* 30b–31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) & *Bundahishn*):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)), the mother contributes the *"red substance"* (maternal blood) that coagulates with the father's *"white substance"* to form flesh and blood within a 40-day embryonic framework ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b)). Similarly, Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 15.1–5) and pre-Islamic Arabian physicians trained in the Greco-Persian tradition (such as **al-Ḥārith ibn Kaladah**) held that the liquid drop (*nuṭfah*) congeals with uterine blood into a red clot (*ʿalaqah*).

51:49.category: All Organisms are Created in Pairs
51:49.title: Universal Binary Pairing vs. Asexual Life & Self-Conjugate Bosons (Quran 51:49)
51:49.summary: [Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49) asserts a universal rule of binary creation: "And of everything We have created two pairs (*wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn*), so that you might take heed." Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/51:49/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) explain that this encompasses male and female pairs across living creatures as well as cosmic polarities (sky and earth, night and day, faith and disbelief) intended to contrast creaturely duality with the singular Oneness of God. Scientifically, universal binary pairing fails in both biology and physics: bacteria, archaea, viruses, and obligate parthenogenetic animals (such as bdelloid rotifers and whiptail lizards) reproduce without male-female pairs, fungi like *Schizophyllum commune* have over 23,000 mating types, and fundamental bosons (photons, Z bosons, Higgs bosons) are their own antiparticles. Historically, this doctrine reproduces ancient Greek, Zoroastrian, and Talmudic (*Chagigah* 15a) polarity cosmologies.
51:49.explanation:
All Organisms are Created in Pairs. In [Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49), the sweeping claim that "of everything We created two pairs" (*wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayn*) reflects ancient Near Eastern binary cosmology and macroscopic observations of sexual dimorphism, conflicting with the empirical realities of asexual reproduction, multiallelic fungal mating systems, and self-conjugate quantum particles.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49) declares: *"And of everything We created two pairs, so that you might take heed"* (`wa-min kulli shayʾin khalaqnā zawjayni laʿallakum tadhakkarūn`; cf. [Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36)). In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *zawjayn* (`زَوْجَيْن`, dual of *zawj*) denotes two counterparts, two spouses (male and female, as in [Quran 53:45](https://quran.com/53/45): *al-zawjayni al-dhakara wa-l-unthā*), or two contrasting kinds (*nawʿayni mukhtalifayn*). Whether interpreted biologically (as universal male-female sexual dimorphism) or physically (as universal matter-antimatter pairing, as claimed by modern concordists), the universal quantifier *min kulli shayʾin* (*"of everything"*) conflicts with empirical science:

- **Asexual Prokaryotes, Viruses, & Unicellular Eukaryotes:** The vast majority of Earth's biosphere by both organism count and evolutionary history lacks male and female pairs entirely. **Bacteria** and **Archaea** reproduce asexually via binary fission (replicating a single chromosome and dividing into two identical daughter cells without gametes or sexes). **Viruses** replicate via host machinery without sexual dimorphism, and protists such as *Amoeba proteus* and *Euglena* reproduce via asexual mitosis.
- **Obligate Parthenogenetic Animals (100% Female Species):** Even among complex multicellular animals, numerous species reproduce exclusively via obligate parthenogenesis with zero males: **bdelloid rotifers** (over 450 species evolving for >40 million years without males), the **New Mexico whiptail lizard** (*Aspidoscelis neomexicanus*, an all-female triploid reptile), and the **Brahminy blind snake** (*Indotyphlops braminus*).
- **Fungi with Thousands of Sexes (Non-Binary Mating Systems):** Sexual reproduction itself is not universally binary (*zawjayn*). Basidiomycete fungi such as the split-gill mushroom (***Schizophyllum commune***) possess tetrapolar multiallelic mating systems yielding **over 23,000 distinct biological mating types (sexes)** rather than two.
- **Self-Conjugate Particles & Baryon Asymmetry in Physics:** Modern concordist attempts to rescue the verse via Paul Dirac's antimatter prediction fail under quantum field theory. Fundamental force-carrying gauge and scalar bosons with zero additive quantum numbers—including the **photon** ($\gamma$), the **neutral Z boson** ($Z^0$), the **Higgs boson** ($H^0$), and neutral pions ($\pi^0$)—are strictly **self-conjugate** (acting as their own antiparticles with no distinct antiparticle twin). Moreover, the observable universe exhibits extreme **baryon asymmetry** (~$10^9$ photons per baryon and virtually zero primordial antimatter) rather than equal pairs.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic commentators confirm that [Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49) was understood both as biological male-female pairing and as a theological contrast between created polar opposites and the unpaired Oneness (*tawḥīd*) of God:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51:49/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī records the two foundational interpretations of the early *Salaf*: (1) **Ibn Zayd** stated directly: *"A male and a female, those are the two pairs (`dhakaran wa-unthā, dhāka al-zawjān`),"* and (2) **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** and **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** stated that *zawjayn* means contrasting pairs across creation: *"Disbelief and faith, misery and happiness, guidance and misguidance, night and day, heaven and earth, mankind and jinn, and the sun and the moon."* Endorsing Mujāhid's view as the most comprehensive (*awlā al-qawlayn*), al-Ṭabarī explains that whereas natural things have a single fixed property (like fire that only heats and snow that only cools), God creates every thing alongside its opposite (*khalaqa li-kulli mā khalaqa min khalqihi thāniyan lahu mukhālifan fī maʿnāhu*) to prove His omnipotence.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51:49/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under *"All Created Things are in Pairs,"* Ibn Kathīr combines both readings: *"{And of everything We have created pairs} meaning: all created beings are pairs (`jamīʿu al-makhlūqāti azwāj`): heaven and earth, night and day, sun and moon, land and sea, light and darkness, faith and disbelief, death and life, misery and happiness, Paradise and Fire, in addition to the animals and plants. And for this reason He said: {that you may remember}, meaning, to know that the Creator, Allah, is One without partners."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The doctrine that all created things exist in binary pairs—both biologically and as cosmic polarities demonstrating the singularity of the Creator—was a widespread motif in Greek, Iranian, and Near Eastern thought centuries before Islam:

- **Greek Polarity Philosophy (Pythagoras, Heraclitus, & Aristotle):** In *Metaphysics* I.5 (986a22), **Aristotle** records the **Pythagorean Table of Opposites** (*Systoichia*, 6th–5th century BC), which organized reality into binary pairs including male and female, light and darkness, and good and evil. **Heraclitus** (Fragments B67, B88) taught that all things exist as interdependent opposites (day and night, winter and summer, life and death), while **Aristotle** (*Generation of Animals* I–II) and **Theophrastus** (*Historia Plantarum*) generalized male-female dimorphism across animals and date palms prior to the discovery of microscopic asexual life.
- **Philo of Alexandria, Zoroastrianism, & Talmudic Polarity ([*Chagigah* 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.15a)):** **Philo of Alexandria** (*Quis Rerum Divinarum Heres* §§207–214, 1st century AD) cataloged cosmic pairs (heaven and earth, night and day, light and darkness, life and death, male and female), arguing that God divided all creation into binary pairs so that humanity would recognize that God alone is Unpaired and One (*to Hen*). Similarly, Sasanian Zoroastrianism (*Greater Bundahishn* 1) and the Talmud ([*Chagigah* 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.15a)) teach that everything in creation was fashioned with its counterpart—righteous and wicked, Paradise and Gehenna, light and darkness, fire and water, and mountains and hills.

36:36.category: All Organisms are Created in Pairs
36:36.title: Universal Botanical and Biological Pairing (al-Azwāja Kullahā Mimmā Tunbitu al-Arḍ)
36:36.summary: [Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36) declares that God created "all the pairs" (*al-azwāja kullahā*) across everything that the earth grows (plants), humans themselves, and unknown creatures. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/36:36/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/36:36/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* on date-palm pollination ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2361](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2361)) confirm that early Muslims understood this as a universal male-female division across flora and living beings. Scientifically, only about 6% of flowering plant species are dioecious (separate male and female plants), while ~90% bear bisexual flowers, many plants reproduce asexually via apomixis, and entire domains of microorganisms (bacteria, archaea) and parthenogenetic animals reproduce without sexual pairing. This echoes pre-Islamic Greco-Roman overgeneralizations from dioecious date palms (Pliny the Elder) and rabbinic teachings ([*Bava Batra* 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.74b)).
36:36.explanation:
All Organisms are Created in Pairs. In [Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36), the Quran asserts a universal binary pairing across all terrestrial plant life, humanity, and unknown creatures, overgeneralizing the dioecious reproductive biology of the Arabian date palm to the entire biosphere.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36) states: *"Glory to the One who created pairs of all that the earth grows (`khalaqa al-azwāja kullahā mimmā tunbitu al-arḍu`), and of themselves (`wa-min anfusihim`), and of what they do not know (`wa-mimmā lā yaʿlamūna`)."* By juxtaposing *mimmā tunbitu al-arḍu* ("that which the earth grows," i.e., vegetation) with *wa-min anfusihim* ("and of themselves," where *azwāj* denotes male and female reproductive partners, cf. [Quran 75:39](https://quran.com/75/39) and [Quran 53:45](https://quran.com/53/45)) and reinforcing the claim with *kullahā* ("all of them"), the verse—alongside [Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49) and [Quran 13:3](https://quran.com/13/3)—posits that all plant species and unseen organisms exist in complementary pairs.

Modern botany and evolutionary biology show that neither plant life nor previously unknown organisms conform to a universal paired or male-female model:
- **Botanical Reproduction (`mimmā tunbitu al-arḍu`):** Unlike the dioecious date palm (*Phoenix dactylifera*), which has distinct male and female trees, **only ~6% of angiosperm (flowering plant) species are dioecious**. Roughly **90% of flowering plants are hermaphroditic (monoclinous)**, possessing both male stamens and female carpels within the same flower, while ~4–5% are monoecious. Moreover, hundreds of plant taxa—including dandelions (*Taraxacum*), hawkweeds (*Hieracium*), and blackberries (*Rubus*)—reproduce by **apomixis** (producing clonal seeds without meiosis or fertilization) or vegetative propagation.
- **Asexual Microorganisms & Parthenogenetic Fauna (`wa-mimmā lā yaʿlamūna`):** The vast realm of organisms unknown to seventh-century Arabia—prokaryotes (**Bacteria** and **Archaea**), unicellular protists (*Amoeba*), and imperfect fungi—reproduces **exclusively asexually** via binary fission, budding, or mitotic spores, possessing neither male nor female sexes. Even among multicellular animals, entire lineages—such as **bdelloid rotifers** (which have diversified for over 40 million years without males or meiosis) and obligate **parthenogenetic vertebrates** like the New Mexico whiptail lizard (*Aspidoscelis neomexicanus*) and the Brahminy blind snake (*Indotyphlops braminus*)—consist solely of all-female populations that procreate without mates.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* confirm that *azwāj* in [Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36) was understood literally in terms of male-female sexual differentiation and categorical counterparts:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36:36/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains the verse as praising *"the One who created all the different kinds from the plants of the earth (`khalaqa al-alwāna al-mukhtalifata kullahā min nabāti al-arḍi`); and {of themselves}, He says: and He created from their offspring males and females (`wa-khalaqa min awlādihim dhukūran wa-ināthan`); and {of what they do not know} as well, from the things of which He has not informed them, He likewise created pairs (`khalaqa kadhālika azwājan`)."* Al-Ṭabarī defines the human *azwāj* as biological males and females (`dhukūran wa-ināthan`) and applies *kadhālika* ("likewise") to unknown creatures.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36:36/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr comments on `{all the pairs of that which the earth produces}`: *"meaning, of crops and fruits and plants (`min zurūʿin wa-thimārin wa-nabātin`). {as well as of their own (human) kind} means, He made them into male and female (`fa-jaʿalahum dhakaran wa-unthā`). {and of that which they know not} means, different kinds of creatures of which they know nothing,"* equating this with [Quran 51:49](https://quran.com/51/49).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Male and Female Date Palms:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2361](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2361) (cf. [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2362](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2362)–[Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2363](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2363)), Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah reports that Muhammad passed by people in Medina tending date palms and asked what they were doing; they replied: *"They are pollinating (`yuʾabbirūnahu`), i.e., they place the male into the female (`yajʿalūna al-dhakara fī al-unthā`)."* Because the staple crop of the Hijaz visibly required pollen from a separate male tree to fertilize a female tree, seventh-century observers assumed all terrestrial flora existed as pairs.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that all plants and creatures are divided into male and female pairs was a pre-Islamic misconception rooted in Near Eastern date-palm agriculture, Greco-Roman natural philosophy, and Talmudic lore:

- **Greco-Roman Overgeneralization from Date Palms (Herodotus, Theophrastus, & Pliny the Elder):** **Herodotus** (*Histories* 1.193, 5th century BC) and **Theophrastus** (*Historia Plantarum* 2.8.4) described Mesopotamian farmers tying the spadix of "male palms" to "female date-bearing palms." Generalizing from this practice to the entire plant kingdom, **Pliny the Elder** (*Natural History* 13.7.31–35, 1st century AD) wrote that naturalists held that *"not only beasts, but all trees and indeed everything that the earth grows (`terra gignat`), even herbs, belong to both sexes (`utriusque sexus`),"* citing date palms as primary proof—an exact counterpart to [Quran 36:36](https://quran.com/36/36)'s *"pairs of all that the earth grows."* Similarly, the Peripatetic treatise *De Plantis* (I.2, 817a, attributed to Aristotle/Nicolaus of Damascus) recorded **Empedocles'** doctrine of male and female sexes across plants.
- **Mesopotamian Botanical Lexicons & Talmudic Universal Pairing ([*Bava Batra* 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.74b) & [*Pesachim* 118a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.118a)):** In Babylonian cuneiform lexical lists (*Urra=hubullu* Tablet III), the date palm (*giš.gišimmar*) and other flora were classified into male (*zikaru*) and female (*sinništu*) counterparts. In the Babylonian Talmud, [*Bava Batra* 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.74b) (and [*Pesachim* 118a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.118a)) similarly declares as a universal rule: *"Everything that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created in His world, He created male and female (`zākār u-neqēvāh`)."*

23:14.title: Sequential Blood-Clot Stage & Bones Formed Before Flesh (Quran 23:14)
23:14.summary: [Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23/14) depicts the human embryo transforming sequentially from a seminal drop (*nuṭfah*) into a congealed blood clot (*ʿalaqah*), then a chewed lump (*muḍghah*), and then rigid bones (*ʿiẓām*) that are subsequently clothed with muscular flesh (*laḥm*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)) affirm that these stages represent literal 40-day transformations culminating in a bare skeletal frame covered with meat before ensoulment at 120 days. In developmental biology, embryos never pass through a coagulated blood stage, organogenesis completes by day 56, and muscle precursors differentiate alongside soft cartilage templates prior to bone ossification. Rather than revealing modern histology, the verse reproduces the four-stage embryological sequence taught in Greco-Roman medicine (Hippocrates, Aristotle, and Galen) and Talmudic embryology (*Niddah* 30b–31a).
23:14.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23/14), embryonic development is described as a linear sequence in which a drop of semen coagulates into a blood clot, solidifies into a lump, forms a naked skeletal framework of bones, and is only then wrapped with flesh—inverting the histological sequence of musculoskeletal development and mirroring 2nd-century AD Galenic medicine.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Following the mention of a seminal drop (*nuṭfah*) placed in the womb ([Quran 23:13](https://quran.com/23/13)), [Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23/14) states: *"Then We made the drop into a clot (ʿalaqah), then We made the clot into a lump (muḍghah), then We made the lump into bones (ʿiẓāman), then We clothed the bones with flesh (fa-kasawnā al-ʿiẓāma laḥman), then We produced him as another creature."* In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *ʿalaqah* (`عَلَقَة`) denotes congealed blood (*dam jāmid*); *muḍghah* (`مُضْغَة`) denotes a bite-sized morsel of meat (*qiṭʿat laḥm qadr mā yumḍagh*); and the conjunction *fa-* (`فَـ`) in *fa-khalaqnā al-muḍghata ʿiẓāman fa-kasawnā al-ʿiẓāma laḥman* signifies immediate sequential order (*al-tartīb wa-l-taʿqīb*), asserting that the lump first becomes mineralized bones (`عِظَام`, distinct from cartilage, *ghuḍrūf*) and is subsequently dressed with muscle.

Empirical human embryology (Carnegie Stages) contradicts this progression on three levels:
- **No Congealed Blood-Clot (*ʿAlaqah*) Stage:** After fertilization in the fallopian tube, the zygote implants as a blastocyst (days 7–12) and gastrulates into a trilaminar embryonic disc (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm). Primitive blood cells circulate within closed vessels by day 21; the conceptus is never a static clot of coagulated blood.
- **Simultaneous Mesodermal Differentiation & Myogenesis Preceding Ossification:** Bones never form as an isolated frame later clothed with flesh. During week 5 (Carnegie Stages 13–15), somites differentiate concurrently into sclerotome and dermomyotome (myoblasts), while limb-bud mesenchyme condenses into soft, unossified **hyaline cartilage templates** simultaneously as migrating myoblasts form muscle masses around them. During weeks 6–7, myoblasts fuse into functional muscle fibers (*myotubes*) around these cartilage models *before* primary endochondral ossification into true bone (*ʿiẓām*) begins in the long-bone shafts at week 8 (Carnegie Stage 23).
- **56-Day Organogenesis vs. 120-Day Timeline:** Human organogenesis concludes by day 56 (week 8), when all major organs, digits, and facial features are present, contradicting the 120-day pre-fetal timeline assigned in canonical Islamic tradition.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* confirm that early Muslim authorities understood [Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23/14) as literal macroscopic transformations across three 40-day intervals:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī cites the reading of **ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd**: *"then We made the lump a bone and nerves, so We clothed it with flesh"* (`thumma khalaqnā al-muḍghata ʿaẓman wa-ʿaṣaban fa-kasawnāhu laḥman`), confirming the lump became a skeletal core prior to receiving muscular covering. Al-Ṭabarī cites **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **ʿIkrimah**, **Mujāhid**, **al-Shaʿbī**, and **al-Ḍaḥḥāk** stating that *"another creature"* means breathing the soul (*nafkh al-rūḥ*) into the body after its bones and flesh are completed.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 23:14](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr defines *ʿalaqah* as *"a red clot, like an elongated clot; ʿIkrimah said: 'This is blood,'"* and *muḍghah* as *"a piece of flesh with no shape or features."* For *"then We made out of that little lump of flesh bones,"* he writes: *"meaning, We gave it shape, with a head, two arms and two legs, with its bones, nerves and veins. Ibn ʿAbbās said: 'This refers to the bone of the spine,'"* citing [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4935](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4935) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2955a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2955a) on the tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*—whereas the coccyx is the last vertebral segment to ossify). For *"then We clothed the bones with flesh,"* he writes: *"We gave it something to cover it, bind it, and strengthen it."*
- **The Canonical 120-Day *Ḥadīth*:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a), Muhammad states creation is gathered in the womb *"for forty days as a nuṭfah, then a clot (ʿalaqah) for a similar period [40 days], then a little lump of flesh (muḍghah) for a similar length of time [40 days]"* before ensoulment. In [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/23:14/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), Ibn Masʿūd states the *nuṭfah* alone remains *"for forty days, then descends in the womb and becomes a clot,"* and **ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib** confirms ensoulment occurs at *"four months [120 days]."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the four-stage progression and bones forming before flesh were standard doctrines in Greco-Roman medicine and Talmudic lore:

- **Galen's Four-Stage Embryology:** In *De Semine* I.8–10 (c. AD 170; cf. [Galen, *On the Natural Faculties* II.3](http://classics.mit.edu/Galen/natfac.2.two.html)), **Galen** divided embryogenesis into four exact stages: (1) seminal fluid (*gonē* = *nuṭfah*), (2) a blood-filled coagulum (*ʿalaqah*), (3) an unarticulated flesh-like mass (*sarx* = *muḍghah*), and (4) hardening of bones followed by wrapping muscle around them (*De Usu Partium* XI.18, likening the skeleton to a ship's keel clothed externally with flesh).
- **Hippocratic, Aristotelian, & Talmudic Parallels ([*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) & [*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a)):** The Hippocratic *On the Nature of the Child* (§§12–18) taught that coagulated seed and blood thicken into flesh before bones condense like branches and are covered by muscle, while **Aristotle** ([*History of Animals* VII.3](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/history_anim.7.vii.html)) modeled conception as semen curdling uterine blood across a 40-day threshold. In the Talmud, [*Niddah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.25a) describes the unarticulated embryo lacking shaped limbs, [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) assigns 40 days to initial formation, and [*Niddah* 31a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.31a) divides bones and sinews (from paternal white seed) from external skin and flesh (from maternal red seed).

16:66.title: Milk Originating in the Belly Between Stomach Dung and Blood (Quran 16:66)
16:66.summary: [Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16/66) claims that cattle milk is provided "from what is in their bellies—from between excretions and blood—pure milk" (*min bayni farthin wa-damin*). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/16:66/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/16:66/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) confirm that early Muslims understood this literally: digested fodder inside the stomach cavity (*al-karish* / *al-maʿidah*) separates into dung (*farth*), blood (*dam*), and milk (*laban*), which then flows to the udder unmixed. In mammalian anatomy, milk is never present inside the abdominal cavity or between intestinal waste and blood; it is synthesized *de novo* by exocrine mammary glands located outside the peritoneal wall, and raw livestock milk frequently harbors zoonotic pathogens.
