The verse reflects pastoral slaughter observations, Talmudic physiology ([*Bekhorot* 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.6b)), and Greco-Roman medical theories (Aristotle and Galen) that milk is blood concocted inside the body.
16:66.explanation:
Source and Purity of Milk. In [Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16/66), mammalian milk is described as originating inside the abdominal cavity (*fī buṭūnihi*) from a spatial position "between stomach-dung and blood" (*min bayni farthin wa-damin*), reflecting pre-modern slaughterhouse observations and ancient humoral physiology rather than external mammary gland biosynthesis.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16/66) (paralleled in [Quran 23:21](https://quran.com/23/21)) declares: *"And surely in the cattle is a lesson indeed for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies—between excretions and blood—pure milk, pleasant tasting to the drinkers"* (`nusqīkum mimmā fī buṭūnihi min bayni farthin wa-damin labanan khāliṣan sāʾighan li-l-shāribīn`). In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *al-Ṣiḥāḥ*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *buṭūn* (`بُطُون`, plural of *baṭn*) denotes the internal abdominal cavity; *farth* (`فَرْث`) specifically denotes semi-digested dung while it remains inside the rumen or stomach (*al-sirqīn mā dāma fī al-karish*, called *rawth* only after excretion); and *min bayni* (`مِنْ بَيْنِ`) denotes spatial extraction from between two adjacent substances. Notably, just three verses later, [Quran 16:69](https://quran.com/16/69) uses the identical anatomical construct for bees regurgitating honey *"from their bellies"* (`min buṭūnihā`).

This account conflicts with mammalian anatomy, biochemistry, and microbiology:
- **Mammary Glands Are External to the Abdominal Cavity (*Baṭn*):** Milk is never produced, stored, or located inside the belly (*baṭn*) or peritoneal cavity, nor does it lie spatially between the rumen/intestines and blood vessels. Ruminant udders are cutaneous exocrine glands derived from the ectoderm and suspended in the superficial inguinal fascia completely *outside* the muscular abdominal wall, tunica flava, and peritoneum.
- ***De Novo* Glandular Biosynthesis vs. Internal Separation:** Milk does not exist inside the abdomen waiting to be filtered from between digestive waste and blood. Instead, alveolar epithelial cells (**lactocytes**) inside the external udder synthesize lactose (via lactose synthase in the Golgi apparatus), casein proteins, and milk lipids *de novo* from dissolved molecular precursors (glucose, amino acids, and volatile fatty acids) delivered by arterial capillaries—the same circulatory pathway that supplies saliva, tears, and sweat.
- **Microbiological Impurity of Raw Milk:** Contrary to the unconditional characterization of raw livestock milk as *khāliṣan* ("pure / uncontaminated"), unpasteurized cattle, goat, and camel milk is a primary vector for zoonotic bacteria—including *Brucella melitensis*, *Mycobacterium bovis*, *Listeria monocytogenes*, *Coxiella burnetii*, and *Salmonella*—shed directly from infected mammary alveoli or fecal contact.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegetes unanimously interpreted [Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16/66) as a literal separation of milk, blood, and dung inside the animal's stomach cavity:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16:66/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** After analyzing why the singular pronoun in *buṭūnihi* refers back to livestock (*al-naʿam*), al-Ṭabarī explains *"from between excretions and blood, pure milk"* in physical terms: *"He says: We give you to drink milk which We extract for you from between dung (*farth*) and blood (*dam*) in a pure state; He says: it is freed from the admixture of blood and dung (`khaluṣa min mukhālaṭati al-dami wa-l-farth`), so neither of them mixes with it."* Classical commentaries (al-Baghawī, al-Qurṭubī, and al-Suyūṭī on 16:66) record the foundational explanation of **Ibn ʿAbbās**: *"When the beast eats fodder and it settles in its rumen (*al-karish*), it cooks it: the bottom of it becomes dung (*farth*), the middle of it becomes milk (*laban*), and the top of it becomes blood (*dam*). The liver rules over these three and divides them, so blood flows into the veins, milk flows into the udder, and dung remains in the rumen."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 16:66](https://quran.com/16:66/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explicitly locates the separation of all four fluids—blood, milk, urine, and feces—inside the animal's stomach: *"His saying {between excretions and blood—pure milk} means: it is extracted in its whiteness, taste, and sweetness from between excretions and blood in the interior of the animal (`fī bāṭini al-ḥayawān`), so each flows to its destination. When the food is digested in its stomach (`idhā naḍija al-ghidhāʾu fī maʿidatihi`), blood is distributed from it to the veins, milk to the udder, urine to the bladder, and feces to the rectum, and none of them mixes with the other after being separated from it."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the pastoral wonder that white milk emerges from an animal filled with green rumen-dung and red blood, and the medical theory that milk is concocted inside the abdomen from digested food and blood, were commonplaces in antiquity:

- **Greco-Roman Physiology (Aristotle & Galen):** In *Generation of Animals* (IV.8, 776a–777a) and [*History of Animals* VII.3](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/history_anim.7.vii.html) (c. 350 BC), **Aristotle** taught that milk is literally *"concocted blood"* (*pepsis haimatos*) diverted from internal vessels to the breasts and whitened by animal heat. **Galen** ([*On the Natural Faculties* II.1](http://classics.mit.edu/Galen/natfac.2.two.html); *De Usu Partium* VII.22, XIV.8, c. AD 170) systematized the doctrine that digested food in the stomach is separated from fecal waste, converted by the liver into venous blood, and channeled to the mammary glands where blood is whitened into milk—the exact model echoed by Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Kathīr.
- **Talmudic Physiology & Ancient Pastoral Lore ([*Bekhorot* 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.6b) & [*Niddah* 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.9a)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Bekhorot* 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.6b) and [*Niddah* 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.9a)), Rabbinic authorities adopt the same pre-modern physiological axiom that *"blood becomes troubled and turns into milk"* (`דָּם נֶעְכָּר וְנַעֲשֶׂה חָלָב`, *dam ne'ekar ve-na'aseh chalav*), discussing how pure white milk is extracted from inside an animal's blood-filled body and entrails. Similar pastoral marvels praising the extraction of sweet white milk from dark cattle fed on green herbage appear in Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 14), *Rigveda* I.62.9, and pre-Islamic Arabian pastoral lore.

2:149.title: Universal Planar Qiblah Geometry Toward Mecca (Fawalli Wajhaka Shaṭra al-Masjid al-Ḥarām)
2:149.summary: [Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2/149) commands believers wherever they travel to turn their faces toward the Sacred Mosque in Mecca (*fawalli wajhaka shaṭra al-masjidi al-ḥarām*), presupposing a flat, planar earth where a single horizontal line of sight connects every observer to Mecca. Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/2:149/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/2:149/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 394](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:394)) treat the *qiblah* as a fixed cardinal orientation across a regional plane where facing east or west universally avoids facing or turning one's back to Mecca. On a spherical Earth, however, straight-line Euclidean sightlines point out into space or down through the mantle, and this planar regional orientation model reflects pre-Islamic Arabian flat-earth geography and Talmudic directional rules in Mishnah *Berakhot* 4:5 and [*Berakhot* 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61b).
2:149.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2/149), the universal command to orient one's face toward the Sacred Mosque in Mecca from any departure point assumes a flat, planar geography rather than the spherical geometry of a globe.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2/149) commands: *"From wherever you go forth, turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (wa-min ḥaythu kharajta fawalli wajhaka shaṭra al-masjidi al-ḥarāmi). Surely it is the truth indeed from your Lord. God is not oblivious of what you do."* Repeating the injunctions of [Quran 2:144](https://quran.com/2/144) and [Quran 2:150](https://quran.com/2/150), the verse employs *tawliyat al-wajh* (`فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ`, directing the front of one's face) toward the *shaṭr* (`شَطْر`, physical direction or side) of the Kaʿbah in Mecca from every land and journey.

While horizontal orientation toward a single landmark is straightforward on a flat plane, it breaks down geometrically on an oblate spheroid (`R ≈ 6,371 km`):
- **Divergence of Planar Sightlines from Spherical Surfaces:** On a globe, a worshipper standing upright faces along the local horizontal tangent plane. Because the Earth curves downward away from that tangent plane (`~8 cm` in the first kilometer, and thousands of kilometers over intercontinental distances), a straight line extending forward from the worshipper's face (`wajh`) shoots out into space, while the Euclidean chord to Mecca passes downward through the solid crust and mantle beneath the worshipper's feet.
- **The Antipodal Singularity & Multi-Directional Paradox:** At the antipode of Mecca in the South Pacific (`~21.4° S, 160.2° W`, near Tematagi atoll), every horizontal compass bearing (`0°`–`360°`) represents an identical great-circle distance (`~20,000 km`) to Mecca, while the direct vector to the Kaʿbah points straight down through the Earth's core (`nadir`). Moreover, on any great-circle geodesic, facing *away* from Mecca (`180°` opposite azimuth) still directs one's gaze along the exact same great circle around the globe toward the Kaʿbah.
- **Failure of the Cardinal East–West Rule on a Globe:** In early Islamic law, facing or turning one's back to the *qiblah* is avoided simply by facing "east or west" ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 394](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:394))—a rule valid only along the north–south Syro-Arabian corridor (`Medina–Damascus–Jerusalem`), whereas for observers directly east or west of Mecca, facing east or west means facing directly toward or away from the *qiblah*.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* reports demonstrate that the *qiblah* command was formulated within a flat, regional Syro-Arabian coordinate frame:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2:149/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī defines the command in strictly literal, planar terms: *"He, may His praise be glorified, means by His statement {From wherever you go forth}: from whichever place you go forth and to whichever place you head, turn, O Muhammad, your face—He says: redirect your face (`ḥawwil wajhaka`). We have already demonstrated that 'turning' (`al-tawliyah`) in this context toward the Sacred Mosque is only: directing the face toward it (`al-iqbālu bi-l-wajhi naḥwahu`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2:149/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under the heading *"The Third Command to Face the Kaʿbah,"* Ibn Kathīr writes: *"This is a third command from Allah to face al-Masjid al-Ḥarām (the Sacred Mosque) from every part of the earth (`min jamīʿi aqṭāri al-arḍi`),"* citing **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **al-Qurṭubī**, and **Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī** to explain that the three repetitions address one who sees the Kaʿbah directly in Mecca, one who is in other cities (*amṣār*), and one who goes forth on overland journeys (*fī al-asfār*).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Regional North–South Axis:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 394](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:394), Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī reports that Muhammad issued a universal directional rule: *"When you go to relieve yourselves, neither face the Qiblah nor turn your back to it, but face east or west (`wa-lākin sharriqū aw gharribū`)."* Similarly, in [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 342](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:342), Muhammad declares: *"What is between the East and the West is Qiblah (`mā bayna al-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi qiblah`),"* and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4486](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4486) records how the Companions in Medina switched from facing Jerusalem (*Bayt al-Maqdis*, due north) to facing Mecca (due south) by pivoting 180 degrees during prayer—all presupposing a flat regional map where north/south is the *qiblah* axis and east/west is perpendicular to it everywhere.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Orienting one's face horizontally toward a central sanctuary from any overland journey presupposed the flat-earth cosmography of pre-Islamic Arabia, the ancient Near East, and Talmudic jurisprudence:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian & Ancient Near Eastern Planar Geography (*Imago Mundi* & *Bundahishn*):** In pre-Islamic Arabian lore as well as Mesopotamian (the Babylonian *Map of the World*, BM 92687) and Sasanian Zoroastrian (*Greater Bundahishn* 5–11) cosmography, the earth was modeled as a flat disc or plane where every city and caravan route lay on one horizontal surface. Within such a planar coordinate frame, turning one's face (*tawliyat al-wajh*) toward a central shrine always defined a direct horizontal sightline across a flat expanse, with no awareness of spherical curvature or an antipode.
- **Rabbinic Halakhah on Traveling Prayer ([Mishnah *Berakhot* 4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Berakhot.4.5) & [*Berakhot* 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a)):** Formulated alongside flat-earth Talmudic models ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b); [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)), [Mishnah *Berakhot* 4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Berakhot.4.5) (c. AD 200) and [*Berakhot* 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a) codify the exact traveling injunction echoed in [Quran 2:149](https://quran.com/2/149): *"One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray. If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face (`yaḥăzir et-pānāyw`) toward the direction of the Sacred Sanctuary."* Likewise, [*Berakhot* 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61b) forbids facing along the fixed sanctuary axis when relieving oneself—the direct antecedent to [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 394](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:394).

88:20.title: The Earth Spread Out Flat Like a Level Surface (Wa-ilā al-Arḍi Kayfa Suṭiḥat)
88:20.summary: [Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88/20) invites desert travelers to gaze upon the ground and consider how it was flattened (*wa-ilā al-arḍi kayfa suṭiḥat*), pairing the level terrestrial surface with the raised sky (88:18) and pitched mountains (88:19). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/88:20/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/88:20/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), and *Tafsīr al-Jalālayn*) and the canonical tradition of Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 63](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:63)) confirm that *suṭiḥat* denotes a literally leveled, planar surface—leading al-Maḥallī and al-Suyūṭī to cite this verse as proof that the earth is flat and not spherical. In geophysics, the Earth is an oblate spheroid formed by gravitational accretion rather than a flattened plane, a description rooted in pre-Islamic Bedouin tent-cosmology, ancient Near Eastern flat-earth models (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*), and Talmudic cosmography ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)).
88:20.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88/20), the physical shape of the earth is explicitly characterized by the passive verb *suṭiḥat* ("spread flat" or "leveled into a plane"), presenting the apparent flatness of the desert horizon as a direct observational proof of divine creation.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88/20) concludes a four-part observational appeal ([Quran 88:17](https://quran.com/88/17)–20): *"Do they not look at the camels, how they are created, and at the sky, how it is raised (`rufiʿat`), and at the mountains, how they are set up (`nuṣibat`), and at the earth, how it was spread flat (`wa-ilā al-arḍi kayfa suṭiḥat`)?"* In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), the root *s-ṭ-ḥ* (`سَطَحَ`) means to spread out, flatten, or level a surface until it is completely planar, from which the noun *saṭḥ* (`سَطْح`, a flat roof-terrace or geometric plane) and the adjective *musaṭṭaḥ* (`مُسَطَّح`, flat/planar, the exact antonym of *kurawī* `كُرَوِيّ`, spherical) are derived.

Scientifically, appealing to direct visual inspection (*a-fa-lā yanẓurūna*, "do they not look?") to see how the earth was flattened (*suṭiḥat*) mistakes the local tangent plane of a massive sphere for the global shape of the Earth:
- **Oblate Spheroidal Geometry:** The Earth is not spread out into a flat plane; it is an oblate spheroid with a mean radius of `~6,371 km` (equatorial radius `6,378.1 km`, polar radius `6,356.8 km`), pulled into a nearly spherical hydrostatic equilibrium by self-gravitation during its accretion `~4.54 billion` years ago.
- **Illusion of Local Flatness:** Because human observers (~1.7 m tall) are roughly `3.7 million` times smaller than Earth's radius, the local horizon at `~4.7 km` appears flat to the naked eye, even though the surface curves downward by approximately `7.85 cm` per kilometer (`h ≈ d² / 2R`).
- **Structural Pairing with a Raised Ceiling:** By grouping *suṭiḥat* (the ground flattened like a floor) with *rufiʿat* (the sky raised overhead like a tent roof) and *nuṣibat* (mountains pitched upright like tent poles/pegs), [Quran 88:18](https://quran.com/88/18)–20 presents a unified three-part Bedouin tent-cosmology.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegetes and canonical traditions consistently understood *suṭiḥat* as describing a literally leveled, planar surface:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88:20/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī defines the verb using the concrete geometry of a flat-topped plateau: *"And His statement {and at the earth, how it was spread flat (`suṭiḥat`)}: He says, and at the earth, how it was spread out (`busiṭat`). It is said: 'a flattened mountain (`jabalun musaṭṭaḥ`)' when there is levelness (`istiwāʾ`) at its top."* Al-Ṭabarī then cites **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah**, who glosses *suṭiḥat* as *"spread out (`busiṭat`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88:20/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) & the Hadith of Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah:** Ibn Kathīr explains: *"{and at the earth, how it was spread flat?} meaning, how it has been spread out, extended, and made smooth (`kayfa busiṭat wa-muddat wa-muhhidat`). Thus, He directs the Bedouin to infer from what he himself witnesses: his camel that he rides upon, the sky that is above his head, the mountain that faces him, and the earth that is under him."* Ibn Kathīr connects this directly to the canonical *ḥadīth* of the Bedouin emissary **Ḍimām ibn Thaʿlabah** recorded in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 63](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:63) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 12a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:12a), who adjured Muhammad by the Creator who raised the sky, spread the earth, and erected the mountains.
- **Explicit Rejection of a Spherical Earth in Classical Tafsir (*Tafsīr al-Jalālayn* & al-Qurṭubī):** In *Tafsīr al-Jalālayn* on [Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88/20), Jalāl al-Dīn al-Maḥallī (d. 1459) and Jalāl al-Dīn al-Suyūṭī (d. 1505) state explicitly: *"As for His words {suṭiḥat}, that is, spread out (`busiṭat`), this literally indicates that the earth is flat (`anna al-arḍa saṭḥun`), which is the opinion of the scholars of the Revealed Law (`ʿulamāʾ al-sharʿ`), and not a sphere (`wa-laysat kuratan`) as the astronomers (`ahl al-hayʾah`) claim."* Similarly, al-Qurṭubī (*al-Jāmiʿ li-Aḥkām al-Qurʾān* on [Quran 13:3](https://quran.com/13/3) and [Quran 88:20](https://quran.com/88/20)) and Ibn ʿAṭiyyah affirmed that Muslim jurists held the earth to be flat (*mabsūṭah / musaṭṭaḥah*) based on the plain wording of *suṭiḥat*.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

While Greek astronomers from Aristotle (*On the Heavens* II.14, c. 350 BC), Eratosthenes (c. 240 BC), and Claudius Ptolemy (*Almagest* I.4, 2nd century AD) had already demonstrated the Earth's sphericity and measured its circumference, pre-Islamic Arabian, ancient Near Eastern, and Talmudic traditions maintained a flat-earth cosmology:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin Tent-Cosmology (*Jāhiliyyah* Poetry):** In pre-Islamic Arabia, nomadic Bedouins conceptualized the cosmos as a desert encampment consisting of a raised tent-canopy (*samāʾ*), upright tent-poles or pegs (*jibāl / awtād*), and a leveled ground mat (*arḍ mabsūṭah / musaṭṭaḥah*). Pre-Islamic poets such as **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** (d. c. AD 605; Ibn Hishām, *Sīrah* I:226), **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah**, and **al-Afwah al-Awdī** (*Dīwān*, p. 77) routinely paired raising the sky with spreading out a flat terrestrial floor stabilized by mountains—the exact observational triad codified in [Quran 88:18](https://quran.com/88/18)–20.
- **Pre-Socratic, Mesopotamian, and Talmudic Flat-Earth Cosmography ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b) & [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b)):** Early Ionian philosophers such as **Anaximenes of Miletus** (c. 586–526 BC; Aristotle, *On the Heavens* II.13, 294b) and **Democritus** modeled the earth as a flat, broad disc (*platy*) resting on air or water, matching the Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV–V) and Zoroastrian (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a) conception of a flat terrestrial plane beneath a solid sky-vault. Likewise, in [Babylonian Talmud, *Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b), [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), and [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b), the inhabited world is depicted as a flat expanse arched over by a solid dome, directly paralleling the flat-earth reading defended by classical Quranic exegetes against spherical astronomy (*ahl al-hayʾah*).

20:53.title: The Earth Spread Out as a Flat Cradle or Bed with Roads (Jaʿala Lakumu al-Arḍa Mahdan)
20:53.summary: In Moses's dialogue with Pharaoh, [Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53) describes God as the One "who made the earth as a cradle (*mahdan*) for you, and put pathways (*subulan*) in it for you, and sent down water from the sky." Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/20:53/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/20:53/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)) explain that both canonical readings (*mahdan* and *mihādan*) equate the earth to a smoothed-out domestic mattress or spread-out furnishing (*al-farsh wa-l-firāsh*) upon whose flat back (*ʿalā ẓahrihā*) humans sleep, stand, and travel. In planetary science, Earth's crust is the curved outer shell of a rotating spheroid rather than a stationary spread-out bed, an image drawn from pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin floor-mat metaphors, ancient Near Eastern flat-earth cosmologies (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*), and Talmudic traditions ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
20:53.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53), the earth is depicted in Moses's address to Pharaoh as a smoothed-out domestic cradle or flat bed (*mahdan* / *mihādan*) paired with an overhead sky sending down rain, reflecting a planar domestic cosmology rather than a spherical planet.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53) states: *"(It is He) who made the earth as a cradle for you, and put (path)ways in it for you, and sent down water from the sky. And by means of it We brought forth pairs of various (kinds of) vegetation (`alladhī jaʿala lakumu al-arḍa mahdan wa-salaka lakum fīhā subulan`)."* Transmitted in two canonical *mutawātir* readings—*mahdan* (`مَهْدًا`, Kufan reading) and *mihādan* (`مِهَادًا`, Medinan and Basran reading)—the noun derives from the triconsonantal root *m-h-d* (`مَهَدَ`), which in classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*) signifies smoothing out, spreading flat, and leveling a soft bed, infant's cradle, or floor-mat (*al-mawḍiʿu al-mumahhadu al-mabsūṭu*). Within the Quran's domestic architectural vocabulary, *mahd / mihād* is used interchangeably with *firāsh* (`فِرَاشًا`, a spread-out mattress/couch in [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22)) and *bisāṭ* (`بِسَاطًا`, a flat carpet in [Quran 71:19](https://quran.com/71/19)) beneath the ceiling (*saqf* / *bināʾ*) of the sky.

Scientifically, characterizing the global Earth as a leveled cradle or spread-out bed (*mahdan*) upon whose flat "back" (*ẓahr*) roads are carved conflicts with planetary geophysics:
- **Spherical Planetary Accretion vs. Leveling a Flat Bed:** The Earth was never smoothed or spread out as a horizontal plane; gravity pulled primordial planetesimals into an oblate spheroid (`R ≈ 6,371 km`) rotating on its axis at `~1,670 km/h` at the equator and orbiting the Sun at `~107,000 km/h`.
- **Active Tectonic Curvature & Relief:** Far from being a static, smoothed-out resting mat, the lithosphere consists of curved rigid plates floating on the ductile asthenosphere, constantly deformed by subduction, rifting, and mountain building.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Authoritative classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* literature confirm that early Muslims understood *mahdan / mihādan* in [Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53) as a literal leveled, stationary bed:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20:53/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī analyzes both canonical recitations and equates them with spreading a flat mattress: *"The majority of the reciters of al-Madīnah and al-Baṣrah recited it as {Who made the earth as a mihād for you}... because al-mihād is a noun of place, whereas al-mahd is a verbal noun; he said: and it is akin to al-farsh (spreading out furnishings) and al-firāsh (a spread-out bed). And the majority of the reciters of the Kufans recited it as {mahdan}, meaning: 'He Who smoothed out (`mahhada`) the earth for you as a mahd.'"* Citing **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah** and **Ibn ʿAbbās**, al-Ṭabarī explains that God smoothed out the terrestrial plane and opened roads (*subulan*, `طُرُقًا`) across it before sending rain down from His sky above.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20:53/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr writes: *"Yet Mūsā continued by saying, {He is the One Who made the earth as a bed (`mihādan` / `mahdan`) for you}, which means: a place of rest (`qarāran`) that you settle down upon, and that which you stand upon, sleep upon, or travel upon its back (`wa-tusāfirūna ʿalā ẓahrihā`). And {put pathways in it for you} means: He made roads for you to walk upon their shoulders (`fī manākibihā`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Stabilized Terrestrial Plane:** In [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369), Anas ibn Mālik reports that Muhammad explained how this flat terrestrial bed was stabilized at creation: *"When Allah created the earth, it began to sway and rock (`jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it (`fa-alqāhā ʿalayhā`), whereupon it became stable (`fa-istaqarrat`)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Summarizing creation by pairing the spreading out of a flat terrestrial floor with overland pathways, rainwater descending from the sky-vault, and sprouting vegetation was a standard cosmological motif across pre-Islamic Arabia, the ancient Near East, and Talmudic literature:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin & Ancient Near Eastern Domestic Floor Metaphors (*Enūma Eliš* & *Bundahishn*):** Across pre-Islamic Arabia and the ancient Near East, the cosmos was routinely modeled as a domestic dwelling or pitched tent whose floor was leveled like a sleeping mat or cradle (*mahd / mihād / firāsh*) beneath a rain-bearing sky-roof. In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet V), Marduk spreads out the flat terrestrial floor over the subterranean *Apsû*, opens watercourses, and releases rain from the overhead sky-vault to bring forth vegetation, while Sasanian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a, 6) and Ancient Egyptian solar hymns (such as the *Great Hymn to the Aten*) similarly celebrate the leveling of the flat land, rain from the sky, and the growth of pasture and plants.
- **Talmudic Planar Earth & Rain-Chamber Cosmology ([Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Ta'anit* 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.10a)):** In [Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) and [*Ta'anit* 9b–10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.10a), the terrestrial world is depicted as a flat expanse spread over subterranean waters and irrigated directly from upper chambers in the firmament so that diverse herbs and trees sprout across its surface—directly paralleling the flat cradle (*mahdan*) and sky-water cosmology of [Quran 20:53](https://quran.com/20/53).

43:10.title: The Earth as a Flat Carpet Spread Over Water and Pinned by Mountains (al-Arḍa Mahdan)
43:10.summary: [Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10) describes God as the One "who made the earth as a cradle/flat bed (*mahdan*) for you, and made pathways in it for you, so that you might be guided." Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/43:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/43:10/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical traditions ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)) interpret this verse within a flat-earth cosmography: al-Suddī glosses *mahdan* as a "flat carpet" (*bisāṭan*), while Ibn Kathīr notes that the earth stays firm like a bed despite being founded atop flowing water (`tayyār al-māʾ`) because God weighed it down with mountains so it would not rock. Scientifically, continental crust does not float on liquid water pinned down by mountain weights, a pre-Islamic motif attested in Meccan poetry (Zayd ibn ʿAmr), Mesopotamian and Zoroastrian cosmography (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*), and Talmudic tradition ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
43:10.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10), the earth is portrayed as a level carpet or flat bed (*mahdan*) stretched out for overland travel, which classical exegesis explicitly identifies as a flat surface resting upon cosmic waters and held motionless by mountain weights.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10) states: *"(It is He) who made the earth as a cradle for you, and made (path)ways in it for you, so that you might be guided (`alladhī jaʿala lakumu al-arḍa mahdan wa-jaʿala lakum fīhā subulan laʿallakum tahtadūna`)."* Following the cosmological assertion in [Quran 43:9](https://quran.com/43/9) that God created the heavens and the earth, the verse characterizes the earth's global form as a *mahd* (`مَهْد` — a smoothed, leveled bed or floor-mat, read *mihādan* `مِهَادًا` in the Medinan and Basran recitations) across which mountain passes and roads (*subulan*) are cut to guide travelers from land to land.

Scientifically, both the textual depiction of the earth as a leveled flat bed and the classical cosmological mechanics attached to it conflict with modern geophysics:
- **Curved Spheroid vs. Level Carpet (*Bisāṭ / الوطاء*):** The Earth's surface is not a flat carpet or horizontal floor (*waṭāʾ* / *bisāṭ*); it is the closed spherical surface (`~510.1 million km²`) of an oblate planet rotating in space.
- **No Subterranean Ocean Beneath the Crust:** Contrary to the classical exegetical explanation of [Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10), the Earth's crust is not resting atop a cosmic current of liquid water (`tayyār al-māʾ`). Seismic wave propagation (both compressional P-waves and shear S-waves, which cannot travel through liquids) proves that beneath the solid lithosphere (`~5–100 km` thick) lies a solid, rocky silicate mantle extending down to `~2,890 km`, surrounding a liquid iron-nickel outer core.
- **Mountains Do Not Anchor the Earth Against Shaking:** Mountains are formed by tectonic plate collisions and volcanism and are the primary global epicenters of earthquakes, rather than heavy anchors cast onto a floating flat disc to stop it from swaying.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

In their commentary on [Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10), foundational Sunni exegetes spell out the exact flat-earth, water-supported cosmology underlying the word *mahdan*:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī paraphrases the verse: *"{(It is He) who made the earth as a cradle (`mahdan`) for you}: He says, He who smoothed out the earth for you (`mahhada lakumu al-arḍa`), and made it a level surface under foot (`waṭāʾan`) for you that you tread upon with your feet and walk upon with your legs."* Al-Ṭabarī then records the verbatim narration of **al-Suddī** (d. 745): *"Muḥammad narrated to us... on the authority of al-Suddī: {(It is He) who made the earth as a cradle (`mahdan`) for you}, he said: 'A flat carpet/expanse (`bisāṭan`).' {and made pathways in it for you}, he said: 'The roads (`al-ṭuruq`).'"*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43:10/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under the heading *"The Earth as a Cradle and Roads for Guidance,"* Ibn Kathīr provides a remarkable summary of classical Islamic cosmography: *"Then He says: {Who has made for you the earth like a bed (`mahdan`)}, meaning: a mattress (`firāshan`), a stationary and firm resting place (`qarāran thābitatan`), on which they travel, stand, sleep, and move about—even though it is created upon a current of water, but He has anchored it with the mountains lest it sway this way or that (`maʿa annahā makhlūqatun ʿalā tayyāri al-māʾi, lākinnahu arsāhā bi-l-jibāli li-allā tamīda hākadhā wa-lā hākadhā`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Floating Earth Anchored by Mountains:** Ibn Kathīr's statement directly reflects the canonical tradition in [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369), where Muhammad states that when God created the earth *"it began to sway and rock (`jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it,"* as well as the early traditions recorded by al-Ṭabarī (*Tārīkh al-Umam wa-l-Mulūk* I:49–51) and Wahb ibn Munabbih that the flat earth was spread out upon the cosmic waters and rocked like a ship until God weighed it down with mountains.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The cosmological model articulated in [Quran 43:10](https://quran.com/43/10) and its classical *tafsīr*—a flat carpet-like earth spread out over cosmic waters and pinned down by mountain weights—was a well-known pre-Islamic Arabian, Near Eastern, and Talmudic tradition:

- **Pre-Islamic Meccan Poetry (Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, d. c. AD 605):** Recorded in Ibn Hishām's *al-Sīrah al-Nabawiyyah* (Vol. 1, p. 226), the pre-Islamic Meccan monotheist Zayd ibn ʿAmr described creation in the exact same terms: *"He spread it out (`daḥāhā`), and when He saw it resting level upon the water (`istawat ʿalā al-māʾi`), He anchored the mountains upon it (`arsā ʿalayhā al-jibālā`)."*
- **Mesopotamian, Zoroastrian, Pre-Socratic, and Talmudic Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*, & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In Babylonian cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV–V), the flat earth is spread out as a resting platform (*Ešarra*) directly above the subterranean freshwater ocean (*Apsû*), a concept echoed by the Ionian philosopher **Thales of Miletus** (c. 585 BC; Aristotle, *On the Heavens* II.13, 294a28), who taught that the flat earth floats on water like a log or ship and rocks when the underlying water moves. Similarly, in Sasanian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 6b, 24), the mountains are driven into the earth as anchors to prevent it from shaking, while [Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) and [*Ta'anit* 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.10a) depict the flat terrestrial plane resting directly atop the subterranean waters.

78:6.title: The Earth Spread Out as a Flat Bed Pinned by Mountain Tent-Pegs (al-Arḍa Mihādan)
78:6.summary: [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6) opens a creation passage with the rhetorical question, "Have We not made the earth as a bed (*mihādan*)?" immediately pairing it in 78:7 with "and the mountains as tent-pegs (*awtādan*)?" Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/78:6/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/78:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)) explain this couplet through a literal Bedouin tent metaphor: the earth was spread out as a flat carpet (*bisāṭan*) that is "stationary, still, and firm" (`qārratan sākinatan thābitatan`), pinned down by mountain stakes so it does not sway. In modern geophysics, the Earth is a rotating spheroid whose tectonic plates continuously drift and collide at seismically active mountain belts, whereas this tent-mat cosmology echoes pre-Islamic Bedouin poetry (Zayd ibn ʿAmr, al-Afwah al-Awdī), Zoroastrian mountain-peg mythology (*Bundahishn*), and Talmudic cosmology ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
78:6.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6), the earth is conceptualized through a nomadic Bedouin architectural metaphor as a flat, stationary sleeping mat or carpet (*mihādan*) spread out on the ground and pinned down by mountain tent-pegs ([Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7)) beneath a constructed roof ([Quran 78:12](https://quran.com/78/12)).

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6) asks: *"Have We not made the earth as a bed (`a-lam najʿali al-arḍa mihādan`)?"* Immediately followed by [Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7) (*"and the mountains as pegs [`wa-l-jibāla awtādan`]?"*) and [Quran 78:12](https://quran.com/78/12)–13 (*"and We built above you seven strong [heavens], and placed a blazing lamp"*), the passage constructs a complete domestic Bedouin tent (*bayt al-shaʿr*) model of the universe. In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *mihād* (`مِهَاد`, from the root *m-h-d*, to level and spread flat) denotes a smoothed-out bed, floor-carpet, or level resting mat (*al-mawḍiʿu al-mumahhadu al-mabsūṭu*), serving as the direct counterpart to *firāsh* (mattress, [Quran 2:22](https://quran.com/2/22)) and *bisāṭ* (flat carpet, [Quran 71:19](https://quran.com/71/19)).

Scientifically, describing the Earth as a leveled, immobile floor-mat (*mihādan*) pinned down by mountain stakes contradicts both planetary astronomy and plate tectonics:
- **Spherical Geometry vs. a Spread-Out Carpet:** The Earth is not a horizontal floor spread out beneath a ceiling; it is an oblate spheroid (`mean radius ≈ 6,371 km`) formed by gravitational accretion in three-dimensional space.
- **Continuous Planetary & Tectonic Motion (Not *Qārrah Sākinah*):** Contrary to the claim that the terrestrial floor was made motionless and fixed, the Earth rotates on its axis (`~465 m/s` at the equator), orbits the Sun (`~29.78 km/s`), and has a lithosphere broken into tectonic plates that continuously drift across the ductile asthenosphere at `1–10 cm/year`.
- **Incompatibility of the Tent-Mat & Peg Couple:** In a Bedouin tent, a flat carpet (*mihād*) is pinned to an underlying substrate by rigid stakes (*awtād*) to stop it from shifting. In geophysics, continental crust (`ρ ≈ 2.7–2.8 g/cm³`) floats hydrostatically on the denser mantle (`ρ ≈ 3.3 g/cm³`), and mountain ranges are the primary epicenters of destructive earthquakes produced by plate collisions—not static pegs immobilizing a flat mat.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Foundational Islamic commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* collections unanimously interpret *mihādan* in [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6) as a literal flat expanse made stationary and motionless:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78:6/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī explains: *"Thus He said to them: {Have We not made the earth} for you {as a bed (`mihādan`)}, which you stretch out upon and use as a spread-out mattress (`tamtaddūnahā wa-taftarishūnahā`)."* Al-Ṭabarī then cites **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah** with his chain of transmission: *"Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us: Mihrān narrated to us, from Saʿīd, from Qatādah: {Have We not made the earth as a bed (`mihādan`)}: meaning, a flat carpet/expanse (`bisāṭan`)."* Under the next verse ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)), al-Ṭabarī adds: *"And the mountains as stakes (`awtādan`) for the earth, lest it sway with you (`an tamīda bikum`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under the heading *"Manifestations of Allah's Power in Creation,"* Ibn Kathīr defines *mihādan* explicitly as both leveled and completely stationary: *"Thus, He said: {Have We not made the earth as a bed (`mihādan`)}? Meaning: leveled and prepared for the creation (`mumahhadatan li-l-khalāʾiqi`), subdued for them, and made stationary, still, and firm (`qārratan sākinatan thābitatan`)."* In [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), he continues: *"He made them as pegs for it, anchoring it, stabilizing it, and fixing it so that it became still (`ḥattā sakanat`) and does not shake with those who are on it."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Pinning the Unsteady Earth:** In [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369) (also cited by Ibn Kathīr under [Quran 79:32](https://quran.com/79/32)), Anas ibn Mālik narrates from Muhammad: *"When Allah created the earth, it began to sway and rock (`jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it, whereupon it became stable."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Comparing the cosmos to a tent whose flat floor-mat is stretched out and pinned down by mountain stakes beneath a vaulted roof was a classic pre-Islamic Arabian, Zoroastrian, and Near Eastern cosmological motif:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Poetry (*Jāhiliyyah*):** Pre-Islamic poets regularly employed the domestic architecture of the Bedouin tent—consisting of a spread-out carpet (*mihād / firāsh*), tent-pegs (*awtād*), pillars (*ʿamad*), and roof canopy—to describe both tribal stability and the cosmos. The 6th-century poet **al-Afwah al-Awdī** (*Dīwān*, p. 77) wrote: *"A tent cannot be erected without pillars, and there are no pillars if the tent pegs (`awtād`) are not firmly fixed,"* while **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah** (*Dīwān*, p. 299) and **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** (d. c. AD 605; Ibn Hishām, *Sīrah* I:226) described God spreading out the flat earth (*daḥāhā*) upon the water and anchoring the mountains upon it as pegs (*awtād* / *rawāsī*).
- **Zoroastrian, Mesopotamian, and Talmudic Mountain-Peg & Pillar Cosmology (*Bundahishn*, *Gilgamesh*, & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 6b, 18, 24; *Zādspram* 3), after the destructive spirit Ahriman assaults the newly created flat earth and causes it to shake violently, Ohrmazd drives the great mountains (led by Mount Hara Berezaiti / Alborz) into the earth as stabilizing pegs and anchors to hold the terrestrial plane still. Similarly, Mesopotamian cosmology (*Epic of Gilgamesh* Tablet IX; *Enūma Eliš* Tablet V) depicts twin cosmic mountains (*Mashu*) anchoring the flat earth and sky-vault, while [Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) depicts the flat terrestrial expanse standing upon fixed pillars (*ʿammûdîm*).

18:47.title: Moving the Mountains to Expose the Entire Earth as an Unobstructed Flat Plain (al-Arḍa Bārizatan)
18:47.summary: [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) declares that on the Day of Resurrection God "shall cause the mountains to move, and you will see the earth coming forth / fully exposed (*wa-tarā al-arḍa bārizatan*)" as humanity is gathered upon it. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/18:47/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/18:47/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6521](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6521)) explain that once mountains, trees, and buildings are removed, the entire earth becomes a single flat, level plain (*saṭḥan mustawiyan*) resembling a round white loaf of fine flour (*ka-qurṣati naqiyyin*) where nothing conceals anyone from onlookers. Geometrically, however, removing surface topography on a spherical planet (`R ≈ 6,371 km`) never renders the earth an unobstructed plane visible at once, since Earth's curvature blocks sightlines beyond `~4.7 km`—a motif rooted in Zoroastrian eschatology (*Greater Bundahishn* 34.31–33) and Talmudic flat-disc cosmology ([*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)).
18:47.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47), the eschatological removal of mountains is said to leave the entire earth openly exposed to sight (*bārizatan*), presupposing that only surface obstacles like mountains, trees, and buildings—rather than the curvature of a spherical globe—prevent unobstructed visibility across the earth.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) states: *"On the Day when We shall cause the mountains to move, and you see the earth coming forth, and We gather them so that We do not leave any of them behind (`wa-yawma nusayyiru al-jibāla wa-tarā al-arḍa bārizatan wa-ḥasharnāhum fa-lam nughādir minhum aḥadan`)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *bārizah* (`بَارِزَة`, active participle of *baraza*, to come out into the open or be fully exposed to view) describes a flat, open plain (*al-barāz*) completely devoid of topographical cover. This verse forms a direct pair with [Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105)–107, which states that when God blasts away the mountains, *"He will leave it as a level, smooth plain (`qāʿan ṣafṣafan`), in which you will see neither crookedness/depression (`ʿiwajan`) nor curve/elevation (`amtan`)."*

From the standpoint of spherical geometry and geodesy, the premise that removing mountains, trees, and structures makes the earth fully exposed to sight (*tarā al-arḍa bārizatan*) and leaves it without curvature (*lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan wa-lā amtan*) is a classic flat-earth inference:
- **Spherical Curvature Creates an Impassable Horizon:** On a flat plane, tall mountains and trees are the sole visual barriers obstructing an observer's sightline; once pulverized, the entire plane becomes visible from end to end. On a spherical Earth (`R ≈ 6,371 km`), however, even if every mountain, building, and tree were leveled to a smooth surface, the planet's curvature drops away by `h ≈ d² / (2R)` (`~7.85 cm` at 1 km, `~7.85 m` at 10 km, and `~785 m` at 100 km).
- **Horizon Limit (`~4.7 km`):** For an observer (`1.7 m` eye height) standing on a featureless globe, the geometric horizon lies just `~4.7 km` away, hiding `99.99998%` of Earth's surface below the curve.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions confirm that [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) envisions the earth reduced to a flat disc or level plane where all gathered humanity is simultaneously exposed to view:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18:47/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī explains the causal connection between removing mountains and exposing the earth to the eye: *"{On the Day when We shall cause the mountains to move} away from the earth, thus crumbling them completely to dust... {and you see the earth coming forth (`bārizatan`)} meaning: apparent (`ẓāhiratan`); and its becoming apparent to the sight of the eyes of the onlookers (`li-raʾyi aʿyuni al-nāẓirīna`), without anything concealing it—neither mountain nor tree—is its 'coming forth' (`burūzuhā`)."* Al-Ṭabarī transmits chains from **Mujāhid ibn Jabr** (*"There is no concealment [`khamar`] in it, nor hidden depression [`ghayābah`], nor building, nor stone in it"*) and **Qatādah ibn Diʿāmah** (*"There is no building or tree upon it"*).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18:47/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under the heading *"Terrors of the Day of Resurrection,"* Ibn Kathīr explicitly equates *al-arḍa bārizatan* in [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) with the flat plane of [Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105)–107: *"Allah says that the mountains will disappear, the resting-places will become level (`wa-tatasāwā al-mihād`), and the earth will remain {as a level smooth plain (`qāʿan ṣafṣafan`)}, meaning a flat planar surface (`saṭḥan mustawiyan`) with {nothing crooked (`lā ʿiwaja`)} in it {or curved (`wa-lā amtan`)}, meaning no valley and no mountain. Thus, Allah says: {and you see the earth coming forth (`bārizatan`)}, meaning clearly visible and apparent (`bādiyatan ẓāhiratan`), with no landmark for anyone, nor any place to conceal anyone; rather, all of creation will be exposed in full view (`ḍāḥūna`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Comparing the Leveled Earth to a Flat Loaf of Bread (*Qurṣat al-Naqiyy*):** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6521](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6521) (and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2790](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2790)), Sahl ibn Saʿd narrates that Muhammad described the leveled earth of Resurrection as a flat round pita-loaf (*qurṣah*): *"The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a reddish-white land like a flat loaf of pure wheaten bread (`ka-qurṣati naqiyyin`), with no landmark (`maʿlam`) on it for anyone."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The apocalyptic expectation that removing all mountains and hills at the end of time will expose the entire earth as a single unobstructed flat plain was a widespread Near Eastern, Zoroastrian, and Talmudic motif:

- **Sasanian Zoroastrian Eschatological Leveling (*Greater Bundahishn* 34.31–33 & *Zādspram* 35):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian eschatology—which circulated widely across the Sasanian Near East and pre-Islamic Arabia—the final renovation of the world (*Frashokereti*) culminates in the melting and leveling of all mountains and hills so that the entire earth becomes a single flat, uniform enclosure without elevations or valleys (*hamōyēn zamīg hāmōn bawēd*, "all the earth becomes a level plain") where nothing conceals one creature from another.
- **Ancient Near Eastern Flat-Disc Cosmography & Talmudic Parallels ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)):** Both ancient Near Eastern disc-maps (such as the Babylonian *Imago Mundi*, BM 92687, which models the earth as a flat circular disc surrounded by water) and Talmudic cosmography ([Babylonian Talmud, *Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b); [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b); [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) presuppose a flat terrestrial disc beneath a solid sky-dome on which only surface topography—mountains, trees, and structures—blocks horizontal sightlines across the world, directly paralleling the flat white bread-loaf (*qurṣat naqiyy*) and unobstructed plain (*bārizatan*) of [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6521](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6521).

20:105.title: Flattening the Mountains Leaves the Entire Earth an Uncurved, Level Plain (Qāʿan Ṣafṣafan)
20:105.summary: [Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105) and its following verses ([20:106–107](https://quran.com/20/106-107)) assert that when God pulverizes the mountains into dust on the Day of Judgment, the entire Earth will be left behind as a smooth, flat plain (*qāʿan ṣafṣafan*) devoid of any depression or curvature (*ʿiwajan wa-lā amtā*). Classical exegetes ([al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/20:105/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/20:105/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and prophetic *ḥadīth* ([Bukhārī 6521](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6521)) confirm that removing surface mountains reduces the world to a single flat sheet resembling a round loaf of bread. In planetary geodesy, mountains make up less than 0.14% of Earth's radius; leveling them would still leave a curved oblate spheroid dropping ~8 inches per mile squared rather than a flat plane. This imagery reflects ancient Near Eastern, Zoroastrian (*Greater Bundahishn* 34.33), Talmudic ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)), and pre-Islamic Bedouin flat-earth cosmologies.
20:105.explanation:
The Earth is Flat. In [Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105) and its syntactical continuation in [Quran 20:106–107](https://quran.com/20/106-107), the Quran presupposes a flat terrestrial geometry in which mountains and valleys are the sole obstacle to a completely level, uncurved Earth.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105) declares: *"They ask you about the mountains. Say: 'My Lord will scatter them as dust'"* (`وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْجِبَالِ فَقُلْ يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا`, *wa-yasʾalūnaka ʿani al-jibāli fa-qul yansifuhā rabbī nasfan*). The sentence continues directly into [Quran 20:106](https://quran.com/20/106)–[20:107](https://quran.com/20/107): *"and He will leave it [the earth] a barren, level plain (fa-yadharuhā qāʿan ṣafṣafan), in which you will not see any crookedness or curve (lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan wa-lā amtā)."* In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *nasf* (`نَسْف`) denotes winnowing grain or pulverizing a structure into wind-blown dust; *qāʿ* (`قَاع`) and *ṣafṣaf* (`صَفْصَف`) denote a flat, horizontal expanse of land; *ʿiwaj* (`عِوَج`) denotes crookedness, inclination, or depression; and *amt* (`أَمْت`) denotes a curve, bulge, swelling, or elevation.

This cause-and-effect sequence—also reflected in [Quran 18:47](https://quran.com/18/47) (*"And the Day We shall cause the mountains to move, and you will see the earth barizan [exposed/flat]"*)—rests on a fundamental misconception of terrestrial geometry:
- **Topographical Relief vs. Planetary Curvature:** The text assumes that the Earth's underlying substrate is already a flat horizontal plane, so that merely blasting away surface mountains (`yansifuhā`) and filling valleys leaves the entire terrestrial surface flat, uncurved, and visible from end to end without inclination (`ʿiwaj`) or bulge (`amt`).
- **Geodetic Reality of an Oblate Spheroid:** The Earth is an oblate spheroid with a mean radius of approximately `6,371 km`. Even the highest peak on Earth, Mount Everest (`8.848 km`), represents less than `0.14%` of the planet's radius. If every mountain range on Earth were completely pulverized and leveled to mean sea level, the resulting surface would not be a flat plain (`qāʿan ṣafṣafan`) devoid of curvature (`amt`). Instead, it would be a smooth sphere whose surface curves downward by `~7.98 inches per mile squared` (`~12.6 cm per km²`), concealing the surface beyond a horizon of `~4.7 km` for a standing observer.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Sunni exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions unanimously understood [Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20/105)–[20:107](https://quran.com/20/107) as a literal physical leveling of the Earth into a single flat, horizontal sheet:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20:105/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) & [20:106](https://quran.com/20:106/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)–[20:107](https://quran.com/20:107/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī glosses *yansifuhā rabbī nasfan* as: *"My Lord will winnow them completely (`yudhrīhā rabbī tadhriyatan`), and He will cause them to fly away by uprooting them and eradicating them from their roots, crushing some of them against others, and turning them into scattered dust particles (`habāʾan munbaththan`)."* Turning to the resulting state of the Earth in [Quran 20:106–107](https://quran.com/20/106-107), al-Ṭabarī cites **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **Mujāhid**, **Qatādah**, and **Ibn Zayd** to explain that *qāʿan ṣafṣafan* means a flat, smooth land (`arḍan malsāʾa... mustawiyatan`), and concludes regarding *lā tarā fīhā ʿiwajan wa-lā amtā*: *"You will not see in it any inclination from levelness, nor elevation, nor depression; rather it is level and smooth (`bal hiya mustawiyatun malsāʾu`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 20:105](https://quran.com/20:105/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) & [20:106](https://quran.com/20:106/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)–[20:107](https://quran.com/20:107/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains that God *"will take them [the mountains] away from their places, wipe them out, and remove them completely,"* leaving the Earth *"as one expanse spread out (`bisāṭan wāḥidan`)."* On [Quran 20:107](https://quran.com/20/107), Ibn Kathīr states: *"meaning, on that Day you will not see in the earth any valley, hill, or any place, whether low or elevated. Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Qatādah, and others of the Salaf all said the same."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Flat Loaf-Shaped Earth:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6521](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6521) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2790](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2790), Sahl ibn Saʿd reports that Muhammad described the Earth after the removal of its mountains on the Day of Resurrection: *"People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a reddish-white land like a pure flat round loaf of bread (`ka-qurṣati al-naqiyy`), having no landmarks (`ʿalam`) for anyone."* Comparing the mountainless Earth to a flat disc of bread (`qurṣah`) reflects the flat-earth cosmology of the verse.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that removing mountains and filling valleys transforms the entire Earth into a flat, uncurved plain was rooted in ancient Near Eastern and Iranian flat-earth cosmologies:

- **Zoroastrian Eschatological Leveling of the Mountains (*Greater Bundahishn* 34.33 & *Zādspram* 34):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 34.33), the Earth was originally created as a completely flat, level disc without mountains or valleys before the assault of Ahriman caused mountains (such as Mount Hara Berezaiti / Alborz) to rise up. At the final cosmic renovation (*Frashokereti*), the metal within the mountains melts and levels every peak and hollow until *"this earth becomes flat and level, with no hill and no summit, no hollow and no high ground."* [Quran 20:105–107](https://quran.com/20/105-107) reproduces this exact flat-earth premise that removing surface mountains leaves the entire world a single uncurved plain (*qāʿan ṣafṣafan*).
- **Mesopotamian, Talmudic, and Pre-Islamic Arabian Flat-Plain Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** Across Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablets IV–V) and Talmudic ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b); [*Pesachim* 94b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.94b)) cosmologies, as well as pre-Islamic Bedouin lore, the terrestrial world was conceived as a flat, spread-out disk (*bisāṭ* / *firāsh*) whose only vertical irregularities were surface mountains and valleys.

27:61.title: The Earth as a Stationary, Unmoving Abode (Qarāran) Anchored by Mountains
27:61.summary: [Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27/61) praises God for making the Earth a stationary resting place (*qarāran*), cutting rivers through it, fixing stabilizing mountains (*rawāsiya*) upon it, and setting a partition (*ḥājizan*) between the two seas. Classical commentators ([Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/27:61/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), [al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/27:61/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) define *qarāran* as completely still, fixed, and motionless (*sākinatan thābitatan lā tataḥarraku*), arguing that human life would be impossible if our planet moved. In reality, the Earth spins on its axis at ~1,670 km/h and orbits the Sun at ~107,200 km/h, its tectonic plates continually drift, and estuarine waters actively mix. This geostatic worldview reflects Greco-Roman geocentric physics (Aristotle's *De Caelo* and Ptolemy's *Almagest*), Mesopotamian and Zoroastrian mountain-anchor cosmology, and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
27:61.explanation:
The Earth does not Rotate. In [Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27/61), the Earth is portrayed as a stationary, immovable foundation (*qarāran*) held still by heavy mountain anchors (*rawāsiya*) with a permanent partition separating sweet and salty waters, reflecting the geostatic cosmology of Late Antiquity.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27/61) states: *"Or (is He not better) who made the earth a dwelling place (qarāran), and placed rivers in the midst of it, and made firm mountains (rawāsiya) for it, and placed a partition (ḥājizan) between the two seas?"* (`أَمَّن جَعَلَ الْأَرْضَ قَرَارًا وَجَعَلَ خِلَالَهَا أَنْهَارًا وَجَعَلَ لَهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ حَاجِزًا`). In classical Arabic lexicography (al-Farāhīdī's *Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; Ibn Manẓūr's *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *qarār* (`قَرَار`, from the root *q-r-r*) denotes a state of rest, stillness, and immobility—the antonym of motion (*ḥarakah*)—paired here with *rawāsiya* (`رَوَاسِيَ`, stationary anchors or ballast weights, from *r-s-w*, "to drop anchor").

Every physical premise of this verse conflicts with modern planetary physics, geophysics, and oceanography:
- **Planetary Rotation and Orbital Motion:** Far from being a motionless, stationary resting place (*qarār*), the Earth rotates continuously on its axis at an equatorial velocity of `~1,670 km/h` (`465 m/s`), revolves around the Sun in a heliocentric orbit at `~107,200 km/h` (`29.78 km/s`), and travels with the Solar System around the Milky Way at `~828,000 km/h`. Because the atmosphere and oceans co-rotate with the planet under conservation of angular momentum and gravity, inhabitants do not feel this high-speed motion.
- **Tectonic Motion vs. Mountain Anchors (*Rawāsiya*):** The Earth's crust is fractured into lithospheric plates that continuously move horizontally across the ductile asthenosphere. Mountains do not immobilize the Earth; rather, mountain belts are formed by tectonic plate collisions and represent the primary zones of continental earthquakes.
- **Estuarine Mixing vs. an Impermeable Partition (*Ḥājizan*):** Freshwater rivers and saltwater seas are not kept apart by a permanent barrier preventing them from corrupting one another; where rivers meet the ocean, freshwater and seawater continuously and completely mix through tidal turbulence and diffusion to form brackish estuaries.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Authoritative classical commentators confirm that *qarāran* and *rawāsiya* in [Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27/61) were understood literally to mean that the Earth is completely stationary and does not move:

- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27:61/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr defines `amman jaʿala al-arḍa qarāran` in unambiguous physical terms: *"meaning: stationary, still, and fixed (`qārratan sākinatan thābitatan`), so that it does not sway or move with its inhabitants (`lā tamīdu wa-lā tataḥarraku bi-ahlihā`), nor shake them, because if it were to do so, life and living upon it would not be pleasant. Rather, by His grace and mercy, He made it a smooth bed and carpet, fixed, which neither quakes nor moves (`mِihādan bisāṭan thābitatan lā tatazalzalu wa-lā tataḥarraku`), as He said in the other verse: {Allah, Who has made for you the earth as a fixed abode (qarāran) and the sky as a canopy (bināʾan)} ([Quran 40:64](https://quran.com/40/64))."* Regarding *rawāsiya*, Ibn Kathīr adds: *"meaning, towering mountains that anchor the earth and fix it (`tursī al-arḍa wa-tuthabbituhā`) lest it sway with you,"* and defines the *ḥājiz* as a barrier preventing sweet river water and salty ocean water from mixing.
- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27:61/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī similarly explains: *"Or is He not better who made the earth for you a place of stillness (`qarāran`) upon which you settle and which does not sway with you (`tastaqirrūna ʿalayhā lā tamīdu bikum`), and placed rivers amidst it, and made for it `rawāsiya`, which are the fixed mountains (`thawābit al-jibāl`), and placed a partition between the two seas—between the fresh and the salty—lest one of them corrupt the other."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369), Anas ibn Mālik reports that Muhammad said: *"When Allah created the earth, it began to sway (`jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it, and it became stationary (`fa-staqarrat`—from the same root `q-r-r` as `qarāran`)."* Conversely, in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3199](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3199) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 159a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:159a), it is the Sun that physically travels across the sky over a stationary Earth and prostrates beneath God's Throne every night.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The conception of the Earth as an unmoving, stationary foundation anchored against motion and bounded from the waters was standard across ancient Near Eastern and Greco-Roman thought:

- **Greco-Roman Geostatic Physics (Aristotle & Claudius Ptolemy):** In *De Caelo* (II.14, 296a–297b, 4th century BC) and the *Almagest* (I.7, 2nd century AD), **Aristotle** and **Ptolemy** argued that the Earth is completely stationary (`ἀκίνητος`) at the center of the cosmos because, if it rotated or moved, living creatures on its surface would feel violent instability—the exact argument repeated by Ibn Kathīr for why the Earth was made stationary (*qarāran*).
- **Mesopotamian, Persian, and Pre-Islamic Arabian Stationary-Earth Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš*, *Bundahishn*, & Jāhilī Poetry):** In Babylonian cosmogony (*Enūma Eliš* Tablets I and IV–V), the flat terrestrial floor (*Ešarra*) is fixed motionless above the sweet subterranean waters (*Apsû*), kept separate from the bitter marine ocean (*Tiāmat*), while in Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 6B–8) the mountains are fastened into the earth as anchors to halt its shaking. Likewise, pre-Islamic Arabian poets such as **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** and **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** celebrated God spreading out the Earth and fixing heavy mountains (*rawāsī*) upon it so it settled still (*fa-qarrat*) after swaying, while the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) depicts a stationary earth resting on pillars, waters, and mountains.

25:53.category: Permanent Barrier between Fresh and Salt Water
25:53.title: An Impermeable Barrier and Inviolable Ban (Barzakh wa-Ḥijran Maḥjūran) Between Fresh and Salt Water
25:53.summary: [Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25/53) states that God released two bodies of water—one potable fresh water (*ʿadhb furāt*) and the other bitter saltwater (*milḥ ujāj*)—while setting an impassable barrier (*barzakh*) and an inviolable quarantine (*ḥijran maḥjūran*) between them. Classical exegetes ([al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/25:53/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/25:53/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) identify the two waters as inland freshwater rivers and the salty ocean, explaining the barrier as dry land or a divine decree preventing them from mixing and spoiling one another. In physical oceanography, freshwater rivers and seawater never remain separated by an impermeable partition; wherever they meet in estuaries, they continuously mix through tidal turbulence and diffusion into brackish water. This motif reflects Mesopotamian dual-ocean cosmogony (*Enūma Eliš*), Persian Gulf submarine-spring lore, and Greco-Roman natural history in Aristotle (*Meteorologica*) and Pliny the Elder (*Naturalis Historia*).
25:53.explanation:
Permanent Barrier between Fresh and Salt Water. In [Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25/53), the Quran asserts that sweet drinking water and bitter ocean brine are kept permanently apart by an impassable barrier (*barzakh*) and an absolute ban (*ḥijran maḥjūran*), contradicting the fluid dynamics of estuarine mixing.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25/53) declares: *"He (it is) who has let loose the two seas, this one sweet and fresh (hādhā ʿadhbun furātun), and this (other) one salty (and) bitter (wa-hādhā milḥun ujājun), and placed between them a barrier (barzakhan), and an absolute ban (wa-ḥijran maḥjūran)"* (`وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا`). In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *baḥr* denotes any large body of water (river or sea); *ʿadhb furāt* denotes intensely sweet, potable drinking water (cf. [Quran 35:12](https://quran.com/35/12)); *milḥ ujāj* denotes salty, bitter seawater; *barzakh* denotes an intervening partition; and *ḥijran maḥjūran* is an emphatic cognate accusative denoting an absolute, inviolable prohibition.

In physical oceanography and estuarine hydrodynamics, no impermeable barrier prevents fresh and salt water from mixing:
- **Complete Turbulent Mixing in Estuaries:** When freshwater rivers (`~0 PSU`, `~1,000 kg/m³`) discharge into the ocean (`~35 PSU`, `~1,025 kg/m³`), velocity shear between the buoyant surface outflow and the dense bottom saltwater wedge generates Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities, while tidal pumping, wind, and bottom friction drive continuous turbulent entrainment. All river runoff mixes with seawater to produce brackish water (`0.5–30 PSU`) before homogenizing into the global ocean.
- **Haloclines Are Active Diffusion Gradients, Not Barriers:** Concordist claims that *barzakh* refers to estuarine pycnoclines or haloclines misrepresent fluid mechanics: a halocline is a transitional zone of rapid salinity change where water molecules and dissolved ions (`Na⁺`, `Cl⁻`) actively diffuse and mix across the gradient—never a forbidden partition (*ḥijran maḥjūran*).
- **Optical Silt Plumes and Salty Straits:** Viral photographs of two-colored water at river mouths merely show temporary optical turbidity fronts of suspended clay and glacial silt that disperse within days. Appealing to oceanic straits like Gibraltar ([Quran 55:19–20](https://quran.com/55/19-20)) contradicts [Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25/53)'s explicit definition that one sea is sweet drinking water (*ʿadhb furāt*), since both the Atlantic (`~36.0 PSU`) and Mediterranean (`~38.4 PSU`) are bitter saltwater (*milḥ ujāj*) that actively mix.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Authoritative classical commentators confirm that [Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25/53) refers to freshwater rivers and the salty ocean, and that they understood the *barzakh* either as dry land or as a miraculous divine ban preventing them from mixing:

- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25:53/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr states: *"The sweet water is like that in rivers, springs, and wells... This was the view of Ibn Jurayj and of Ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī], and this is the meaning without a doubt, for nowhere in creation is there a stationary sea which is fresh and sweet."* Noting that God made the seas salty *"lest the air turn putrid"* ([Sunan Abī Dāwūd 83](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:83)), Ibn Kathīr defines the barrier: *"His saying: {a barrier (barzakhan)} means a partition, which is dry land (`wa-huwa al-yābisu mina al-arḍ`). {and a complete partition (wa-ḥijran maḥjūran)} meaning, preventing one of them from reaching the other,"* citing [Quran 55:19–20](https://quran.com/55/19-20) and [Quran 27:61](https://quran.com/27/61).
- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 25:53](https://quran.com/25:53/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī cites **Ibn ʿAbbās** (*"the barzakh is the land between them,"* `al-arḍu baynahumā`), **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** (*"this is the dry land"*), **Mujāhid** (*"an invisible partition; the sweet does not mix in the sea"*), and **Ibn Zayd** (*"a veil so they do not meet"*). Al-Ṭabarī also records from **Ibn Jurayj** (d. AD 767): *"I have not found a sweet sea except the sweet rivers. For the Tigris falls into the sea, and an expert regarding it informed me that it falls into the sea, yet it does not surge into it; between them is something like a white thread... and the Nile pours into the sea."* Al-Ṭabarī concludes that God mixes river water into the sea yet miraculously prevents the salty brine from spoiling the sweet water.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the theological motif of separated sweet and bitter cosmic waters and the observation of buoyant river plumes and submarine springs were well known centuries before Islam:

- **Mesopotamian Cosmogony (*Enūma Eliš*) & Gulf Submarine Springs:** Since the 2nd millennium BC (*Enūma Eliš*, Tablet I, lines 1–5), Mesopotamian cosmology divided the waters into **Apsû** (sweet freshwater) and **Tiāmat** (bitter ocean brine). At **Bahrain** (`al-Baḥrayn`, *"The Two Seas"*), mariners and pearl divers routinely collected drinking water from submarine artesian freshwater springs bubbling up through the salty seabed (cf. [Quran 35:12](https://quran.com/35/12), [Quran 55:22](https://quran.com/55/22)).
- **Greco-Roman Natural History (Aristotle, Pliny, & Strabo):** **Aristotle** (*Meteorologica* II.2, 355b–356a) and **Pliny the Elder** (*Naturalis Historia* II.106.224–227, AD 77) documented that lighter sweet water floats atop heavier seawater, noting that *"fresh water wells up even in the sea itself, as at the island of Aradus [recorded also by **Strabo**, *Geographica* XVI.2.13] and in the Persian Gulf... Moreover, many rivers flow through the sea without mingling."*
- **Sasanian Persian Cosmology (*Bundahishn*) & Talmudic Hydrology ([*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b) & [*Bava Batra* 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.74b)):** The Quranic noun *barzakh* (`بَرْزَخ`, "barrier") is a Middle Persian loanword (*barsakh* / *pardak*), and Zoroastrian hydrography (*Greater Bundahishn* 10–11) describes cosmic partitions separating the salty sea (*Frāxkard*) from pure freshwater sources (*Ardwīsūr*). Similarly, in the Babylonian Talmud ([*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b); [*Bava Batra* 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.74b)), rabbinic sages discuss sweet river waters—specifically the Euphrates (*Perat*, cognate with *furāt*) and Tigris—flowing into the salty ocean while remaining distinct.

16:15.title: Casting Down Mountains as Anchors (Alqā Rawāsiya) to Prevent the Earth from Pitching
16:15.summary: [Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16/15) declares that God cast firm mountains (*alqā rawāsiya*) onto the Earth so that it would not pitch or sway beneath human beings (*an tamīda bikum*). Classical commentators ([al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/16:15/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/16:15/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and prophetic *ḥadīth* ([Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)) explain that the newly created Earth rocked like a vessel on water until God dropped mountains onto its surface overnight as stabilizing ballast weights. In modern plate tectonics and seismology, mountains are never cast down from above onto a pre-existing surface, nor do they suppress shaking; rather, mountain belts form endogenously where colliding tectonic plates buckle and fault, generating over 95% of continental earthquakes. This motif echoes pre-Islamic Arabian poetry by Zayd ibn ʿAmr and Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt, Zoroastrian mountain-ballast cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn*), and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
16:15.explanation:
Geology. In [Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16/15), mountains are depicted as heavy anchors cast down onto the Earth from above to prevent it from pitching and swaying beneath its inhabitants, inverting the geological reality of tectonic mountain building and seismicity.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16/15) declares: *"And He cast on the earth firm mountains, so that it does not sway with you (on it), and rivers and (path)ways, that you may guide yourselves"* (`وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ وَأَنْهَارًا وَسُبُلًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ`). Each lexical component of `wa-alqā fī al-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bikum` carries a specific physical meaning in classical Arabic (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*):
- ***Alqā* (`أَلْقَىٰ`):** Form IV transitive verb from *l-q-y*, meaning to throw, cast, or drop an object downward from above onto a surface—explicitly confirmed by the parallel verse [Quran 41:10](https://quran.com/41/10) (*"And He placed therein firm mountains from above it,"* `wa-jaʿala fīhā rawāsiya min fawqihā`).
- ***Rawāsiya* (`رَوَاسِيَ`):** Broken plural of *rāsiyah* (from *r-s-w*, "to anchor a vessel in water," whence *mirsāh*, a ship's stone anchor; cf. [Quran 11:41](https://quran.com/11/41)), denoting heavy stationary anchors or ballast weights.
- ***An Tamīda Bikum* (`أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ`):** Negative purpose clause (*karāhiyata an tamīda* / *li-allā tamīda*, "lest it sway with you") governed by the verb *māda / yamīdu* (`مَادَ / يَمِيدُ`), which denotes the mechanical listing, pitching, and rolling of a ship on water (*mādat al-safīnah*) that causes sea-vertigo (*al-mayd*).

Modern structural geology, plate tectonics, and observational seismology refute both the mechanism and the function described in the verse:
- **Causal Inversion of Earthquakes:** Mountains do not prevent the ground from shaking beneath human inhabitants. Rather, continental mountain belts (orogens) are created by tectonic plate collisions, crustal shortening, and thrust faulting. Consequently, mountain ranges—such as the Alpine-Himalayan belt (Zagros, Himalayas) and the Circum-Pacific belt (Andes, Japan)—are the most seismically volatile zones on Earth, generating over 95% of catastrophic continental earthquakes, whereas flat, mountainless continental cratons (such as the Canadian and Baltic Shields) are the most seismically stable regions on the planet.
- **Endogenous Uplift vs. Top-Down Casting (*Alqā*):** Mountains were never dropped onto a pre-existing surface from above.
