Orogeny is an endogenous, bottom-up process unfolding over millions of years as converging plates fold and uplift former seafloors (evidenced by marine fossils atop Mount Everest).

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Early Islamic commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* collections unanimously confirm that [Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16/15) describes God dropping physical mountains onto a newly created, swaying Earth to weigh it down:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16:15/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains: *"He, Exalted is His praise, anchored the earth with mountains lest His creation upon its back should sway, for it was indeed swaying before it was anchored by them (`bal wa-qad kānat māʾidatan qabla an tursā bihā`)."* Defining *al-mayd* as *"shaking and listing (`al-iḍṭirābu wa-l-takaffuʾ`); it is said: 'mādat al-safīnatu tamīdu maydan' when a ship lists with its passengers and tilts, and from this comes al-mayd (seasickness) which afflicts the rider of the sea,"* al-Ṭabarī cites **Mujāhid** (*"Lest it tilt with you,"* `an takfaʾa bikum`), **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī**, and **Qays ibn ʿAbbād**: *"When Allah, Blessed and Exalted, created the earth, it began to pitch (`jaʿalat tamūru`), so the angels said: 'This will not let anyone settle upon its back.' But when morning came, it contained its firm mountains (`fa-aṣbaḥat ṣubḥan wa-fīhā rawāsīhā`)."* Al-Ṭabarī also records from **ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib** that when God created the Earth, *"it bucked (`qamaṣat`)... So Allah anchored upon it the mountains which you see and which you do not see, and its settling was like meat quivering (`ka-l-laḥmi yatarajraju`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16:15/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr cites the same reports from Qatādah, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Qays ibn ʿAbbād, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, noting that by morning the mountains were created on the swaying Earth.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)):** Narrated by Anas ibn Mālik, Muhammad stated: *"When Allah created the earth, it began to sway (`lammā khalaqa Allāhu al-arḍa jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it, and it stabilized (`fa-alqāhā ʿalayhā fa-staqarrat`)."*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that the Earth originally pitched upon primordial waters until God weighted it down with mountains was a widespread motif in pre-Islamic Arabia and the ancient Near East:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Poetry:** The Meccan monotheist **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** (d. c. AD 605, preserved in Ibn Isḥāq's *Sīrah* and Ibn Kathīr's *al-Bidāyah wa-l-Nihāyah* 2:223) composed the verse: *"He spread it [the earth] out, and when He saw it resting upon the water, He anchored the mountains upon it"* (`daḥāhā fa-lammā raʾāhā istawat ʿalā al-māʾi arsā ʿalayhā al-jibālā`). Likewise, **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** (*Dīwān*, ed. Schulthess) wrote using the exact vocabulary of [Quran 16:15](https://quran.com/16/15): *"And He scattered upon it the firm mountains (`rawāsiya al-jibāl`), so it settled, whereas it had been swaying and rocking (`wa-kānat māʾidatan tamīdu`)."*
- **Zoroastrian, Mesopotamian, and Talmudic Mountain-Anchor Cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 6B.1–5, 8.1–2; *Zādspram* 3.26–30), when the Evil Spirit (*Ahriman*) assaulted the newly created Earth, the terrestrial disc violently shook and pitched until the creator fastened mountains (beginning with Mount Hara Berezaiti / Alborz) into the ground as stabilizing weights and pegs to hold the Earth steady. Similarly, in the *Epic of Gilgamesh* (Tablet IX) the twin peaks of Mount Mashu anchor the cosmos at the sun's rising and setting, while the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) depicts the terrestrial platform supported upon pillars, cosmic waters, and mountains.

43:11.title: Rain Sent Down in Measure from Heavenly Storehouses Without Evaporation & Bodily Sprouting
43:11.summary: [Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43/11) declares that God sends down water from the sky in a fixed measure (*nazzala mina al-samāʾi māʾan bi-qadarin*) to revive dead land, adding that human corpses will be resurrected in the exact same way. Across the Quran, classical exegesis ([al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/43:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/43:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)), and prophetic *ḥadīth* ([Muslim 2955a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2955a)), rain is portrayed not as evaporated surface water, but as pre-existing water metered down from heavenly storehouses, which will also cause decayed corpses to sprout like herbs from an indestructible tailbone. In modern hydrology and biology, rain is driven by solar evaporation (~505,000 km³/year), dormant seeds rather than dead dirt germinate when watered, and the human coccyx is not indestructible. This account mirrors Mesopotamian, Persian, and Talmudic ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) doctrines on heavenly rain storehouses and resurrection dew.
43:11.explanation:
No Evaporation in Water Cycle. In [Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43/11), precipitation is depicted as water rationed and sent down directly from heavenly reservoirs (`mina al-samāʾi māʾan bi-qadarin`) without any mention of solar evaporation, and this same celestial water is said to resurrect decayed human bodies just as rain revives barren soil.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43/11) declares: *"and (it is He) who sends down water from the sky in measure – and by means of it We give some barren land life, and in this way you (too) will be brought forth"* (`وَالَّذِي نَزَّلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً بِقَدَرٍ فَأَنشَرْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ`). Read alongside [Quran 23:18](https://quran.com/23/18) and [Quran 15:21–22](https://quran.com/15/21-22), this passage exhibits two scientific misconceptions:
- **Omission of Evaporation & the Heavenly Storehouse Model:** Throughout the Quran, the hydrological cycle lacks its primary thermodynamic driver: the **evaporation** of liquid water from Earth's oceans and rivers into atmospheric water vapor (`H₂O(g)`). Instead, water is portrayed as descending one-way *from the sky* (`mina al-samāʾ`), where it is kept in celestial storehouses (`khazāʾin`, [Quran 15:21](https://quran.com/15/21)) or an upper cosmic sea and metered out in fixed quotas (`bi-qadarin`), even claiming in [Quran 23:18](https://quran.com/23/18) that terrestrial groundwater originated from the sky. In atmospheric physics, the sky does not house permanent storehouses of liquid water; solar radiation evaporates `~505,000 km³` of water annually from Earth's surface (`~86%` from oceans), which ascends as vapor, cools adiabatically, condenses into clouds, and precipitates back down in a closed cycle.
- **Dead Soil Analogy & Indestructible Tailbone Sprouting (*Kadhālika Tukhrajūn*):** The verse equates plant germination after rainfall with the resurrection of decomposed corpses. Biologically, barren soil (*baldatan maytan*) does not generate life from dead matter when wetted; rather, living, dormant plant embryos inside seeds hydrate and resume mitosis. Moreover, the prophetic doctrine ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2955a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2955a)) that heavenly rain causes human bodies to sprout like vegetables from an indestructible tailbone (*ʿajb al-dhanab*) contradicts osteology: the human coccyx is composed of ordinary hydroxyapatite and collagen that decomposes, burns in cremation, and dissolves in acidic soil like any other bone.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* collections confirm both the top-down heavenly rationing of water and the literal sprouting of decomposed human bodies from celestial rain:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) & [23:18](https://quran.com/23:18/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** On [Quran 23:18](https://quran.com/23/18), al-Ṭabarī quotes **Ibn Jurayj**: *"Water, it is from the sky (`al-māʾu huwa mina al-samāʾi`)."* On [Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43/11), al-Ṭabarī explains `māʾan bi-qadarin` as rain sent down in a measured allotment (*"not like the Flood... nor so scarce that crops would not grow"*), and explains `kadhālika tukhrajūn`: *"Just as We brought forth by this water which We sent down from the sky, from this dead land after its drought and aridity, vegetation and crops, likewise, O mankind, you will be brought forth, after your annihilation and your becoming crumbled remains (`rufātan`) in the earth, by means of the water which He sends down into it to give you life after your death,"* citing **Qatādah**.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains that God sends down water from the sky according to the measure needed for crops and livestock, adding: *"By referring to the revival of the earth, Allah draws attention to how He will bring bodies back to life on the Day of Resurrection, after they have been dead, saying: {and in this way you (too) will be brought forth}."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2955a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2955a) & [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4935](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4935)):** Abū Hurayrah reports that Muhammad said: *"Then Allah will send down water from the sky, and they [the dead] will sprout forth just as herbs/vegetables sprout (`fa-yanbutūna kamā yanbutu al-baqlu`). There is nothing of a human being that does not decay except a single bone, and it is the tailbone (`ʿajb al-dhanab`), and from it creation will be reconstructed on the Day of Resurrection."* In [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 39:68](https://quran.com/39:68/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), this water descends from a sea beneath God's Throne and resembles thick male semen (*ka-maniyyi al-rijāl*).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Every element of [Quran 43:11](https://quran.com/43/11) was rooted in pre-Islamic Near Eastern and Rabbinic tradition:

- **Mesopotamian, Persian, and Pre-Islamic Arabian Sky-Reservoir Cosmology (*Enūma Eliš* & *Anwāʾ* Lore):** Across ancient Mesopotamian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV.137–140, where Marduk stations guards over the upper waters of Tiamat to release rain only by command) and Zoroastrian (*Greater Bundahishn* 21, where Tishtrya distributes measured portions of celestial water from cosmic reservoirs) cosmologies, as well as pre-Islamic Arabian *anwāʾ* meteorology, rain was conceived not as a closed evaporative cycle driven by solar heat, but as liquid water stored in upper heavenly treasuries (*khazāʾin*) and rationed downward by decree.
- **Talmudic Heavenly Rain Storehouses, Resurrection Dew, and the Indestructible *Luz* Bone ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), c. AD 500; cf. Rabbi Eliezer in [*Ta'anit* 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.9b)), the upper heavens house physical storehouses of rain and snow alongside *"the dew that the Holy One, Blessed be He, will use to revive the dead"* (`וְטַל שֶׁעָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחֲיוֹת בּוֹ מֵתִים`). In late antique rabbinic aggadah (recorded in the dialogue between Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananiah and Emperor Hadrian), when this heavenly rain or dew descends upon graves, human bodies sprout anew like herbs from a single indestructible nut-shaped bone at the base of the spine called the *luz* bone—which neither decays, dissolves, nor burns, matching the *ʿajb al-dhanab* tradition in [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2955a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2955a).

4:11.title: Over-Allocated Inheritance Fractions for Daughters and Parents (Fawqa Ithnatayni wa-li-Abawayhi)
4:11.summary: [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) mandates fixed fractional shares of an estate (*farāʾiḍ*) for children and parents: two-thirds (`2/3`) for multiple daughters, one-half (`1/2`) for one daughter, and one-sixth (`1/6`) for each surviving parent when the deceased leaves children. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/4:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/4:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6732](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6732), [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1615a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1615a)) confirm these fractions are literal obligations assumed to leave a remainder for male agnates. Mathematically, however, two or more daughters (`2/3`) and two parents (`1/6 + 1/6 = 1/3`) already consume 100% (`6/6`) of the estate, so adding a surviving wife (`1/8`) or husband (`1/4`) pushes the total to `27/24` (112.5%) or `15/12` (125%), an overflow absent from the hierarchical succession of Roman and Talmudic ([*Bava Batra* 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.108a)) law.
4:11.explanation:
Mathematical Error in Hereditary Laws. In [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11), the fixed fractional shares (*farāʾiḍ*) mandated simultaneously for daughters and parents exhaust 100% of an estate on their own, causing any estate that also includes a surviving spouse to exceed 100% (`27/24` or `15/12`) and producing an arithmetic impossibility.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) legislates the foundational descendant and ascendant shares of Islamic inheritance law: *"God charges you concerning your children: to the male, a share equal to two females (`li-l-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi al-unthayayni`). But if they be (only) women, more than two, then to them two-thirds of what he leaves (`fa-in kunna nisāʾan fawqa ithnatayni fa-lahunna thuluthā mā taraka`). But if there be (only) one, then to her a half (`fa-lahā al-niṣfu`). And to his parents, to each of them, a sixth of what he leaves, if he has children (`wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā al-sudusu mimmā taraka in kāna lahu waladun`)... (This is) an obligation from God (`farīḍatan min Allāhi`)."*

When evaluated as a system of simultaneous linear fractions of the net estate (*mā taraka*), [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) contains two structural defects—one arithmetic and one logical:
- **Fractional Sum Exceeding 100% (`> 1`):** Within [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) alone, if a deceased person leaves two or more daughters (`2/3`) and both parents (`1/6` + `1/6`, since the deceased has children), their shares consume the entire estate (`2/3 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 6/6 = 100%`). Because `100%` of the estate is exhausted by the daughters and parents under [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11), **zero estate remains** for a surviving spouse whose share (`1/8` for a wife or `1/4` for a husband when the deceased has children) is simultaneously mandated in [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12):
  1. **Man Leaving 2+ Daughters, Both Parents, and a Wife (*al-Minbariyyah*):** `2/3 + 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/8 = 16/24 + 4/24 + 4/24 + 3/24 = 27/24 = 112.5%`.
  2. **Woman Leaving 2+ Daughters, Both Parents, and a Husband:** `2/3 + 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/4 = 8/12 + 2/12 + 2/12 + 3/12 = 15/12 = 125.0%`.
  3. **Woman Leaving 1 Daughter, Both Parents, and a Husband:** `1/2 + 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/4 = 6/12 + 2/12 + 2/12 + 3/12 = 13/12 = 108.33%`.
  In each of these common family structures, the Quranic shares cannot be paid as written because the numerator exceeds the denominator.
- **The Two-Daughters Textual Lacuna (`Fawqa Ithnatayni`):** Literally, [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) specifies a share for *"more than two"* daughters (`fawqa ithnatayni`, ≥ 3 → `2/3`) and for *"one"* daughter (`wāḥidah` → `1/2`), omitting the share for **two daughters** (`ithnatayni`). Sunni jurists bridged this gap via *ḥadīth* or analogy with [Quran 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176), whereas **Ibn ʿAbbās** held that two daughters receive `1/2` based on the wording *fawqa ithnatayni*.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical *tafsīr* and canonical *ḥadīth* show that Muhammad and the early community understood the fractions in [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) as literal proportions of the estate and assumed they would leave a remainder (`mā baqiya`) rather than overflowing past `100%`:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4:11/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī cites **al-Suddī** (#8725) and **Ibn ʿAbbās** (#8726) explaining that in the *Jāhiliyyah* only adult males who fought in battle inherited, so [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) was revealed after the widow Umm Kujjah and five female relatives complained that male agnates had seized the estate. Al-Ṭabarī confirms the literal enforcement of each fraction (`2/3`, `1/2`, `1/6`).
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4:11/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr cites **Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh** ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 4577](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:4577), [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1616c](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1616c)) and the report of the widow of **Saʿd ibn al-Rabīʿ** ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 2092](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:2092)), who brought her two daughters to Muhammad after Saʿd fell at Uḥud. Muhammad ruled: *"Give two-thirds of Saʿd's wealth to Saʿd's two daughters (`2/3`), and one-eighth to their mother (`1/8`), and whatever is left is yours [the uncle's]."* Because Saʿd's parents were deceased, `2/3 + 1/8 = 19/24`, leaving `5/24`; had Saʿd's parents been alive (`1/6 + 1/6 = 8/24`), the shares would have totaled `27/24`.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Assuming a Remainder (`Mā Baqiya`):** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6732](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6732) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1615a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1615a), Muhammad stated: *"Give the Farāʾiḍ to those who are entitled to receive them, and whatever remains (`fa-mā baqiya`) goes to the nearest male relative (`li-awlā rajulin dhakarin`)."* Only after Muhammad's death did **ʿUmar** and **ʿAlī** confront estates summing to `27/24` and invent *ʿawl* (proportional reduction to `16/27`, `4/27`, and `3/27`).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The mathematical overflow in [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) stems from grafting ad-hoc unit fractions onto pre-Islamic Arabian custom without the sequential priority structure of ancient legal codes:

- **7th-Century Arabian Agnatic Custom (*ʿAṣabah*):** As documented by al-Ṭabarī (#8725–8726), pre-Islamic (*Jāhilī*) custom passed property exclusively to adult male agnates (*ʿaṣabah*) who bore arms. [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) grafted fixed unit fractions (`2/3`, `1/2`, `1/6`) onto this framework—assuming every estate would pay those fractions and leave a remainder (*mā baqiya*) for the nearest male agnate, without testing whether simultaneous claims by daughters, parents, and a spouse exceed `100%`.
- **Babylonian, Roman, and Talmudic Hierarchical Succession ([Mishnah *Bava Batra* 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bava_Batra.8) & [*Bava Batra* 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.108a)):** In Babylonian law (*Code of Hammurabi* §§165–184), Roman succession (*Novellae* 118), and Talmudic law ([*Bava Batra* 8:1–2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bava_Batra.8); [*Bava Batra* 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.108a)), lineal descendants formed the first priority class and inherited `100%` of the estate before ascendants or collaterals took a share. Merging fixed fractions for daughters (`2/3`), parents (`1/6` each), and spouses (`1/4` or `1/8`) into a simultaneous draw created an over-allocated system (`27/24` and `15/12`).

4:12.title: Spousal and Kalālah Fractional Overflows in Quranic Inheritance Law (al-ʿAwl wa-l-Kalālah)
4:12.summary: [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) assigns fixed fractional shares of an estate to surviving spouses (`1/2` or `1/4` to a husband; `1/4` or `1/8` to wives) and to collateral siblings in childless (*kalālah*) estates (`1/6` for one sibling; `1/3` shared for two or more). Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/4:12/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/4:12/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) document that early caliphs struggled to define *kalālah* and encountered severe mathematical crises when combining [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12)'s spousal and maternal-sibling shares with sister and parent shares. In a childless woman's estate, a husband (`1/2`), mother (`1/6`), two maternal siblings (`1/3`), and two full sisters (`2/3`) sum to `10/6` (166.7% of the estate), while in *al-Masʾalah al-Mushtarakah* (`1/2 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 6/6`), full brothers receive 0%, an arithmetic breakdown unseen in the sequential tier hierarchy of Roman and Talmudic ([*Bava Batra* 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.108a)) succession law.
4:12.explanation:
Mathematical Error in Hereditary Laws. In [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12), the fixed fractional shares prescribed for surviving spouses (`1/2`, `1/4`, `1/8`) and childless (*kalālah*) collateral siblings (`1/6`, `1/3`) produce severe arithmetic overflows—reaching up to `10/6` (166.7% of the total estate)—when combined with the Quran's other mandatory inheritance rules.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) legislates the inheritance fractions for husbands, wives, and collateral relatives in childless (*kalālah*) estates: *"And to you a half of what your wives leave, if they have no children (`wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum in lam yakun lahunna waladun`). But if they have children, then to you the fourth (`fa-lakumu al-rubuʿu`)... And to them the fourth of what you leave, if you have no children. But if you have children, then to them the eighth (`fa-lahunna al-thumunu`)... If a man or a woman has no direct heir (`yūrathu kalālatan`), but has a brother or a sister, then to each of them the sixth (`fa-li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā al-sudusu`). But if they are more than that, then they share in the third (`fa-hum shurakāʾu fī al-thuluthi`)."*

Because [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) defines every spousal and sibling share as a fixed unit fraction of the net estate (*mā taraka*) without a normalization denominator or priority cascade, combining [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) with the sibling and parent rules in [Quran 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176) and [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11) generates mathematical anomalies in childless (*kalālah*) estates:
- **The First *ʿAwl* Overflow (`7/6 = 116.7%`):** When a childless woman dies leaving a **husband** (`1/2` per [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12)) and **two full sisters** (`2/3` per [Quran 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)), the shares sum to `1/2 + 2/3 = 3/6 + 4/6 = 7/6 = 116.67%`.
- **Spouse + Mother + Siblings Overflows (`8/6 = 133.3%` and `9/6 = 150%`):** If she leaves a **husband** (`1/2`), a **mother** (`1/6` per [Quran 4:11](https://quran.com/4/11)), and **two full sisters** (`2/3`), the estate sums to `3/6 + 1/6 + 4/6 = 8/6` (`133.3%`). Adding one maternal sibling (`1/6` per [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12)) raises the sum to `9/6` (`150%`).
- **Maximum *Kalālah* Overflow (*Umm al-Furūkh* — `10/6 = 166.7%`):** If a childless woman leaves a **husband** (`1/2`), a **mother** (`1/6`), **two maternal siblings** (`1/3` per [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12)), and **two full sisters** (`2/3` per [Quran 4:176](https://quran.com/4/176)), the fractions sum to `1/2 + 1/6 + 1/3 + 2/3 = 10/6 = 166.67%` (**10 sixths** out of **6 sixths**).
- **Zero Remainder for Full Brothers (*al-Masʾalah al-Mushtarakah*):** Conversely, if a childless woman leaves a **husband** (`1/2`), a **mother** (`1/6`), **two maternal siblings** (`1/3` per [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12)), and **full brothers** (who inherit only the remainder under [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1615a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1615a)), the shares sum to `1/2 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 6/6 = 100%`, leaving **0%** for full brothers while maternal half-brothers take `1/3`.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators on [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) document the exegetical and mathematical crises caused by the *kalālah* and spousal fractions after Muhammad's death:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4:12/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī confirms that a husband receives `1/2` when his wife dies childless and `1/4` if she has a child, while wives share `1/4` or `1/8`. On `{inherited as Kalālah}`, al-Ṭabarī records (#8745–8769) that the Companions had no prophetic definition of *kalālah*, quoting **Abū Bakr** (#8745): *"I have formed an opinion regarding al-Kalālah; if it is correct, it is from Allah alone, and if it is an error (`khaṭaʾ`), it is from me and from Shayṭān: that al-Kalālah is whatever is other than the child and the parent (`mā khalā al-walada wa-l-wālida`)."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4:12/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Under **`### The Shared Issue (Al-Mas'alah Al-Mushtarakah)`**, Ibn Kathīr discusses the `6/6` exhaustion anomaly: *"The scholars differed regarding the Shared Issue (`al-Masʾalah al-Mushtarakah`), which is: a husband (`1/2`), a mother or grandmother (`1/6`), two maternal siblings (`1/3`), and one or more full siblings."* Applying [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6732](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6732) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1615a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1615a), **ʿUmar** initially awarded full brothers nothing (`0%`) because `1/2 + 1/6 + 1/3 = 6/6`, before reversing himself later and forcing maternal siblings to share their `1/3` with the full brothers.
- **Ibn ʿAbbās's Critique of *ʿAwl* on Quran 4:12 Estates:** When **ʿUmar** faced the `1/2 + 2/3 = 7/6` overflow and introduced *al-ʿawl* (reducing `1/2` to `3/7` and `2/3` to `4/7`), **Ibn ʿAbbās** (*Muṣannaf ʿAbd al-Razzāq* 19004; al-Bayhaqī 6/253) protested: *"Do you think the One who counted the sand-grains of ʿĀlij placed in a single wealth a half and a half and a third? These two halves have already taken the entire wealth, so where is the place for the third?"*

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The mathematical contradictions in [Quran 4:12](https://quran.com/4/12) stem from adapting Near Eastern collateral succession customs without preserving sequential residue calculation:

- **Greco-Roman & Talmudic Sequential Succession ([Mishnah *Bava Batra* 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bava_Batra.8)):** In Roman succession (*Novellae* 118, Chs. 2–3) and Talmudic law ([*Bava Batra* 8:1–2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Bava_Batra.8); [*Bava Batra* 108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.108a)), collateral inheritance followed strict **sequential priority and residual calculation**: any spousal provision (*quarta uxoria* or *ketubbah*) was deducted first, and surviving ascendants or siblings divided **100% of the remaining net residue**, preventing combined shares from exceeding `100%` or maternal half-siblings from crowding out full brothers.
- **7th-Century Hijazi Ad-Hoc Gross-Estate Fractions:** In pre-Islamic custom (where Akkadian *kallatu* / Aramaic *kaltā* denoted collateral kin, leaving Abū Bakr and ʿUmar uncertain of *kalālah* in al-Ṭabarī #8745–8769), estates were settled by arbitration. Stating spousal (`1/2`, `1/4`, `1/8`), maternal-sibling (`1/6`, `1/3`), parent (`1/6`), and sister (`2/3`) shares as simultaneous slices of the **gross estate (*mā taraka*)** rather than the **remaining residue** produced over-determined sums (`7/6` to `10/6`).

22:5.title: The Forty-Day Blood-Clot Stage & Formed vs. Unformed Miscarriages (Quran 22:5)
22:5.summary: [Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22/5) states that humans are created sequentially from dust (*turāb*), a drop of fluid (*nuṭfah*), a blood clot (*ʿalaqah*), and a lump of flesh, "formed and unformed" (*muḍghatin mukhallaqatin wa-ghayri mukhallaqatin*), before God establishes in the wombs what He wills for an appointed term. Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/22:5/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208)) explain that the conceptus remains a drop for 40 days and a red blood clot for 40 days before becoming a lump that is either fashioned into a child or expelled as an unformed miscarriage (*al-siqṭ*). Scientifically, human gestation has no coagulated blood-clot phase, cellular differentiation is continuous rather than divided into formed and unformed meat, and organogenesis finishes by day 56. This description mirrors Greek medicine and the Rabbinic distinction between formed and unformed miscarried tissue in *Niddah* 25a.
22:5.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22/5), human gestation is presented as a macroscopic progression from a seminal drop to a congealed blood clot and a lump of flesh that is either "formed" (retained to full term) or "unformed" (expelled as a shapeless miscarriage), reflecting Late Antique medical and Talmudic classifications of aborted tissue rather than cellular embryology.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

Addressing doubts about bodily resurrection, [Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22/5) declares: *"O people! If you are in doubt about the raising up—surely We created you from dust (turābin), then from a drop (thumma min nuṭfatin), then from a clot (thumma min ʿalaqatin), then from a lump, formed and unformed (thumma min muḍghatin mukhallaqatin wa-ghayri mukhallaqatin), so that We may make it clear to you. And We establish in the wombs what We please for an appointed time."* Each stage is linked by *thumma* (`ثُمَّ`), denoting sequential progression with an intervening interval (*al-tartīb maʿa al-tarākhī*), while *mukhallaqah* (`مُخَلَّقَة`) and *ghayr mukhallaqah* (`غَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَة`) denote a lump visibly fashioned with external bodily features versus one left unfashioned.

This description conflicts with empirical reproductive biology in three ways:
- **Absence of a Blood-Clot (*ʿAlaqah*) Phase:** Following fertilization of the oocyte by a single spermatozoon, the zygote undergoes cleavage, implants as a blastocyst (days 7–12), and forms a trilaminar embryonic disc. At no point in healthy gestation does the embryo consist of congealed blood (*dam jāmid*); intrauterine blood clots represent pathological hematomas or spontaneous abortion.
- **Continuous Cellular Differentiation vs. "Formed and Unformed" Lumps:** Modern concordist claims that *mukhallaqah wa-ghayr mukhallaqah* anticipates microscopic histology (differentiated vs. undifferentiated cells) misrepresent both Arabic philology and developmental biology. Histological differentiation is a continuous molecular process beginning at cleavage and gastrulation across the entire conceptus; an embryo is never a macroscopic piece of meat partitioned into "formed" and "unformed" halves. Rather, as the verse's appeal to naked-eye observation (*"so that We may make it clear to you"*) and the contrasting clause (*"And We establish in the wombs what We please"*) confirm, the text contrasts viable fetuses retained to term against unformed miscarried tissue expelled from the uterus.
- **Chronological Conflict with Organogenesis:** By week 8 (day 56, Carnegie Stage 23), all human organ systems, digits, and facial features are established. Yet the canonical prophetic timeline governing this verse keeps the conceptus as an unformed drop, clot, and lump across 42 to 120 days before limb fashioning.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Authoritative Islamic exegetes and canonical *ḥadīth* unanimously interpret [Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22/5) as describing macroscopic 40-day transformations and miscarried tissue (*al-siqṭ*):

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22:5/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī cites **ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd**: *"When the drop settles in the womb, Allah sends an angel and he says: 'O Lord, formed, or unformed?' If He says: 'unformed,' the wombs expel it as blood (`majjat-hu al-arḥāmu daman`)."* Citing **Mujāhid**, **Qatādah**, **Abū al-ʿĀliyah**, and **al-Shaʿbī**, al-Ṭabarī rules that the most accurate interpretation (*awlā al-aqwāl bi-l-ṣawāb*) is: *"The 'formed' (*al-mukhallaqah*) is that which is fashioned in a complete creation, and the 'unformed' (*ghayr mukhallaqah*) is the miscarried fetus (*al-siqṭ*) prior to the completion of its creation, when the mother casts it out as a lump before it is fashioned or the soul is breathed into it."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22:5/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr writes: *"If the nuṭfah establishes itself in the woman's womb, it stays like that for forty days, then more material is added to it and it changes into a red clot (`ʿalaqah ḥamrāʾ`)... for forty days. Then it changes and becomes a lump of flesh (`muḍghah`), like a piece of meat with no form or shape. Then it starts to take on a form and shape, developing a head, arms, chest, stomach, thighs, legs, feet and all its members. Sometimes a woman miscarries before the fetus is formed and sometimes she miscarries after it has formed, as Allah says: {then from a little lump of flesh—some formed and some unformed}, meaning, as you see (`kamā tushāhidūnahā`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** Both commentators anchor their exegesis in [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2643a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2643a) (40 days each as *nuṭfah*, *ʿalaqah*, and *muḍghah* totaling 120 days), [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318), and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a) (asserting an angel arrives after 42 nights to shape the *nuṭfah*'s hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Every motif in [Quran 22:5](https://quran.com/22/5)—creation from clay/dust, coagulation of seed into blood and flesh, and the binary between "formed" and "unformed" miscarriages—was well established across the ancient Near East:

- **Greco-Roman Inspection of Miscarriages (Hippocrates, Aristotle, & Galen):** Alongside Mesopotamian (*Atrahasis*) and Greek myths of humans molded from clay, Greek physicians inspected spontaneous abortions. In *On the Nature of the Child* (§13) and **Aristotle's** [*History of Animals* VII.3](http://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/history_anim.7.vii.html) (c. 350 BC), the conceptus up to day 40 is described as a blood-clot or *"fleshlike substance without distinction of parts"* before resolving into limbs. **Galen** (*De Semine* I.8–9; cf. [*On the Natural Faculties* II.3](http://classics.mit.edu/Galen/natfac.2.two.html)) categorized the fleshy conceptus (*sarx*) following the blood-coagulum stage into **unformed** (*adiaplastos*) versus **formed** (*diaplastos*)—the exact Greek antecedent to *ghayr mukhallaqah* and *mukhallaqah*.
- **Rabbinic Halakhah ([Mishnah *Niddah* 3:1–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Niddah.3) & [*Niddah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.25a)):** In [Mishnah *Niddah* 3:1–3](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Niddah.3) (c. AD 200) and [*Niddah* 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.25a) (c. AD 500), Rabbinic law evaluates a miscarried lump of flesh (*ḥatikhah*—Hebrew counterpart of *muḍghah*) or blood sac (*shafir*) as either **formed** (`מְרֻקָּם`, *meruqqam*) or **unformed** (`שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְרֻקָּם`, *she-eino meruqqam*).

75:38.title: Emitted Semen Coagulating into a Blood Clot Before Proportioning (Quran 75:38)
75:38.summary: Following [Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37) ("Was he not a drop of emitted semen?"), [Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38) states: "Then he was a clot (*ʿalaqah*), and He created and fashioned him," before [Quran 75:39](https://quran.com/75/39) adds that God then made from him the male and female sexes. Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/75:38/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318)) confirm that *ʿalaqah* denotes literal blood (*dam*) into which ejaculated semen transforms prior to limb fashioning and sex assignment. In human reproductive biology, ejaculated semen never solidifies into a blood clot in the uterus, and genetic sex (XX or XY) is determined at fertilization rather than after a blood-clot and body-fashioning stage. This sequence mirrors Greco-Roman coagulation theories (Aristotle and Galen) and Rabbinic embryology (*Pirkei Avot* 3:1 and *Niddah* 30b).
75:38.explanation:
Embryology. In [Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38)—within [Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37)–[Quran 75:39](https://quran.com/75/39)—human development is depicted as ejaculated male semen transforming into a congealed blood clot (*ʿalaqah*) before being fashioned and differentiated into male or female, reflecting pre-modern coagulation models of conception rather than cellular genetics.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37)–[Quran 75:39](https://quran.com/75/39) presents a chronological argument for resurrection: *"Was he not a drop of semen emitted (nuṭfatan min maniyyin yumnā)? Then he was a clot, and He created and fashioned him (thumma kāna ʿalaqatan fa-khalaqa fa-sawwā), and made of him the two sexes, the male and the female (fa-jaʿala minhu al-zawjayni al-dhakara wa-l-unthā)."* Grammatically, the passage chains each phase with temporal conjunctions: *thumma* (`ثُمَّ`, "then, after an interval") transitions the emitted seminal drop (*maniyyin yumnā*) into an *ʿalaqah* (`عَلَقَة`, congealed blood clot), while consecutive *fa-* (`فَـ`, "and then immediately") particles place creation (*fa-khalaqa*), anatomical proportioning (*fa-sawwā*), and sex differentiation (*fa-jaʿala minhu al-zawjayni*) *after* the blood-clot stage.

This developmental sequence conflicts with modern reproductive biology on three counts:
- **Semen Does Not Transform into a Blood Clot:** In [Quran 75:37](https://quran.com/75/37)–[Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38), the subject of *thumma kāna ʿalaqatan* is the emitted drop of semen (*nuṭfatan min maniyyin yumnā*). Biologically, bulk seminal plasma never enters the fallopian tube or congeals into blood inside the uterus; only a single microscopic spermatozoon fuses with the female oocyte (ovum)—a gamete unmentioned in the text—to form a unicellular zygote that divides mitotically into a blastocyst.
- **No Coagulated Blood Stage in Embryogenesis:** At no point between fertilization and morphological proportioning (*taswiyah*) does the human embryo exist as a clot of congealed blood (*dam jāmid*). The conceptus consists of living cellular germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm), and embryonic hematopoiesis produces circulating blood cells confined within closed endothelial vessels.
- **Chromosomal Sex Precedes All Morphological Stages:** By placing *"and made of him the two sexes, the male and the female"* ([Quran 75:39](https://quran.com/75/39)) via the sequential particle *fa-* after the *ʿalaqah* and *sawwā* stages, the passage reflects the ancient belief that an embryo remains sexually indeterminate until its body is physically fashioned. In reality, genetic sex (`46,XX` or `46,XY`) is fixed at the very moment of fertilization (Carnegie Stage 1) when an X- or Y-bearing sperm fertilizes the ovum.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegesis and canonical *ḥadīth* confirm that early Muslims understood [Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38) as describing literal blood coagulation followed by delayed anatomical shaping and angelic sex assignment:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75:38/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī defines *ʿalaqah* unambiguously as literal blood resulting from the transformation of semen: *"And His statement {Then he was a clot (thumma kāna ʿalaqatan)}: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: then he was blood after he was a drop of semen (`thumma kāna daman min baʿdi mā kāna nuṭfatan`), then a clot, then He fashioned him (`thumma sawwāhu`) into a well-proportioned human being, speaking, hearing, and seeing."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75:38/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains the sequential progression of [Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38): *"Meaning: he became a clot (`fa-ṣāra ʿalaqatan`), then a lump of flesh (`thumma muḍghatan`), then he was formed and the soul was blown into him (`thumma shukkila wa-nufikha fīhi al-rūḥ`). Then he became a perfect creation with sound limbs, as either a male or a female by the permission and decree of Allah."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on Post-Clot Sex Assignment:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 318](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:318) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3333](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3333), Anas ibn Mālik narrates from Muhammad: *"At every womb Allah appoints an angel who says: 'O Lord! A drop of semen (nuṭfah)! O Lord! A clot (ʿalaqah)! O Lord! A little lump of flesh (muḍghah)!' Then if Allah wishes to complete its creation, the angel asks: 'O Lord! Male or female? Wretched or blessed?'"* Likewise, [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 6594](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:6594) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2645a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2645a) place the angelic shaping of limbs and sex decree only after 40 to 120 days of gestation.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the rhetorical argument from a humble seminal drop and the biological belief that semen coagulates with uterine blood before being shaped into a male or female fetus were widespread across Greco-Roman medicine and Late Antique Rabbinic thought:

- **Greco-Roman Coagulation & Delayed Sex Differentiation (Aristotle, Hippocrates, & Galen):** In *Generation of Animals* (I.19–20, 727a–729a; II.4, 739b, c. 350 BC), **Aristotle** taught that emitted male semen acts like rennet curdling milk, coagulating menstrual blood inside the uterus into a blood-clot conceptus (*kyēma*) before the embryonic body is articulated (*diarthrōsis*) and differentiated into male or female according to maternal and paternal vital heat. Similarly, the Hippocratic treatise *On the Nature of the Child* (§§12–18) and **Galen** (*On Semen / De Semine* I.8–10, c. AD 170) described the emitted seminal drop transforming into a blood-filled coagulum prior to limb fashioning and sexual differentiation.
- **Rabbinic & Talmudic Parallels ([*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3), [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b), & [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a)):** In [*Pirkei Avot* 3:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.3) (c. AD 200), the Mishnah employs the exact rhetorical structure of [Quran 75:36](https://quran.com/75/36)–[Quran 75:38](https://quran.com/75/38)—reminding man of his origin from a *"putrid drop"* (`טִפָּה סְרוּחָה`, *tippah seruchah*) to prove future judgment—while the Babylonian Talmud in [*Niddah* 30b](https://www.sefaria.org/Niddah.30b) debates whether male and female embryos are fashioned at 40 or 80 days after conception, and [*Berakhot* 60a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.60a) permits praying for the fetus's sex up to the fortieth day on the assumption that sex is assigned only when the embryo is physically shaped.

21:31.title: Mountains Placed as Ballast Weights on a Water-Submerged Earth (Rawāsiya & Fijājan)
21:31.summary: [Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31) asserts that God set firm mountains (*rawāsiya*) upon the Earth lest it tilt with its inhabitants (*an tamīda bihim*) and cut mountain passes (*fijājan*) through them as roads. In classical exegesis ([Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), [al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and prophetic *ḥadīth* ([Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)), commentators explain that because the Earth sits submerged in cosmic water with only one-quarter of its surface exposed, it pitched beneath mankind until God weighted it down (*thaqqalahā*) overnight with mountains and breached them with passes. Geophysically, continental crust does not require surface ballast to keep from capsizing in water, and mountain belts are active zones of tectonic convergence and earthquakes rather than seismic stabilizers. This model reflects Greco-Roman quarter-earth geography (Crates of Mallus, Ptolemy), Zoroastrian mountain-ballast cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn*), and the Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
21:31.explanation:
Geology. Following the parting of the heavens and the earth in [Quran 21:30](https://quran.com/21/30), [Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31) asserts that God weighted down the Earth with firm mountains (*rawāsiya*) to stop it from tilting with mankind and breached them with mountain passes (*fijājan subulan*), reflecting a pre-modern hydrological-ballast cosmology rather than plate tectonics.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31) states: *"We have placed on the earth firm mountains, so that it does not sway with them (on it), and placed in it passes (to serve) as (path)ways, so that they might be guided"* (`وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا فِجَاجًا سُبُلًا لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ`). Here, *rawāsiya* (`رَوَاسِيَ`, plural of *rāsiyah*, from *r-s-w*, "to anchor or moor a floating vessel") is paired with *an tamīda bihim* (`أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِهِمْ`, "lest it tilt, list, or pitch with them") and *fijājan* (`فِجَاجًا`, plural of *fajj*, a wide cleft, breach, or defile between mountain walls).

This depiction of terrestrial geology conflicts with empirical geophysics on three distinct counts:
- **Orogenic Belts Are Seismic Epicenters, Not Stabilizers:** The verse states that mountains were placed specifically so that the Earth does not shake or tilt with people (*an tamīda bihim*). In plate tectonics, mountains are the structural result of horizontal plate convergence, folding, and thrust faulting. Because immense elastic strain accumulates along these active plate boundaries, mountain belts (such as the Zagros, Himalayas, Alps, and Andes) are the exact locations where the vast majority of destructive continental earthquakes occur.
- **Inversion of Crustal Density and Buoyancy:** Unlike heavy stone ballast placed on top of a vessel to weigh it down (*thaqqalahā*), mountain ranges are composed of low-density felsic continental crust (`~2.7 g/cm³`) that is lighter than the denser ultramafic mantle (`~3.3 g/cm³`) beneath it. High mountain chains are regions of thickened, buoyant crust that undergo gravitational spreading and normal faulting rather than pinning the lithosphere in place.
- **Geomorphology of Mountain Passes (*Fijāj*):** Mountain passes and gorges are not pre-formed gaps carved into instantaneous ballast barriers; they are carved continuously over millions of years by fluvial erosion, glacial valley incision, and differential tectonic uplift.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators on [Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21/31) explicitly connect the stabilizing role of *rawāsiya* to the belief that the terrestrial landmass floats or sits submerged in a surrounding cosmic sea:

- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr explains the physical mechanics behind `wa-jaʿalnā fī al-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bihim`: *"meaning, mountains with which He anchored the earth, settled it, and weighed it down (`arsā al-arḍa bihā wa-qarrarahā wa-thaqqalahā`), lest it sway with the people—that is, shake and move (`taḍṭariba wa-tataḥarraka`) so that they could not obtain stability upon it—because it is submerged in water except for one-quarter of its extent (`li-annahā ghāmiratun fī al-māʾi illā miqdāra al-rubʿ`), which is exposed to the air and the sun."* Regarding *wa-jaʿalnā fīhā fijājan subulan*, Ibn Kathīr adds: *"meaning, breaches (`thaghran`) in the mountains through which they travel as roads from region to region."*
- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī glosses *an tamīda bihim* as *"so that it does not tilt/capsize with them (`an lā tatakaffaʾa bihim`); so We placed in this earth these firm mountains, stabilizing it lest it tilt with the people."* Citing **Qatādah**, al-Ṭabarī records: *"They were on the earth while it pitched with them, not stabilizing (`kānū ʿalā al-arḍi tamūru bihim lā tastaqirru`). Then they awoke in the morning, and Allah had made the mountains, which are the rawāsī, as pegs for the earth."* Al-Ṭabarī also cites **Ibn ʿAbbās** (via Ibn Jurayj) explaining that *fīhā fijājan* refers to passes cut through the *rawāsī* (mountains).
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* Corroboration:** In [Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369), Anas ibn Mālik narrates from Muhammad that when God created the Earth, *"it began to sway (`jaʿalat tamīdu`), so He created the mountains and cast them upon it, and it stabilized (`fa-staqarrat`)."* Likewise, in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 68:1](https://quran.com/68:1/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr record early reports from Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid that the Earth rests upon a cosmic whale (*al-Nūn*) swimming in the primordial waters, whose motion caused the land to rock until mountains were anchored upon it.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the concept of mountains weighting down a water-submerged earth and the doctrine that only one-quarter of the terrestrial surface protrudes above the water derive from pre-Islamic Hellenistic and Near Eastern cosmology:

- **Greco-Roman "One-Quarter Exposed Earth" Geography (Crates of Mallus, Strabo, & Ptolemy):** In Hellenistic and Roman geography—formulated by **Crates of Mallus** (2nd century BC), **Strabo** (*Geographica* II.5.5–6), and **Claudius Ptolemy** (*Almagest* II.1, 2nd century AD)—the inhabited landmass (*oikoumenē*) was calculated to occupy only one-quarter (*al-rubʿ al-maʿmūr*) of the terrestrial surface, while the remaining three-quarters were covered by the surrounding ocean. Commentators such as Ibn Kathīr under [Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) combined this quarter-earth ratio with the ancient Near Eastern belief in a water-borne flat earth to explain why the landmass required heavy mountain weights (`thaqqalahā`) to prevent it from bobbing and tilting in the water.
- **Zoroastrian, Pre-Islamic Arabian, and Talmudic Water-Foundation Cosmology (*Bundahishn* & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In Babylonian (*Enūma Eliš* Tablets IV–V) and Zoroastrian (*Greater Bundahishn* 6B, 8) cosmologies, the Earth rests above cosmic waters and is pinned down by heavy mountain chains so it cannot pitch or shake. Likewise, pre-Islamic Arabian poets (**Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl** and **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt**) described God anchoring mountains (*rawāsī*) upon the water-borne Earth to halt its swaying (*tamīdu*), and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) portrays the terrestrial platform supported upon pillars, cosmic waters, and mountains.

31:10.title: A Pillarless Sky-Vault and Mountain Weights Stopping Lateral Motion on Water
31:10.summary: [Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10) pairs two ancient Near Eastern cosmological claims: that God built the heavens without visible pillars (*bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā*) and cast heavy mountains (*rawāsiya*) onto the Earth lest it pitch beneath humanity. In [al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) and [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir), early authorities debate whether the solid sky-vault rests on invisible pillars, while explaining that mountains were dropped onto the Earth to weigh it down upon the surface of the water (*ʿalā wajhi al-māʾ*) so it would not lurch left or right—corroborated by [Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369). In modern physics and geology, the sky is not a solid roof requiring pillars, nor is the Earth a floating platform stabilized against earthquakes by dropped mountains. This dual architecture reflects Mesopotamian, Egyptian, and Zoroastrian (*Bundahishn*) roof-and-ballast cosmologies, pre-Islamic Bedouin poetry, and the Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
31:10.explanation:
Geology. In [Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10), the Quran combines the architectural motif of a solid heaven suspended without visible pillars (*bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā*) with the geological claim that heavy mountains were cast onto the Earth from above (*wa-alqā fī al-arḍi rawāsiya*) to prevent it from swaying on the primordial waters.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31/10) declares: *"He created the heavens without any pillars you (can) see, and He cast on the earth firm mountains, so that it does not sway with you (on it), and He scattered on it all (kinds of) creatures"* (`خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا ۖ وَأَلْقَىٰ فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ`). Both halves of this cosmological pairing reflect pre-scientific misconceptions of the physical universe:
- **The Solid Sky-Vault Without Visible Pillars (*Bi-ghayri ʿAmadin Tarawnahā*):** Presenting the absence of visible supporting columns (*ʿamad*, plural of *ʿamūd*, a structural tent-pole or architectural pillar; cf. [Quran 13:2](https://quran.com/13/2)) as a miraculous sign presupposes that the sky (*al-samāwāt*) is a heavy, solid dome or ceiling over the flat Earth that would ordinarily require physical pillars to keep from falling ([Quran 22:65](https://quran.com/22/65)). In astrophysics and atmospheric science, the sky is neither a solid canopy nor a weight-bearing roof; it is the optical scattering of sunlight through Earth's gaseous atmosphere opening into the vacuum of space.
- **Mountains Cast Down to Prevent Terrestrial Swaying (*Wa-Alqā fī al-Arḍi Rawāsiya An Tamīda Bikum*):** The verse asserts that God cast (*alqā*) heavy mountain anchors (*rawāsiya*) onto the surface of the Earth so that it would not sway or rock (*an tamīda bikum*, analyzed by the Kufan grammarian al-Farrāʾ in *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān* as *li-allā tamīda bikum*, "lest it sway with you"). In plate tectonics and seismology, mountains were never dropped onto the Earth from above to stop it from rocking on water or to prevent earthquakes. Rather, mountain ranges are formed endogenously by the collision and crustal shortening of moving tectonic plates, making mountain belts the primary zones of active faulting and destructive continental earthquakes.
- **Failure of the Rotational-Balance Defense:** Modern attempts to reinterpret *an tamīda bikum* as mountains acting like wheel-weights to prevent planetary rotational wobble (precession or nutation) fail geophysically: Earth's highest mountains (`<8.9 km` on a `6,371 km` radius globe, `<0.14%` relief) do not stabilize planetary axial tilt (which is stabilized gravitationally by the Moon), and tectonic mass shifts in mountain belts actually perturb Earth's moment of inertia.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators on [Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari) confirm both the literal architectural reading of the sky's pillars and the floating-earth ballast function of the mountains:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** On *bi-ghayri ʿamadin tarawnahā*, al-Ṭabarī records multiple authentic chains from **Ibn ʿAbbās**, **ʿIkrimah**, and **Mujāhid** stating: *"Indeed, they [the heavens] have pillars that you do not see (`innahā bi-ʿamadin lā tarawnahā`),"* alongside the view of **al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī** and **Qatādah** that God holds the solid vault aloft without any pillars at all. On *wa-alqā fī al-arḍi rawāsiya an tamīda bikum*, al-Ṭabarī explains: *"And He placed on the surface of the earth (`ʿalā ẓahri al-arḍi`) firm foundations (`rawāsī`), which are the fixed mountains, lest it sway with you—meaning: lest it shake with you, nor move to the right or to the left (`wa-lā tataḥarraka yamnatan wa-lā yasratan`), but rather settle firmly with you."* He quotes **Qatādah**: *"He anchored it with the mountains, and were it not for that, it would not have settled any creation upon it."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** After summarizing the debate between Ibn ʿAbbās/Mujāhid (invisible pillars) and al-Ḥasan/Qatādah (no pillars), Ibn Kathīr states explicitly why God cast mountains onto the Earth: *"(`wa-alqā fī al-arḍi rawāsiya`) meaning: the mountains anchored the earth and weighed it down lest it shake with its inhabitants upon the surface of the water (`arsat al-arḍa wa-thaqqalathā li-allā taḍṭariba bi-ahlihā ʿalā wajhi al-māʾ`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)):** Narrated from Anas ibn Mālik, Muhammad taught that when God created the Earth, it pitched and swayed (*jaʿalat tamīdu*) until God created the mountains and cast them onto its surface (*fa-alqāhā ʿalayhā*), causing the Earth to come to rest (*fa-staqarrat*).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The juxtaposition of a solid heaven suspended without visible pillars and an Earth stabilized by mountains upon the waters was a classic cosmological pairing in the ancient Near East and pre-Islamic Arabia:

- **Ancient Near Eastern, Persian, and Pre-Islamic Arabian Pillarless-Dome Cosmology (*Bundahishn* & Jāhilī Poetry):** In ancient Egyptian cosmology (*Book of Nut*) and Mesopotamian myth (*Enūma Eliš* Tablet IV), the sky was conceived as a solid vault held aloft over the flat Earth. In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 1a.6; *Dādestān ī Dēnīg* 36), the sky (*asmān*) is explicitly described as a solid metallic or stone vault suspended around and above the Earth *without pillars* while Mount Hara Berezaiti and the mountain chains are staked into the Earth to stop its shaking. Pre-Islamic Arabian poets—including **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** and **Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl**—likewise marveled at the solid ceiling of the sky raised without visible tent-poles (*bi-ghayri ʿamad*) while heavy mountains (*rawāsī*) were cast onto the water-borne Earth to stop it from swaying (*tamīdu*).
- **Rabbinic Talmudic Cosmology ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b) & [*Bava Batra* 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.25b)):** In the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b), c. AD 500), rabbinic sages similarly debate whether the stacked heavens and the flat Earth stand upon a single cosmic pillar, twelve pillars, or rest upon the cosmic waters and mountains—the exact dispute over invisible pillars (*bi-ʿamadin lā tarawnahā*) versus no pillars preserved from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and Qatādah in [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 31:10](https://quran.com/31:10/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari).

78:7.title: Mountains as Tent-Pegs or Stakes (Awtādan) Pinning Down the Earth-Carpet
78:7.summary: Following [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6)'s description of the Earth as a spread-out bed or carpet (*mihādan*), [Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7) asks: *"and [have We not made] the mountains as stakes (wa-l-jibāla awtādan)?"* Classical commentators ([al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), [Ibn Kathīr](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir)) and prophetic *ḥadīth* ([Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)) explain that mountains act as literal tent-pegs driven into the Earth to pin it down so it remains still and does not shake beneath its inhabitants. Modern claims that *awtād* anticipates deep crustal roots (Airy isostasy) misrepresent geophysics: crustal roots are low-density felsic rock floating buoyantly in the denser mantle like icebergs—they do not pin tectonic plates in place or prevent earthquakes. This tent-peg imagery reflects pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin tent cosmology, Zoroastrian mountain-peg mythology (*Greater Bundahishn*), and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)).
78:7.explanation:
Geology. In [Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7), mountains are described as tent-stakes or pegs (*awtādan*) driven into the spread-out Earth (*mihādan*, [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6)) to hold it motionless and prevent it from shaking, reflecting ancient Near Eastern tent-cosmology rather than lithospheric plate tectonics or isostasy.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

In a single rhetorical couplet, [Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78/6)–[78:7](https://quran.com/78/7) asks: *"Have We not made the earth as a bed (mihādan), and the mountains as stakes (wa-l-jibāla awtādan)?"* (`أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا * وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا`). In classical Arabic lexicography (*Kitāb al-ʿAyn*; *Lisān al-ʿArab*), *awtād* (`أَوْتَاد`) is the broken plural of *watad* / *watid* (`وَتَد`), which designates a wooden or iron tent-peg driven into the ground to stretch and fasten the corners of a Bedouin tent or ground-mat (*mihād* / *firāsh*) while a roof canopy (*bināʾ*, [Quran 78:12](https://quran.com/78/12)) is raised overhead.

In the late 20th century, concordist authors (such as Maurice Bucaille and Zaghloul El-Naggar) argued that *awtād* miraculously anticipates **Airy isostasy**—the geophysical principle that mountain ranges possess deep subterranean "roots" extending into the underlying mantle. Both the literal tent-peg model and the concordist isostasy harmonization conflict with empirical geology and physics:
- **Archimedean Buoyancy vs. Mechanical Pegging:** Formulated by George Biddell Airy (AD 1855), isostasy is an application of Archimedes' principle of hydrostatic buoyancy, not mechanical pinning. Continental crust is composed of relatively light felsic rock (`~2.7 g/cm³`) floating atop denser ultramafic mantle peridotite (`~3.3 g/cm³`). Just as 90% of a floating iceberg's mass lies submerged in water to support its tip above the waterline, a tall mountain range has a thickened downward bulge of low-density crust displacing the denser mantle to maintain gravitational equilibrium. An iceberg's submerged base does not "peg" it to the ocean floor or stop it from drifting; likewise, crustal roots do not pin continental plates to the Earth's interior—the entire lithosphere slides horizontally across the ductile asthenosphere (`1–10 cm/year`).
- **Tectonic Uplift vs. Driven Stakes:** A tent-peg (*watad*) is a rigid, pre-formed stake driven downward from above into a softer substrate. Mountains, by contrast, are formed by horizontal tectonic plate convergence, folding, and thrust faulting that squeeze and thicken the crust from the sides.
- **Seismic Instability of Mountain Roots:** Rather than stabilizing the Earth so that it remains still, mountain belts and their over-thickened crustal roots are the primary zones of continental earthquakes and post-orogenic gravitational collapse.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators and canonical *ḥadīth* traditions unanimously interpret *awtādan* in [Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7) as physical pegs that immobilize the Earth and prevent it from shaking:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī states concisely: *"({and the mountains as stakes?}) He says: And the mountains as stakes for the earth, lest it sway with you (`wa-l-jibāla li-l-arḍi awtādan an tamīda bikum`)."* In [Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 21:31](https://quran.com/21:31/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari), al-Ṭabarī similarly quotes **Qatādah**: *"They were on the earth while it quaked with them, not stabilizing; then they awoke in the morning, and Allah had made the mountains, which are the rawāsī, as pegs (`awtādan`) for the earth."*
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78:7/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Following his explanation in [Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 78:6](https://quran.com/78:6/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir) (*"made stationary, still, and firm"*), Ibn Kathīr defines [Quran 78:7](https://quran.com/78/7): *"({and the mountains as stakes?}) Meaning, He made them as pegs for it (`jaʿalahā lahā awtādan`), anchoring it, stabilizing it, and fixing it so that it remains still and does not shake with those who are on it (`arsāhā bihā wa-thabbatahā wa-qarrarahā ḥattā sakanat wa-lam taḍṭarib bi-man ʿalayhā`)."*
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* ([Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī 3369](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3369)):** In the prophetic narration of Anas ibn Mālik, Muhammad explains that when God created the Earth, it swayed (*jaʿalat tamīdu*) until God created the mountains and cast them down onto it, causing it to become still (*fa-staqarrat*).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The metaphor of the cosmos as a giant pitched tent—with the sky stretched out as a canopy and the flat Earth fastened down by stakes and pegs—was commonplace across pre-Islamic Arabia and the ancient Near East:

- **Pre-Islamic Arabian Bedouin Tent-and-Peg Cosmology (Jāhilī Poetry):** In pre-Islamic pastoral Bedouin culture, the domestic hair-tent (*bayt al-shaʿr* or *bināʾ*) served as the direct architectural model for the universe: the flat desert ground was the spread sleeping-mat (*mihād* / *firāsh*), the sky was the raised tent-canopy (*bināʾ* / *saqf*), and the mountains were the heavy wooden or iron tent-pegs (*awtād*) and ballast stones (*rawāsī*) driven in to keep the ground-mat taut and stationary. Pre-Islamic poets such as **al-Afwah al-Awdī** (d. c. AD 570), **Labīd ibn Rabīʿah**, and **Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt** routinely described the mountains as the stabilizing pegs (*awtād*) of the flat Earth.
- **Zoroastrian and Rabbinic Mountain-Peg Parallels (*Greater Bundahishn* & [*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)):** In Middle Persian Zoroastrian cosmology (*Greater Bundahishn* 6B, 8; *Menog-i Khrad* 56), the roots of Mount Hara Berezaiti (Alborz) and the 2,244 mountains are explicitly described as pegs and nails driven into the Earth to hold it fast and prevent it from trembling after Ahriman's assault. Likewise, the Babylonian Talmud ([*Chagigah* 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.12b)) and rabbinic aggadah (*Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer* 5) depict the newly formed dry land threatening to shift over the abyssal waters until mountains were fastened upon it like stakes to secure its borders.

22:46.category: The Heart as the Organ of Thinking
22:46.title: Cardiocentrism: Cognitive Reasoning Localized to Hearts in the Chest (Quran 22:46)
22:46.summary: [Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46) asks whether people have "hearts to understand with" (*qulūbun yaʿqilūna bihā*) or "ears to hear with," concluding that physical sight is not what goes blind, "but the hearts inside the breasts grow blind." Classical commentators ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/22:46/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 52](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:52)) confirm that early Islam regarded the physical heart in the thorax as the literal biological seat of intellect (*ʿaql*) and moral judgment. Modern neuroscience establishes that all higher cognition, reasoning, and sensory processing occur in the cerebral cortex of the brain—an organ never mentioned in the Quran—while the thoracic heart is purely a muscular blood pump. The verse reflects the ancient Egyptian, Mesopotamian, Talmudic ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a)), and Aristotelian cardiocentric misconception.
22:46.explanation:
The Heart as the Organ of Thinking. In [Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46), the capacity for rational comprehension (*yaʿqilūna bihā*) is explicitly localized to "the hearts which are within the chests" (*al-qulūbu allatī fī al-ṣudūr*), reflecting the pre-modern cardiocentric belief that the thoracic heart—rather than the brain—is the anatomical organ of human intellect.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46) declares: *"Have they not traveled on the earth, so that they have hearts to understand with (fa-takūna lahum qulūbun yaʿqilūna bihā) or ears to hear with (aw ādhānun yasmaʿūna bihā)? Surely it is not the sight which is blind, but the hearts which are within the chests are blind (wa-lākin taʿmā al-qulūbu allatī fī al-ṣudūr)."* Two grammatical and lexical features in this verse preclude modern attempts to treat "heart" (*qalb*) as a detached metaphor for the brain:
1. **Direct Functional Pairing with Sense Organs:** The verse pairs *qulūbun yaʿqilūna bihā* (*"hearts by which they reason/understand,"* from the root `ع-ق-ل`, *ʿaql*, intellect) in strict syntactic parallel with *ādhānun yasmaʿūna bihā* (*"ears by which they hear"*). Just as the physical ear is the instrument of audition, the heart is presented as the anatomical instrument of reasoning.
2. **Explicit Anatomical Localization in the Thorax:** By appending the restrictive relative clause *allatī fī al-ṣudūr* (`الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ`, *"which are within the chests"*), the text specifies the physical organ inside the ribcage and rules out any metonymic reference to the brain (*al-dimāgh* inside the skull, *al-raʾs*)—a word entirely absent from the Quran.

Neurobiologically, this localization is erroneous:
- **Encephalic Seat of Intellect (*ʿAql*):** All human reasoning, conceptual comprehension, memory consolidation, and executive decision-making are performed by the ~86 billion neurons of the **brain**, specifically the prefrontal and association cortices inside the cranial cavity.
- **Myogenic Pump & Transplant Evidence:** The heart inside the chest (*ṣadr*) is a four-chambered striated muscular pump driven by pacemaker cells in the sinoatrial node. Its intrinsic cardiac nervous system (~40,000 neurons) is an autonomic relay that modulates only local heart rate and contractility. Patients who undergo complete orthotopic heart transplantation or live on total artificial hearts retain 100% of their intellect, memories, beliefs, and reasoning capacity.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical Islamic exegetes, lexicographers, and canonical *ḥadīth* unanimously affirm that the physical organ in the chest is the literal locus of intellect (*ʿaql*):

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22:46/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains *{hearts to understand with}* as: *"so that they might ponder over that, draw a lesson from it, and have hearts with which they comprehend (`qulūbun yaʿqilūna bihā`) the proofs of Allah."* Addressing why the verse specifies *{which are within the chests}*, al-Ṭabarī states verbatim: *"And it is said: {but the hearts which are within the chests are blind}—and hearts are only ever in the chests (`wa-l-qulūbu lā takūnu illā fī al-ṣudūr`)—as a means of emphasizing the speech, just as it was said: {They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts} ([Quran 3:167](https://quran.com/3/167))."* For al-Ṭabarī, just as speech literally occurs with the mouth in the head, understanding literally occurs with the heart in the chest.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22:46/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** Ibn Kathīr comments that traveling and pondering *"illuminates the heart with thought"* (`wa-nawwirhu bi-l-fikr`), and quotes the Andalusian poet Abū Muḥammad ibn Sārah al-Shantarīnī (d. 517 AH), who contrasts the two sensory organs located in the head—hearing and sight (*"in your head the two conscious ones: hearing and sight"*, `fī raʾsika al-wāʿiyān: al-samʿu wa-l-baṣar`)—with the understanding heart located in the chest.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Physical Heart (*Muḍghah*):** In [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 52](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:52) and [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 1599a](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1599a), al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports that Muhammad pointed to his chest and declared: *"Beware! Verily in the body there is a piece of flesh (`muḍghah`); if it is sound, the entire body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the entire body is corrupt. Behold, it is the heart (`al-qalb`)."* Classical Islamic jurists and lexicographers (*Lisān al-ʿArab*, s.v. `عقل`; al-Ghazālī) cited [Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46) and this *ḥadīth* as proof that the intellect (*al-ʿaql*) resides in the thoracic heart rather than the brain.

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

The belief that the physical heart in the chest is the biological organ of thought while the brain plays no role in cognition—**cardiocentrism**—was the dominant anatomical misconception across the ancient Near East, pre-Islamic Arabia, and Aristotelian philosophy:

- **Ancient Egyptian, Mesopotamian, Talmudic, & Pre-Islamic Arabian Cardiocentrism ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a)):** In ancient Egypt (*Ebers Papyrus*; *Memphite Theology*; *Book of the Dead* Spell 30B), the heart (*ib* / *ḥ3ty* inside the thorax) was considered the anatomical seat of intelligence, memory, and moral accountability weighed on the scales of judgment, whereas the brain was extracted through the nostrils and discarded during mummification. Ancient Mesopotamian (Akkadian *libbu*) and pre-Islamic Jāhilī Arabic poetry likewise localized rational intellect (*ʿaql* / *lubb* / *fuʾād*) inside the ribcage (*ṣadr*), and the Babylonian Talmud ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a)) explicitly cataloged the functions of internal organs by declaring: *"The heart understands (`לֵב מֵבִין`)."*
- **Aristotle & Stoic Cardiocentrism vs. Greek Encephalocentrism:** Although **Alcmaeon of Croton** (5th century BC), the Hippocratic *On the Sacred Disease* (§§17–20), **Herophilus** and **Erasistratus** (3rd century BC), and **Galen** (*On the Doctrines of Hippocrates and Plato*) proved through anatomical dissection that the brain governs thought and sensation, **Aristotle** (*Parts of Animals* II.10, 656a; III.4, 666a, c. 350 BC) and the **Stoics** (Chrysippus) rejected encephalocentrism, insisting that the heart in the chest is the central *akropolis* of intellect while the brain merely cools the blood—the exact misconception preserved in [Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46).

7:179.category: The Heart as the Organ of Thinking
7:179.title: Hearts, Eyes, and Ears Grouped as Parallel Organs of Perception (Quran 7:179)
7:179.summary: [Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7/179) states that many jinn and humans possess "hearts with which they do not understand (`lahum qulūbun lā yafqahūna bihā`), eyes with which they do not see, and ears with which they do not hear," comparing them to grazing cattle (*ka-l-anʿām*). Classical exegetes ([Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī](https://quran.com/7:179/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari)) and canonical *ḥadīth* ([Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2655](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2655)) classify the heart alongside the eye and ear as one of the physical bodily organs (*al-jawāriḥ*) created specifically for contemplation and comprehension (*fiqh*). In modern neuroscience, conceptual comprehension and sensory integration take place exclusively in the cerebral cortex of the brain, whereas the heart is a muscular circulatory pump. This tripartite formula directly reflects ancient Egyptian (*Memphite Theology*), Aristotelian, and Talmudic (*Berakhot* 61a) cardiocentric physiology.
7:179.explanation:
The Heart as the Organ of Thinking. In [Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7/179), the heart (*qalb*) is grouped in strict anatomical and instrumental parallel with the eye (*ʿayn*) and the ear (*udhun*) as the bodily organ responsible for conceptual comprehension (*yafqahūna bihā*), reflecting ancient cardiocentric anatomy rather than neurobiology.

### 1. The Scientific Error & Textual Claim

[Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7/179) declares: *"Certainly We have created for Gehenna many of the jinn and humans: they have hearts, but they do not understand with them (lahum qulūbun lā yafqahūna bihā); they have eyes, but they do not see with them (wa-lahum aʿyunun lā yubṣirūna bihā); they have ears, but they do not hear with them (wa-lahum ādhānun lā yasmaʿūna bihā). Those are like cattle—No! They are even farther astray!"* A parallel triad appears in [Quran 46:26](https://quran.com/46/26) (*"hearing, sight, and hearts [afʾidah]"*).

Grammatically, the verse employs an identical three-part instrumental construction (`لَهُمْ [عضو] لَّا [يفعلون] بِهَا`, *"they have [an organ] with which they do not [perform its function]"*), governed each time by the instrumental preposition *bi-* (`بِهَا`, *"by means of them"*). Just as the anatomical eye (`أَعْيُن`) is the biological organ whose natural function is vision (`يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا`), and the anatomical ear (`آذَان`) is the organ whose natural function is audition (`يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا`), the verse identifies the heart (`قُلُوب`) as the biological organ whose natural function is comprehension and deep understanding (`يَفْقَهُونَ بِهَا`, from *fiqh*).

Scientifically, this physiological division of labor is incorrect:
- **Cortical Localization of Comprehension (*Fiqh*) and Sensory Processing:** Neither conceptual comprehension (*fiqh*) nor conscious visual and auditory perception occurs in the heart. Photons transduced by retinal photoreceptors travel via the optic nerve (CN II) to the lateral geniculate nucleus and primary visual cortex (occipital lobe), while acoustic vibrations transduced in the inner ear travel via the vestibulocochlear nerve (CN VIII) to the primary auditory cortex (temporal lobe). Propositional understanding and semantic comprehension occur in cortical language and executive networks (Wernicke's area, angular gyrus, and prefrontal cortex) within the **brain**.
- **Zero Cognitive Function of the Myocardium:** The heart is a hollow muscular pump composed of cardiomyocytes that circulates oxygenated blood. It possesses no neural architecture capable of semantic comprehension, logical inference, or processing visual and auditory information.

### 2. Classical Tafsir & Hadith Corroboration

Classical commentators explicitly treat the heart, eye, and ear in [Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7/179) as three physical bodily organs (*jawāriḥ*) assigned distinct cognitive and sensory tasks:

- **[Tafsīr al-Ṭabarī on Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7:179/tafsirs/ar-tafsir-al-tabari):** Al-Ṭabarī explains *{they have hearts, but they do not understand with them}*: *"Its meaning is: these individuals whom Allah created for Gehenna possess hearts with which they do not ponder upon the signs of Allah (`qulūbun lā yatafakkarūna bihā fī āyāti Allāh`), nor do they contemplate with them His proofs for His Oneness."* Al-Ṭabarī explicitly classifies all three—the heart, the eye, and the ear—as bodily organs (`baʿḍa jawāriḥihi`), stating that Arabic speakers describe someone who fails to employ one of his bodily organs (`jawāriḥ`) in the function for which it was created as lacking its benefit.
- **[Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr on Quran 7:179](https://quran.com/7:179/tafsirs/en-tafisr-ibn-kathir):** After citing [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2653b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2653b) and [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 3208](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3208) on divine decree, Ibn Kathīr explains the triad of hearts, eyes, and ears: *"Meaning: they do not benefit from any of these bodily organs (`al-jawāriḥ`) which Allah made as a means of gaining guidance, just as Allah said: {And We had assigned them hearing, seeing, and hearts [afʾidah]} ([Quran 46:26](https://quran.com/46/26))... and {it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts which are in the breasts that grow blind} ([Quran 22:46](https://quran.com/22/46))."* He notes that disbelievers who do not use these faculties (*al-ḥawāss*) are compared to grazing cattle (*ka-l-anʿām al-sāriḥah*) that hear their shepherd's voice without comprehending his speech.
- **Canonical *Ḥadīth* on the Heart as the Seat of Volition:** In [Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2655](https://sunnah.com/muslim:2655), ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr reports that Muhammad said: *"Verily, the hearts of all the sons of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful, like a single heart; He turns them wherever He wills,"* and prayed: *"O Allah, Turner of the hearts (`muṣarrifa al-qulūb`), turn our hearts to Your obedience"* (cf. [Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 52](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:52)).

### 3. Ancient World Misconceptions & Historical Parallels

Both the cardiocentric triad of "understanding hearts, seeing eyes, and hearing ears" and the comparison of uncomprehending humans to senseless cattle were well-known medical and literary tropes across the ancient Near East:

- **Ancient Egyptian, Mesopotamian, & Pre-Islamic Arabian Sensory Triads:** In ancient Egyptian cardiocentric anatomy—codified in the **Memphite Theology** (Shabaka Stone, lines 53–57) and the *Instruction of Ptahhotep*—the physical **eyes** that see and **ears** that hear transmit their impressions directly to the **heart** (*ib*) in the chest, which produces all conceptual understanding (*"The sight of the eyes, the hearing of the ears, and the breathing of the nose report to the heart; it is this which causes every completed concept to come forth"*). Likewise, Mesopotamian wisdom texts (*Counsels of Wisdom*) and pre-Islamic Jāhilī poetry paired the eye, ear, and thoracic heart (*qalb* / *fuʾād*) as the triad of perception while comparing uncomprehending men to driven livestock (*al-anʿām*).
- **Aristotelian, Stoic, & Talmudic Cardiocentrism ([*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a)):** In Greek philosophy, **Aristotle** (*De Partibus Animalium* II.10, 656a; III.4, 666a) and the **Stoics** taught that the eyes and ears transmit sensory motions via blood vessels to the **heart** (*kardia*) as the central *sensorium commune* and organ of understanding, whereas the brain merely cools the blood. Similarly, Talmudic folk physiology in [*Berakhot* 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.61a) assigns understanding specifically to the physical heart (*"the heart understands,"* `לֵב מֵבִין`).
